title: fleet create asks which agent the fleet's seats run on, beside the store question, installs that agent's pack from the fleet-packs source and tag this binary pins, and writes [agent] adapter; an unset key means claude-code and claude_code is its alias
description:
SPEC (fleet-x93d.1, drafted 2026-09-25). Sites at 2a48e90. Blocked by flight 13 (the claude-code pack exists and passes `fleet agent check`), fleet-3krx.1 (the store question, `PINNED_PACKS_SOURCE`/`PINNED_PACKS` in core/src/supported.rs, `--packs-from`) and fleet-14p8.6 (the `[agent] adapter` key, resolved through packs).

**Behaviour.** Today `fleet create` asks "which agent?" out of `controller::AGENTS = ["claude_code"]` (cli/src/lifecycle.rs 124-130; controller/src/policy.rs 537-540; known_agent 322-331) and records the answer as a comment only, `# Its agent is `claude_code`.` (controller/src/lifecycle.rs:91, in embedded_text 87-121). No key is written and nothing is installed. After this row:

- **The default name and its alias (Reviewer call 2026-09-25, E12).** Two constants sit beside fleet-14p8.6's opener, the store's `None → "bd"` pattern: `DEFAULT_AGENT_ADAPTER = "claude-code"` (a missing `[agent] adapter` resolves this name through packs) and `AGENT_ADAPTER_ALIASES = [("claude_code", "claude-code")]`. The alias is read wherever a name is read (`--agent`, the key), and nothing is rewritten. These two lines are the only Claude Code literals left in core, cli and controller, and fleet-x93d.3's gate names them.
- **The prompt**, after fleet-3krx.1's store question and before the defaults are written (cli/src/lifecycle.rs:272): `which agent?` over the agent packs this binary knows at its pinned tag. That list is built from `DEFAULT_AGENT_ADAPTER` alone today, and each entry's fleet-packs path is `//adapters/agent/<name>`, derived rather than spelled. There is **no `none`** (E12). `--agent <name>` answers it, alias accepted. No TTY and no flag takes the default, as the store question does; the refusal at docs/getting-started.md:399 goes.
- **The install.** Create runs the path `fleet pack add <PINNED_PACKS_SOURCE>//adapters/agent/<name> --version <PINNED_PACKS>` runs (cli/src/main.rs pack_add 912 → core/src/add.rs add 433), pinned in packs.lock beside the store pack.
- **The key.** Create writes `[agent] adapter = "<name>"` (ruling 11) into the fleet's policy file, so the choice is on record even though unset means the same. embedded_text (controller/src/lifecycle.rs 87-121) takes the key in place of the comment at 91.
- **The example model.** The example seat row's `model` (116, `policy::DEFAULT_MODEL` today) becomes the installed adapter's `capabilities().default_model`, read after the install as create reads the store's `item_prefix` (cli/src/lifecycle.rs 179-193). An adapter that cannot be opened leaves the example out rather than guessing.
- **A failed install** refuses create with the `fleet pack add` line to run, after the files already written, as fleet-3krx.1's store install does.
- **Start.** Its binary gate (cli/src/lifecycle.rs 582-591, `ClaudeCode::resolve_effect_bin`) becomes fleet-14p8.6's opener plus `version`, unless fleet-14p8.3 already made it so. A fleet whose adapter name resolves to no installed pack (one created before this row, or a pack removed) refuses with fleet-14p8.6's text naming `fleet pack add`. That is ruling 10's no-adoption rule; nothing is migrated.
- **Standalone.** The agent is the fleet's (ruling 11), so the question is not asked. `--agent` naming a different adapter than the fleet's refuses with a usage line naming the fleet's. project_text's header (controller/src/lifecycle.rs 125-) stops recording `--agent`.
- `--packs-from <path>` (fleet-3krx.1) serves both packs from one clone. The done lines (274-317) gain an `agent:` line naming the pack and tag.

**Sites.** cli/src/lifecycle.rs CreateArgs 30-43 (`agent` 37-39), create 62-318 (94-96, 124-130, 134-147, 154, 272, 274-317), known_agent 322-331, the start gate 582-591; controller/src/lifecycle.rs written_by 62-73, embedded_text 87-121, project_text 125-, tests 758-840 (their `claude_code` literals become the constants); controller/src/policy.rs 534-540 (this row stops reading them; fleet-x93d.2 deletes them); core/src/supported.rs (fleet-3krx.1's constants; the agent pack rides the same tag). The golden files at cli/tests/lifecycle.rs 28 and 42-90 build their expected text from the constants, not a literal, and so does the call at cli/tests/seat_add.rs:62. Docs are fleet-x93d.3's.

**Interfaces produced.** `DEFAULT_AGENT_ADAPTER`, `AGENT_ADAPTER_ALIASES`; `[agent] adapter` written by create. fleet-x93d.2 deletes `AGENTS`/`AGENT_CLAUDE_CODE`, and fleet-x93d.3's gate allows exactly the two constant lines.

**Acceptance.**
- A fresh `fleet create --embedded` with defaults, on a machine with network: both packs installed and pinned at the tag; fleet.toml carries `[agent] adapter = "claude-code"`; `fleet agent check --adapter claude-code` passes offline; `fleet start` loads.
- `--agent claude_code` gives the same file and pack.
- `--agent nosuch` is a usage refusal listing the known names.
- No TTY and no flag takes the default.
- A fleet.toml with no `[agent]` table and the pack installed starts; with the pack removed, start refuses naming the pack add line.
- `--packs-from <scratch clone>` installs both packs from the clone.
- A standalone create into a fleet refuses a mismatched `--agent`.

title: The claude-code pack proves itself in CI: an offline fleet agent check and the pack's tests on every push, and a live check against the pinned Claude Code, tmux and fleet tag on demand and nightly
description:
SPEC (fleet-jymr.7, drafted 2026-09-25). In fleet-packs; sites at 2a48e90. Blocked by fleet-jymr.2, fleet-jymr.3, fleet-jymr.4 and fleet-jymr.5 (the verbs, fixtures and plugin), fleet-14p8.8 (`fleet agent check`, `--live`) and fleet-rsia.5 (the workflow and the pinned fleet tag it introduces).

**Behaviour.** Two jobs in fleet-packs' GitHub Actions, beside the bd pack's (fleet-rsia.5), sharing its one-line fleet pin (`FLEET_VERSION` or `versions.toml`; moving it is a commit).

- **Every push, offline, no claude on the runner.** Install Deno 2.9.7 (runtimes/ts's pin) and fleet at the pinned tag (built with cargo at that tag, cached). In `adapters/agent/claude-code/`: `deno fmt --check`, `deno lint`, `deno test` (the lessons and fixture tests, fleet-jymr.6), `deno task types` then `git diff --exit-code contract.d.ts`. Then `fleet agent check --adapter adapters/agent/claude-code/adapters/agent/claude-code/main.ts` must print no FAIL: capabilities valid, launch and resume usable, read and context matching every fixture, and `version` answering `null`, which fleet-14p8.8 counts as an answer offline. One end-to-end hook arm: with the pack installed in a scratch fleet, a recorded Claude Code PreToolUse payload for a command the shell-trap class refuses, piped to `fleet guard --adapter claude-code`, prints the deny document cli/src/claude.rs `refusal` prints today with the reason filled. That holds the `[hook]` table to the built-in manifest until fleet-x93d.2 deletes the built-in.
- **Live, on `workflow_dispatch` and nightly, never on push.** It costs a model turn and needs a login secret. Install Claude Code 2.1.280 with the doctor check's own fresh-install line (`curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash -s 2.1.280`, core/defaults/doctor/claude-code-version/run.sh:35), with the agent's auto-updater off (lessons A1: a spread means an unfinished move only while it is off). Install tmux 3.7b (the minimum fleet-rge6.6 declares; built from source where the image carries an older one) and fleet at the pinned tag. Then run `fleet agent check --adapter … --live`: a scratch worktree, a scratch socket (`tmux -L`), a scratch config dir, never a live fleet. It reads starting → idle, one cheap turn → busy, stop, resume, context (fleet-14p8.8's script). The model is a vendor string the workflow names (ruling 7: passed through), the cheapest the account has. The same job runs the arms owed to a live binary: D8's `an_interactive_start_under_tmux` (fleet-jymr.6), where a scoped session's transcript lands (fleet-jymr.4's first open item), a launched seat reaching idle in a fresh scratch worktree with no trust dialog, because launch seeds trust (Ruled 2026-09-25, ruling 13; fleet-jymr.2), a launched seat's `/wake` and a refused Bash command denied with the guard's reason (fleet-jymr.5), a flagged full-id resume keeping plugin, model and posture (E3), and `fleet doctor` reporting `claude-code-version` and `isolation-pair` holding from the pack (fleet-jymr.2).
- **Without the secret** (a fork, a lapsed login) the live job is skipped with a line saying why, never red. A red live run is read by a person; nothing files a bead on its own.
- Each live run's log is kept as an artifact: the recorded measurement a re-pin (fleet-031's successor) cites.

**Sites (this repository, read).** core/defaults/doctor/claude-code-version/run.sh 33-35 (the pin and both install lines); core/src/supported.rs:35; cli/src/claude.rs 47-56 (`refusal`, the deny document the hook arm expects); brain/lessons/claude-code.md A1 (the updater), D8 (tmux 3.7b).

**Interfaces consumed.** fleet-14p8.8's `--live` arms and exit; fleet-jymr.2–fleet-jymr.5's verbs, fixtures and `pluginDir()`; fleet-rsia.5's workflow file and fleet pin.

**Acceptance.** The push job is green on fleet-packs' main. A deliberate break (read mapping `waiting` to `idle`) turns the offline check red on the fixture it contradicts. A manual live run is green on 2.1.280 with tmux 3.7b and fleet at the pinned tag, its log linked on this bead. A run without the secret shows the live job skipped, not failed.

**Reviewer calls 2026-09-25.** (1) The live job runs on a macOS runner: the credential knob (A11) was measured against the macOS keychain only, and a Linux login path is its own measurement for later. (2) The nightly turn and manual runs are paid from Alberto's account, on the cheapest model the account has; the workflow names it. (3) The job sets `DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER=1` and its first run records `claude --version` before and after a sleep to show the pin held; if it did not, the setting that worked is recorded here.

title: The Claude Code lessons are split: the entries the pack rests on move beside its fixtures in fleet-packs, the daemon-era entries stay in brain/ as history marked with the row that retired them, and every lessons:: test is a pack test, a core test, or retired with its entry

The claude-code pack carries fleet's Claude Code plugin: the manifest, one hooks.json calling fleet guard --adapter claude-code and fleet prime, the shim, the skills, and the renderer of fleet's neutral permissions, and launch loads that plugin into every seat
description:
SPEC (fleet-jymr.5, drafted 2026-09-25). In fleet-packs; sites at 2a48e90. Blocked by fleet-jymr.1 (the skeleton), fleet-jymr.2 (launch, which calls this row's renderer and passes `pluginDir()`), fleet-14p8.4 and fleet-14p8.9 (`fleet guard --adapter` with no class runs the classes the layers declare), and fleet-14p8.2's launch request carrying neutral `permissions` (E8). Closes fleet-78r and fleet-bz9 (E17).

**Behaviour.** The root's plugin moves into the pack (ruling 6), and the adapter points each seat at it.

- **Where.** `adapters/agent/claude-code/adapters/agent/claude-code/plugin/`, beside `main.ts`. `pluginDir()` (fleet-jymr.2) is a path relative to the adapter's own file and is never a request field (Reviewer call 2026-09-25, E8).
- **Manifest.** `plugin/.claude-plugin/plugin.json` is the root's (.claude-plugin/plugin.json) with `version` = the pack's version. fleet-packs' root carries `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` listing the one plugin `fleet` at that path. The pack's README carries a person's own install lines (`claude plugin marketplace add <fleet-packs>`, `claude plugin install fleet@fleet`); fleet-x93d.3 points there.
- **One hooks.json.** A `PreToolUse` entry, matcher `Bash`, with a single command `"${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}"/bin/fleet guard --adapter claude-code`. With no class argument, fleet-14p8.9 runs the compiled classes the layers declare. It replaces hooks/hooks.json's four lines (1-35). `SessionStart` runs `"${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}"/bin/fleet prime`. The root prefix is lessons D5: a hook's PATH does not carry `bin/`.
- **The shim.** `plugin/bin/fleet` is bin/fleet (1-89) with its exit contract whole (fleet-78r's landed half, beb99a2): a guard with no binary exits 2 and blocks, prime exits 127, anything else exits 127.
  - The checkout search (83-87) and the `cargo build` advice (44, 50, 55) go; `FLEET_BIN` (70-81), which core sets on every seat it launches, is the only source.
- **Skills (Reviewer call 2026-09-25, E16: this row owns their new home).** `plugin/skills/version/` (skills/version/SKILL.md, a real directory) plus the twelve tiny skills the root links today (skills/adopt … skills/wake, each `-> ../packs/tiny/skills/<name>`), linked by relative links to fleet-packs' `tiny/skills/<name>`. The loader follows a link (D6); `/wake {seat}` reaches a seat this way.
- **Permissions (Reviewer call 2026-09-25, E8).** Launch's request carries fleet's neutral `permissions`: what cli/src/transient.rs settings_of (647-680) and without_the_touched_rule (682-) build today from core/defaults/overlay/per-provider/claude/permissions.json, stated provider-neutrally.
  - **Commands allowed, by prefix:** the template's `Bash(<cmd>:*)` entries, plus the builder's `touched` command when a spawn names one. Core adds it as today, so the pack needs nothing more from core.
  - **Paths writable:** the worktree (`Edit(/{worktree}/**)`).
  - **Commands refused, by prefix:** the five `git push` denials.
  - `lib/permissions.ts` renders those into Claude Code's rules. It adds the pack's own fixed tool denials (`AskUserQuestion`, `EnterPlanMode`, `ExitPlanMode`, `mcp__*__request_access`): Claude Code tool names stay the adapter's format, the E11 line.
  - Launch writes the result through `writeInside` to the worktree's `.claude/settings.local.json`, where Claude Code reads it today (local_settings, controller/src/adapter/claude_code.rs 421-423; write_settings, controller/src/transient.rs 957-, called at 703). A request with no `permissions` (a named seat) writes no file.
- **Launch loads the plugin.** Every launch passes `--plugin-dir <pluginDir()>`, so no fleet names it. `[controller] plugin_dir` (controller/src/policy.rs 126, 213-216; effect.rs 252-255; claude_code.rs 463-467) goes in fleet-x93d.2.

**Beads (E17).** fleet-78r's remaining half (an installed plugin has nothing pointing at a binary) is answered here. **Ruled 2026-09-25 (ruling 16):** fleet-bz9 folds here, with no interim fix. Both close when this row lands. The consequence until flight 13 lands: a fresh fleet's seats get the plugin only when set up by hand, with `[controller] plugin_dir` written in fleet.toml to a checkout, as policy.rs 118-126 reads it today. fleet-bz9 was P0, due 2026-10-07, and that date passes with this fold; fleet-adz.7's written clean-machine path (due 2026-10-10) must carry the manual `plugin_dir` step, or its seats run with no guards, prime or `/wake`. The reviewer notes this on fleet-adz.7 when the fold is recorded.

**Sites.** .claude-plugin/, hooks/hooks.json, bin/fleet, skills/ (13 entries), core/defaults/overlay/per-provider/claude/permissions.json; cli/src/transient.rs 614-680; controller/src/transient.rs 703, 957-; controller/src/effect.rs 245-256; cli/tests/plugin.rs 1-633, restated as deno tests (manifest 66, marketplace 89, prime hook 113, shim 126-412, version skill 413, D5 497, D6 535, skills linked 600); cli/tests/seat.rs 746-1210 (the permission file's arms, restated over the renderer).

**Interfaces produced.** `pluginDir()`; `lib/permissions.ts renderPermissions(permissions, worktree) -> string`, which fleet-jymr.2's launch calls. fleet-x93d.2 deletes the repo's copies, and fleet-x93d.3 points the docs at the pack's README.

**Acceptance.**
- deno tests:
  - the manifest names `fleet` at the pack's version, and the marketplace lists one plugin;
  - hooks.json holds exactly one PreToolUse command and the prime line, both root-prefixed;
  - the shim runs an absolute `FLEET_BIN`, refuses a relative one, and with none exits 2 on a guard and 127 otherwise;
  - every tiny skill resolves;
  - rendering today's template, stated neutrally, equals settings_of's document as JSON, with and without `touched`.
- `claude plugin validate` passes on 2.1.280.
- Under `--live` (fleet-jymr.7) a launched seat runs `/wake`, a refused Bash command is denied with the guard's reason, and an allowed one runs unprompted under `unattended`.

**Reviewer calls 2026-09-25.** (1) Whether relative skill links survive a marketplace install's copy into the plugin cache is this row's first measurement, on 2.1.280; if they do not, the skills are copied into `plugin/skills/` at build time and CI diffs the copy against fleet-packs' `tiny/skills/`. (2) A person's own marketplace-installed session has no `FLEET_BIN`, and the shim keeps blocking a guard it cannot run (fail closed, the half of fleet-78r that landed); the pack's README tells a person to set `FLEET_BIN` once in their shell profile. No PATH fallback, as fleet-78r ruled.

title: The claude-code pack's context verb reads each seat's transcript: the last main-chain window in tokens, the turns taken and the last write, ported from observe.rs's reader with recorded fixtures
description:
SPEC (fleet-jymr.4, drafted 2026-09-25). In fleet-packs; sites at 2a48e90. Blocked by fleet-jymr.1 (the skeleton and `configDirFor`).

**First step (reviewer call 2026-09-25).** Where a scoped interactive session's transcript lands is unmeasured (lessons B10's last clause: the scoped session there took no turn), and every spawned seat is scoped. On 2.1.280, under a scratch config dir and socket, take one turn and record the transcript's path before anything below is built; if it is not under `<config_dir>/projects/`, the path rule follows the measurement.

**Behaviour.** `context {seats: [{seat, session_id?, config_dir?, worktree}]}` → per seat `{tokens, window, turns, last_write}`, one process per poll, a port of the transcript reading fleet-14p8.3 moves out of observe.rs into the in-process adapter (ruling 4).

- **Where.** `<configDirFor(seat)>/projects/<encodeProjectDir(worktree)>/<session_id>.jsonl` (transcript_path, controller/src/adapter/mod.rs 353-358). The encoding replaces every non-alphanumeric character with `-` (encode_project_dir, 346-351; lessons C1, censused on 2.1.261). A path past about 200 characters (said to be truncated with a hash) and a non-ASCII character are unmeasured, and like a missing file they give no reading, never a guess.
- **`tokens`.** The last main-chain assistant entry whose `input_tokens + cache_read_input_tokens + cache_creation_input_tokens` is non-zero (context_tokens_in, controller/src/observe.rs 439-453; lessons C2). Sidechain entries are skipped (C3: a subagent's window); a zero-usage entry, written for a turn that made no model call, is skipped; a torn or malformed line is skipped, because the file is read while it is appended to.
- **`turns`.** Main-chain assistant entries carrying a usage block, the zero-usage ones counted (turns_in, observe.rs 540-548): the same filter one step shorter, as the doc comment there argues.
- **`last_write`.** The transcript's mtime as a Stamp, `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ` in UTC to the second (Reviewer call 2026-09-25, E9; core/src/store/types.rs 213-216's form, which the contract reuses), not the milliseconds ended_at answers today (controller/src/adapter/claude_code.rs 627-642). It is the value ruling 3's end-time fallback uses; the second's resolution is far inside any window set in hours (the reasoning at 620-626).
- **`window`.** `null`. The transcript states no window, and the window is the agent's and moves by model (lessons C5: auto-compaction measured near 967K on one model and near 1,000K on another), so the rest threshold stays fleet policy (controller/src/policy.rs 17-20) and this adapter reports no denominator it cannot read.
- A seat with no session id, or whose file does not resolve, answers all four `null`, never `0`: every reader renders a missing reading as blind (observe.rs 430-435), and a 0 would read as an empty session. A file that opened and holds no turn is `turns: 0`, a measured zero (controller/src/transient.rs 1702-1708 keeps the two apart today).
- The entry decoder (observe.rs 386-418: `type`, `isSidechain`, `message.usage`, `error`, `isApiErrorMessage`) and `loggedOutFirstTurn` (476-494) live in the same module, since fleet-jymr.3's logged-out arm reads the same entries.

**Fixtures.** Transcripts recorded on Claude Code 2.1.280 in a scratch config dir: a main chain with a sidechain turn after the last main one; a zero-usage entry last; a torn final line; a logged-out first turn (`authentication_failed`, zero window); a session whose worktree path carries a dot, an underscore and a space. Stored under the adapter's `fixtures/` beside fleet-jymr.3's.

**Sites (source ported).** controller/src/observe.rs 384-548; controller/src/adapter/mod.rs 328-358; controller/src/adapter/claude_code.rs 607-642. The in-process callers these readings replace, which fleet-14p8.3 already routes through the verb: controller/src/run.rs 661-690 (the loop's read of `context_tokens` and the logged-out sighting) and controller/src/transient.rs 1700-1710 (the spawn's status reading). Tests restated as deno tests: controller/tests/observe.rs `the_transcript_path_encoding` 256, `the_transcript_entry_shape` 435, `the_turn_reader_counts_the_entry_the_window_reader_skips` 464, `sidechains_carry_another_window` 510, `a_transcript_resolves_under_the_directory_it_is_read_with` 1080; the drive arm at cli/tests/drive_effects.rs 1756.

**Interfaces produced.** `lib/transcript.ts`: `encodeProjectDir(path)`, `transcriptPath(configDir, worktree, sessionId)`, `entries(body)`, `contextTokens(entries)`, `turns(entries)`, `loggedOutFirstTurn(entries)`. fleet-jymr.3 consumes the path and `loggedOutFirstTurn`; fleet-jymr.6's C1–C3 arms consume the rest.

**Acceptance.** deno tests over every fixture: `last_write` is the file's mtime to the second in the Stamp form; the sidechain's larger window is not the answer; the zero-usage entry is counted as a turn and skipped as a window; a torn line changes nothing; the encoding of `/Users/av/.claude/jobs/tmp` is `-Users-av--claude-jobs-tmp`. Offline `fleet agent check --adapter` passes context against the fixtures; under `--live` (fleet-14p8.8), after one cheap turn, `tokens > 0`, `turns >= 1`, and `last_write` parses as a Stamp inside that turn's minute.

**Reviewer calls 2026-09-25.** (1) Settled by the first step above. (2) The per-project renaming variable (C1, 2.1.234) is ignored, as observe.rs ignores it today, and the pack's lessons say a fleet that sets it reads blind. (3) `window` stays `null`: nothing measured supports deriving it from a model name.

title: The claude-code pack's read answers every seat from one claude agents listing per config dir: status and waitingFor become activity and blocked_on, the row teaches the session id, a logged-out first turn reads as blocked, and fixtures recorded from the real listing prove it
description:
SPEC (fleet-jymr.3, drafted 2026-09-25). In fleet-packs; sites at 2a48e90. Blocked by fleet-jymr.1 (the skeleton) and fleet-jymr.4 (`lib/transcript.ts`, which the logged-out arm reads; see Open).

**Behaviour.** `read {seats: [{seat, session_id?, pid?, config_dir?, worktree, screen}]}` → per seat `{activity, blocked_on?, evidence, session_id?, cause?}`, one process per poll (fleet-14p8.2).

- **First step (Reviewer call 2026-09-25, E14).** B10, the interactive row this verb reads, was measured on 2.1.282 (brain/lessons/claude-code.md:610): re-measure it on 2.1.280 (fields, `status`, `waitingFor`) as the fixtures are recorded, and note the version in the pack's lessons (fleet-jymr.6).
- **One listing per distinct config dir.** Seats are grouped by `configDirFor(seat)`; each group gets one `claude agents --json --all` under `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` = that dir and `CLAUDE_SECURESTORAGE_CONFIG_DIR` = `credentialDir()` (status, claude_code.rs 584-605). A config dir scopes the listing (lessons A11, interactive rows too per B10), so a spawned seat is only visible through its own dir. The listings run concurrently inside the per-call bound.
- **Unreadable is per dir, never empty.** Exit non-zero, zero bytes with exit 0 (lessons B4; parse_roster 802-815), or rows that do not parse: every seat under that dir answers `activity: unknown` with the listing's failure as `cause`; seats under other dirs are read as usual (the rule controller/tests/observe.rs:1044 pins today). An empty array is a listing that answered.
- **Matching** (lessons B5, B10). The listing is parsed into the adapter's own private row type (Reviewer call 2026-09-25, E6: short ids never leave the adapter). An interactive row carries `cwd`, `kind`, `name`, `pid`, `sessionId`, `startedAt`, `status`, never `id` or `state`; unknown fields are tolerated (B1); a background row is never matched to a seat. A seat with a `session_id` matches the row with that `sessionId`. A seat without one matches the `kind: interactive` row whose `pid` equals the request's `pid` (the pane's, fleet-14p8.2), the one attribution fleet-rge6.3 kept, and that row's `sessionId` is answered as `session_id`; there is no cwd match (fleet-rge6.3 removed it): the learning core records, since there is no short address any more (B10).
- **Activity, typed.** `status` idle → `idle`, busy → `busy`, waiting → `blocked`; `evidence: typed`. `waitingFor` is keyed on presence (B8): `permission prompt` → `blocked_on: permission`; any other present value → `blocked` with no `blocked_on`, the value kept in the fixture.
- **No row.** Launch seeds trust (Ruled 2026-09-25, ruling 13; fleet-jymr.2), so the dialog should not appear; if it does (the seed failed, or fleet-rge6.2 fell back to answering it), a screen showing the workspace-trust question (lessons A15; B10: the row is absent while it is up) → `blocked`, `blocked_on: question`, `evidence: screen`; otherwise `starting`, typed. Whether a start that never arrives has failed is core's (presence from tmux, the `until` window; ruling 3), never this answer's.
- **Logged out** (lessons A11). For a matched idle row with a session id, the transcript's first main-chain assistant entry read by the three-term rule (logged_out_first_turn, controller/src/observe.rs 476-494; `AUTHENTICATION_FAILED`, 457) → `blocked`, `blocked_on: logged_out`, typed. The adapter answers the state every poll; the once-per-row dedupe and the transient-only rule (logged_out_dispatch, 512-520) stay core's, as fleet-14p8.3 leaves them.
- **`usage_limit` is never answered** until its shape is measured (fleet-tnkuq.54).

**Fixtures.** Recorded from Claude Code 2.1.280 under a scratch config dir and scratch tmux socket, never the live fleet: listings idle, busy, waiting at a Bash approval, two rows in one worktree, an unknown field, `[]`, zero bytes; the trust-question screen; a logged-out transcript. Under the adapter's `fixtures/` in fleet-14p8.8's layout, each with its expected answer. The background-era rows of controller/tests/observe.rs 65-100 are not ported.

**Sites (source ported).** controller/src/adapter/claude_code.rs 584-605, 802-815; controller/src/adapter/mod.rs 170-279 (AgentRow, dir_key); controller/src/observe.rs 220-382 (observe_seat's matching, `newest`), 457-520; controller/tests/observe.rs lessons arms `the_roster_is_one_command` 141, `the_roster_read_can_go_silently_dead` 186, `cwd_names_a_seat_and_proves_nothing` 207, `waiting_for_names_the_block` 281, and the logged-out arms 1163-1250, restated as deno tests over the fixtures.

**Interfaces produced.** `lib/listing.ts` (`listingsFor(seats) -> Map<configDir, Row[] | Unreadable>`, `match(seat, rows)`); `verbs/read.ts`. fleet-jymr.7's `--live` job and fleet-jymr.6's lessons arms consume them.

**Acceptance.** Offline `fleet agent check --adapter` passes read on every fixture; a recording fake `claude` shows seats across three config dirs cost exactly three listings in one process; one dir's failing listing leaves the others read; a seat with no session id is answered the row's `sessionId`; `--live` (fleet-14p8.8) reads starting → idle → busy, typed, on the pinned binary.

**Reviewer calls 2026-09-25.** (1) Only `permission prompt` maps to `blocked_on: permission` until the recording shows other `waitingFor` strings; each new one recorded gets its fixture and its mapping in the same landing. (2) The trust question's text is re-recorded on 2.1.280 in the first step. (3) The row stays blocked by fleet-jymr.4 as well: the logged-out arm reads through its transcript reader, and one reader is better than two.

title: The claude-code pack answers capabilities, version, launch and resume: the onboarding and trust seed, three posture words and their flags, /wake {seat} as the first turn, 2.1.280 declared measured, and the two Claude Code doctor checks carried by the pack
description:
SPEC (fleet-jymr.2, drafted 2026-09-25). In fleet-packs; sites at 2a48e90. Blocked by fleet-jymr.1 (the skeleton and its libs), fleet-031 (narrowed per E15: the re-measure on 2.1.280 of the entries the pack keeps) and fleet-rge6.2 and fleet-rge6.4 (the trust-seed and flagged-resume measurements this row ports).

**Behaviour.** Four verbs, each a port of the in-process ClaudeCode after fleet-rge6.2, fleet-rge6.4, fleet-14p8.3 and fleet-1jr1e; nothing is re-decided.

- **First step (Reviewer call 2026-09-25, E14).** B10 and D8, which launch rests on, were measured on 2.1.282 (brain/lessons/claude-code.md:610, :908). Re-measure both on 2.1.280 (scratch config dir, scratch socket) and record them on the pack's lessons (fleet-jymr.6) before `measured` is declared.
- `capabilities` → `postures: ["ask", "auto", "unattended"]`, `default_model: "claude-opus-5"` (controller/src/policy.rs:39; lessons A5), `first_turn: "/wake {seat}"` (policy.rs:60), `context: true`, `measured: ["2.1.280"]` (core/src/supported.rs:35), `posture_models: {auto: ["claude-opus-5", "claude-fable-5", "claude-sonnet-5"]}` (policy.rs 54-55, prefix match, lessons D3; E9).
- `version` → `{name: "claude-code", version}`: the first token of `claude --version` under the bound (parse_version, claude_code.rs 855-857), or `null` when claude cannot run or exits non-zero (644-652). Comparing it with `measured` stays core's (run.rs 1119-1150; ruling 8).
- `launch` → `{argv, env}`. The argv is the pane's own command (E2): `[claudeBin(), "--name", name, "--model", model, "--permission-mode", <flag>, "--plugin-dir", pluginDir(), first_turn]`. Today's start argv (claude_code.rs 459-468) without `--bg`; the plugin dir is the adapter's own, never a request field (E8).
  - **Ruled 2026-09-25 (ruling 14): three words, the rest refused.** ask → `default`, auto → `auto`, unattended → `dontAsk`. Core reads stored `default`/`auto`/`dontAsk` as aliases (fleet-1jr1e). A request carrying any other posture exits 1 `refused`, naming the word and the three.
  - `env` is set exactly (D1, E2): `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` = the seat's config dir when the request names one; `CLAUDE_SECURESTORAGE_CONFIG_DIR` = `credentialDir()`, defined even when empty (with_environment 179-203; A11); plus the request's `env` (core's `FLEET_ACTOR`, `FLEET_BIN`, PATH).
  - **The seed** (lessons D8; fleet-rge6.2's rules moved out of the controller). When the request names a config dir, launch writes `<config_dir>/.claude.json` through `writeInside`, merged into any file there. It copies `hasCompletedOnboarding`, `lastOnboardingVersion`, `theme` and `oauthAccount` from the operator's own `.claude.json` (`<CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR>/.claude.json` when that is set, else `$HOME/.claude.json`). A source missing a key refuses, naming it.
  - **Ruled 2026-09-25 (ruling 13): trust is seeded.** The same file gets the trust acceptance for the seat's own worktree, under the key and shape fleet-rge6.2's first step records on 2.1.280, and nothing else. fleet trusts only worktrees it created, so the entry is written only for a seat with a scoped config dir, which only a spawn into fleet's own worktree has. If fleet-rge6.2 finds the seed does not hold, this line goes and the screen fallback (D8: Down, then Enter) is core's.
  - The permission file, rendered from the request's neutral `permissions`, is fleet-jymr.5's; launch calls it.
- `resume` → `[claudeBin(), "--resume", session_id, "--model", model, "--permission-mode", <flag>, "--plugin-dir", pluginDir()]`, with the same env as launch. **Reviewer call 2026-09-25 (E3):** resume carries the start flags with the full id. fleet-rge6.4 measures on 2.1.280 that it keeps plugin, model and posture (A9 was background-only); the pack ports fleet-rge6.4's argv.
- **Two doctor checks move into the pack,** as fleet-rsia.5 moved bd-version:
  - `doctor/claude-code-version/` comes from core/defaults/doctor/claude-code-version. Its `SUPPORTED=2.1.280` (run.sh:33) becomes the pack's, held equal to `measured`'s last entry by a deno test that replaces core/tests/pack.rs 951-1037.
  - `doctor/isolation-pair/` comes from core/defaults/doctor/isolation-pair (run.sh 27-53). It is wholly Claude Code's.
  - `FLEET_CLAUDE_BIN` stays their seam. The defaults' copies go in fleet-x93d.2.

**Sites (source ported).** controller/src/adapter/claude_code.rs 179-203, 286, 392-416, 436-492, 502-504, 644-652, 855-857; controller/src/policy.rs 39, 47-49, 54-55, 60; core/src/supported.rs 20-35; core/defaults/doctor/claude-code-version/, core/defaults/doctor/isolation-pair/.

**Interfaces produced.** `lib/capabilities.ts` (fleet-jymr.6's pin arm and fleet-jymr.7 read it); `pluginDir()` (fleet-jymr.5 fills the directory); `lib/seed.ts seedOnboarding(configDir)`, `seedTrust(configDir, worktree)`; `lib/posture.ts flagFor(posture)`.

**Acceptance.**
- Offline `fleet agent check --adapter <path>/main.ts` passes capabilities, version (null with no claude on PATH counts as an answer, fleet-14p8.8), launch and resume.
- deno tests:
  - launch's argv for each posture (`ask` gives `--permission-mode default`), and `acceptEdits` is refused;
  - the credential variable is present in its empty and named arms;
  - the seed holds the four onboarding keys and the trust entry for exactly the request's worktree, keeps a present file's other keys, and refuses a source missing `oauthAccount`;
  - no trust entry is written for a named seat;
  - resume's argv carries the full id and the three start flags;
  - a config dir that is a symlink out of itself is refused.
- `--live` (fleet-jymr.7): a launched seat in a fresh worktree reaches idle with no trust dialog.
- `fleet doctor` lists both checks from the pack.

**Reviewer call 2026-09-25.** Reading `$HOME/.claude.json` widens nothing: fleet-jymr.1's `--allow-read` is already unscoped, because a static shebang cannot name the per-request directories. The write helper's refusal is the boundary that matters, and it holds.

title: The claude-code pack stands in fleet-packs: a manifest carrying its hook mapping, one main.ts that dispatches the six verbs, contract types generated from fleet agent schema, and the least Deno grant that runs claude
description:
SPEC (fleet-jymr.1, drafted 2026-09-25). In fleet-packs; this repository's sites at 2a48e90. Blocked by fleet-rsia.1 (the repo, runtimes/ts and adapters/agent/ exist), fleet-14p8.5 (`fleet agent schema`, the types' source) and fleet-14p8.4 (the `[hook]` table's keys).

**Behaviour.** The claude-code agent pack's skeleton: every verb dispatched, `capabilities` the only one answered in full; fleet-jymr.2–fleet-jymr.4 fill the rest.

- `adapters/agent/claude-code/pack.toml`: `[pack] name = "claude-code"`, `version = "0.1.0"`, `schema = 3` (core/src/pack.rs:84), a description naming Claude Code 2.1.280; `[imports.ts] source = "../../../runtimes/ts"`, the bd pack's pattern (fleet-rsia.2): a pack whose adapter runs on Deno imports the runtime pack rather than pinning Deno itself. The name `claude-code` is the default core resolves when `[agent] adapter` is unset, and `claude_code` its alias (Reviewer call 2026-09-25, E12); the pack answers to the first only, and the alias is core's.
- `adapters/agent/claude-code/adapters/agent/claude-code/adapter.toml`: `[adapter]` with the five keys core reads (core/src/pack.rs:40 ADAPTER_KEYS; `kind = "agent"`, AdapterKind 44-66), `entry = "main.ts"`. `[hook]` in fleet-14p8.4's key names, carrying Claude Code's mapping exactly as cli/src/claude.rs states it today: tool `/tool_name` (the guard acts on `Bash` only, claude.rs:30), command `/tool_input/command`, cwd `/cwd`, no paths pointer (fleet-14p8.4 dropped it: no guard class reads a path); deny template `{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PreToolUse","permissionDecision":"deny","permissionDecisionReason":"{reason}"}}` (claude.rs `refusal`). It equals the built-in manifest fleet-14p8.4 compiles in, until fleet-x93d.2 deletes that one; fleet-jymr.7's CI diffs the two.
- `main.ts`, executable, shebang `#!/usr/bin/env -S deno run --allow-run=claude --allow-read --allow-write --allow-env=HOME,CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR,FLEET_CLAUDE_BIN`. It reads one JSON value off stdin, dispatches `Deno.args[0]` to `verbs/<verb>.ts`, prints one JSON value carrying `schema_version: 1`, and exits by fleet-14p8.2's table: an unknown verb or a request that fails the schema is 2; a `claude` that cannot be run is 3 with `{error}`; stderr's last line is for people.
- The grant: `--allow-read`/`--allow-write` cannot be narrowed on a static shebang to the per-request `config_dir` (the limit fleet-rsia.2 documents for bd's root), so the pack documents the grant, and every write goes through one helper that refuses a path resolving outside the request's config dir and worktree (Reviewer call 2026-09-25, E8: launch may write in both, since the transient permission file lands in the worktree today, controller/src/transient.rs:703). `--allow-run=claude` covers the bare name; an absolute `FLEET_CLAUDE_BIN` needs its path added to the grant, documented as `FLEET_BD_BIN` is.
- `contract.d.ts`: generated by `deno task types` from `fleet agent schema` (the emitter fleet-rsia.2 chose, reused), committed; a hand-edited type is a defect.
- `capabilities` answers fleet-jymr.2's values from `lib/capabilities.ts`, so `fleet agent check` exercises the envelope from this row on.

**Sites (this repository, read, not edited).** cli/src/claude.rs 1-56 (the mapping's source: `payload`, `refusal`); core/src/pack.rs 33-84 (slot, manifest keys, schema); controller/src/adapter/claude_code.rs:66 (`DEFAULT_TIMEOUT`, the 20 s per-call bound fleet-14p8.2 carries), 132-160 and 302-310 (the binary's resolution and `FLEET_CLAUDE_BIN`, which the pack keeps as its own seam), 392-416 (`config_dir_from`, `credential_dir_from`).

**Interfaces produced.** `lib/claude.ts`: `claudeBin()` (`FLEET_CLAUDE_BIN` when absolute and executable, refused when relative, else `claude`: resolve_effect_bin's rule) and `run(argv, {configDir, credentialDir}, boundMs)`; `lib/answer.ts` (envelope, exit table); `lib/config_dir.ts`: `writeInside(roots: {configDir?, worktree}, path, body)`, `configDirFor(seat)` (the request's optional `config_dir` (E9: named seats have none), else `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, else `$HOME/.claude`), `credentialDir()` (`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` trimmed, or empty: lessons A11). fleet-jymr.2–fleet-jymr.5 consume them.

**Acceptance.** `fleet pack add <fleet-packs>//adapters/agent/claude-code --version main` installs it with ts imported; `fleet agent check --adapter <path>/main.ts` passes the capabilities checks and reports the unfilled verbs as failing with exit 2, never as a crash; `deno task types && git diff --exit-code contract.d.ts` is clean; `deno fmt --check` and `deno lint` clean; a deno test refuses a `writeInside` path outside both roots (`../x`) and a `FLEET_CLAUDE_BIN` naming a relative path.

**Reviewer call 2026-09-25.** fleet-14p8.6's agent exec inherits the controller's environment, as the store's exec does (core/src/store/exec.rs), so `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` and `FLEET_CLAUDE_BIN` reach this process with no manifest key; the per-seat variables travel in the request, not the environment.

title: A pack turns on core's guard classes by declaring them in pack.toml, and fleet guard with no class runs the classes the layers declare
description:
SPEC (fleet-14p8.9, drafted 2026-09-25). Sites at 2a48e90. Blocked by fleet-14p8.4 (`fleet guard --adapter`, the path the declared classes run through). If fleet-rsia.1 has already moved packs/tiny out, tiny's edit lands in fleet-packs' `tiny/pack.toml`.

**Behaviour.** Reviewer call 2026-09-25 (E11): class declarations only. Which guards a session runs stops being a provider's hook file and becomes a pack declaration that `fleet guard` reads (ruling 6). There is no pattern-rule language.

Today the four `fleet guard <class>` lines are wired in three Claude Code hook files:
- hooks/hooks.json 7-22: all four, and the plugin loads this one;
- core/defaults/overlay/per-provider/claude/hooks.json: shell-trap and record;
- packs/tiny/overlay/per-provider/claude/hooks.json 7-10: all four.

After this row, ruling 6's one line, `fleet guard --adapter <name>` with no class, runs:
- core's two classes, shell-trap and record, always. They are the classes "every fleet gets" (core/src/guard/mod.rs 4-11). They need no declaration, because the defaults layer carries no manifest (core/src/resolve.rs 22-24).
- every class an installed layer's `pack.toml` declares, run in `CLASSES` order (guard/mod.rs 87-92) with the first refusal winning.

Each class still honours its `[guards].<class>.enabled` opt-out in the fleet's or project's own file (guard/mod.rs 293-309, and `enabled_in` as main.rs 1219-1262 resolves it).

- **The declaration.** Reviewer call 2026-09-25: pack.toml's `[pack]` table gains one key, so it cannot be mistaken for the fleet file's `[guards]` opt-out table (core/src/policy.rs 30, 62):
  ```toml
  [pack]
  guard_classes = ["release-ref", "production-write"]
  ```
  tiny declares exactly that. It restates tiny's hook lines: two of its four are core's and run anyway. A name outside the four `Class::parse` names (guard/mod.rs 95-103) is a pack defect. A value that is not a list of strings is a defect too.
- **The verb.** `fleet guard [<CLASS>] --adapter <name>` (cli/src/main.rs 344-352: `class` becomes `Option<Class>`). A named class runs that class alone, exactly as today. With no class, `guard_run` (1149-1167) loops the declared set. `guard_check` (1169-1209) with no class reports every class in the set. The set is `guard::declared(&Packs) -> Vec<Class>`, core's two plus the union of each layer's `Manifest.guards`, read through `Packs::under` (core/src/item/brief.rs 39-41) with the machine's pack dirs that main.rs 1373-1384 already builds.
- **What reads the set.** `fleet prime`'s guards line (cli/src/prime.rs 68-70, 100) and the brief's (core/src/item/brief.rs 164-175, 278) name the declared set, not all of `CLASSES`. A class that is declared but switched off prints as switched off, as today.
- **The defaults' permissions deny list** (core/defaults/overlay/per-provider/claude/permissions.json, `deny`) stays the adapter's permissions format (fleet-jymr.5). Its entries are tool-level denials (AskUserQuestion, EnterPlanMode, `mcp__*__request_access`) and push patterns that no class declaration expresses.

**Sites.**
- core/src/pack.rs:
  - the `[pack]` table's key list gains `guard_classes`.
  - `Manifest` 169-181 gains `guards: Vec<guard::Class>`.
  - `parse_manifest` 433+ parses and checks it, with a `Defect` variant for an unknown class.
- core/src/guard/mod.rs: `declared`, and the header 4-11 rewritten: which pack classes run is the pack's declaration, not its overlay.
- packs/tiny/pack.toml (the table).
- cli/src/main.rs 344-352, 1142-1209.
- cli/src/prime.rs 68-70, 100.
- core/src/item/brief.rs 164-175, 278.

title: fleet agent check proves an agent adapter: offline against the fixtures it ships, and with --live against the real agent in a scratch worktree under a scratch tmux socket
description:
SPEC (fleet-14p8.8, drafted 2026-09-25). Sites at 2a48e90. Blocked by fleet-14p8.7 (the stub it is proven on), and so by fleet-14p8.6 and fleet-14p8.5.

**Behaviour.** `fleet agent check [--adapter <path|name>] [--live]` runs the agent contract's checks against one adapter. Its output, exits and flush-per-line are `fleet store check`'s (cli/src/store.rs 94-221; docs/store.md 537-599). Without `--adapter` it checks what the fleet's `[agent] adapter` selects, else the built-in. `--adapter` takes an absolute path or a pack's name, resolved as fleet-14p8.6 resolves the key.

- **The library.** `controller/src/adapter/conformance.rs` (new, as store/conformance.rs 1-146 is). In the controller because the trait is (fleet-14p8.3): `Ctx { agent: &dyn Agent, fixtures: Option<&Path>, scratch: &Path }`, `CHECKS: &[(&str, Check)]` and `run(&Ctx) -> impl Iterator`. Live checks take the host as a seam.
- **Offline checks, in order.** `version` answers with a name; `capabilities` validates; each declared posture launches (a non-empty argv, nothing written outside the scratch `config_dir` and `worktree` (E8), the tree walked before and after); an undeclared posture is refused `unsupported`; `resume` of a made-up id answers an argv or `missing`; `read` of no seats answers none; `read` and `context` match each fixture (context skipped where undeclared); an unknown verb and a `schema_version: 2` request each exit 2. Every answer also passes fleet-14p8.5's schema through `fleet_core::schema::check`.
- **Fixtures.** The adapter ships `fixtures/` beside its `adapter.toml` (or `--fixtures <dir>` for a bare path). Each case is `fixtures/<verb>/<case>/{request.json, answer.json, env.json?}`. `{fixture}` in any request string is replaced by the case's absolute directory, so a recorded listing or transcript sits beside it. `env.json` is set on that one call, so an adapter replays its recording (the Claude Code pack puts a recorded `claude agents --json --all` behind its own binary seam). A case passes when the answer equals `answer.json`, envelope removed. No fixtures SKIPs those checks.
- **`--live`.** Costs a model turn, so never by default. A temp dir holds a git worktree (fleet-made, so launch may trust it: Ruled 2026-09-25, ruling 13), a `config_dir`, and a tmux server on socket `fleet-check-<pid>`, never the controller's `fleet` (E1). Core's fleet-rge6.1 host drives it (ruling 2), and the pane's command is launch's argv with its env set exactly (E2). Steps, each a line: `launch` → host `new` → `read` goes `starting` then `idle` within 60 s; one one-word turn, sent as a bracketed paste and then a separate submit (E4, D8) → `busy` within 10 s, then `idle`; host kill → pane dead with an exit status; `resume` with the learned `session_id` → `idle`; `context` answers `turns ≥ 1` and a `last_write` after the turn. Then kill and remove the temp dir whatever happened (a Drop guard, as cli/src/store.rs 78-86). The summary names the agent's `version`, because these steps rest on B10 and D8 (E14).

**Sites.** controller/src/adapter/conformance.rs (new); cli/src/agent.rs (`Verb::Check { adapter, fixtures, live }`); cli/tests/agent_check.rs (new: every offline check passes on target/debug/fleet-agent-stub with its own fixtures dir; a stub scripted to write outside `config_dir` FAILs that check and names the path; a relative `--adapter` exits 2; `--live` against the stub's `session` mode on real tmux, skipped without tmux); docs/agent.md `## Checking an adapter` with its refusal table, through the docs skill.

**Interfaces produced.** `fleet_controller::adapter::conformance::{run, CHECKS, Ctx, Passed}`, the fixture layout, and the verb. fleet-jymr.3, fleet-jymr.4 (fixtures recorded to this layout) and fleet-jymr.7 (CI: offline on every push, `--live` nightly) consume them.

**Acceptance.** `fleet agent check --adapter $PWD/target/debug/fleet-agent-stub` prints only PASS and SKIP lines, ending `agent check: stub — N passed, 0 failed, M skipped`, and exits 0 in under 5 s. The same with `--live` on a box with tmux ≥ 3.7b exits 0 and leaves no `fleet-check-*` socket behind (`tmux -L fleet-check-<pid> ls` fails).

**Reviewer calls 2026-09-25.** (1) The live check logs in exactly as a spawned seat does: the scratch `config_dir` with the credential knob defined empty, so the operator's login is used and nothing else of theirs (A11). (2) The live turn runs on `capabilities.default_model` unless `--model <m>` names another; CI (fleet-jymr.7) passes the cheapest model the adapter's `posture_models` gate allows for the posture it launches.

title: fleet-agent-stub answers the agent contract from a fake whose state is a file, and the controller and cli suites run on it through Exec with no claude and no tmux
description:
SPEC (fleet-14p8.7, drafted 2026-09-25). Sites at 2a48e90. Blocked by fleet-14p8.6 (Exec and `[agent] adapter`) and fleet-rge6.1 (`FakeHost`, the `FLEET_TMUX_BIN` seam and `fleet-tmux-stub`). Precedent: fleet-wpf0.7 (fleet-store-stub, open), whose shape this copies.

**Behaviour.** A test-only executable that answers every agent verb from the rebuilt `StubAgent` (fleet-14p8.3). Every agent path a suite drives then goes through `AgentExec` with no `claude` on the box and no shell stub. Each Exec call is a fresh process, so the fake's state lives in a file.

- **The binary.** `controller/src/bin/agent_stub.rs`, with `[[bin]] name = "fleet-agent-stub", required-features = ["test-support"]` in controller/Cargo.toml. Today that file has no `[[bin]]`, and `test-support = []` sits at 17-18.
- **One call.** `fleet-agent-stub <verb>` reads the request off stdin and loads `<root>/.agent-stub/state.json`: the `Answers` of test_support.rs 91-121 as rebuilt by fleet-14p8.3 (capabilities, version, per-seat activity and context, a `launch`/`resume` refusal to answer), plus a call log. It answers through the fleet-14p8.2 types and appends `{verb, request}` to the log. It writes the state back, prints the answer with `schema_version: 1`, and exits by the table: 0; 1 with the scripted `{"refused": …}`; 2 for an unknown verb, an undecodable request, or `context` while undeclared; 3 for a scripted could-not-tell.
- **What launch answers.** `argv = [<its own path>, "session", <seat>]`. Run in a pane, `fleet-agent-stub session <seat>` is the fake agent process. It sets the seat `idle`, flips it to `busy` on a line of input then back to `idle`, and exits on `/exit`, writing each move into state.json. Under real tmux, which is fleet-rge6.1's one integration arm and fleet-14p8.8's `--live` against the stub, a suite sees starting → idle → busy with no model. Under `fleet-tmux-stub` no pane process runs, and the rig scripts the activity instead (below). `resume` answers the same argv with the session id.
- **Scripting.** `fleet_controller::test_support::agent_stub::{path() -> PathBuf, script(root, |a: &mut Answers|)}` writes state.json between ticks, the file twin of `StubAgent::set` (167-169). `calls(root) -> Vec<Call>` reads the log back into the `Call` shape of 74-83, so arms written against `verbs()`/`calls_of()` (171-190) port by swapping the source. Two failure seams: `FLEET_STUB_SLOW=<secs>` sleeps before answering (for the 20 s bound arms), and `FLEET_STUB_DEAF=1` answers without writing state.
- **Hosts (Reviewer call 2026-09-25, E7).** The in-process controller suites pair the stub with fleet-rge6.1's `FakeHost`. The binary-driven cli suites set `FLEET_TMUX_BIN` to fleet-rge6.1's `fleet-tmux-stub`, which keeps its state in a file, and read its recorded new-session commands to assert the launched argv. This row adds `FLEET_TMUX_BIN` and the agent key beside `CLAUDE_BIN` in the hermetic env list (controller/tests/common/hermetic.rs 23-36) if fleet-rge6.1 has not.
- **Suites move.** controller/tests/{adoption,blocked_poll,effects,observe,rehost,routines,transient,substrate}.rs, and cli/tests/drive/rig.rs, whose shell `claude` stub (1541-1620, file seams per verb, the escape helper 1636-1658) goes. So do `adapter_at` 1729-1739 and cli/tests/drive_causes.rs, drive_effects.rs, run.rs and in_process.rs where they name `FLEET_CLAUDE_BIN`. Each writes `[agent] adapter = "<stub path>"` into the rig's fleet.toml. controller/tests/common/hermetic.rs 31-36 and `refusing_stub` 160-177 remain for the arms that are about the in-process adapter's binary resolution, and nowhere else.

**Sites.** controller/Cargo.toml; controller/src/bin/agent_stub.rs (new); controller/src/test_support.rs (state (de)serialization, the `agent_stub` helpers); the suites above. The cli's tests reach the binary through `env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_fleet")`'s directory, as fleet-wpf0.7 does for core's.

**Interfaces produced.** The binary beside `fleet` in target/debug, `agent_stub::{path, script, calls}`, and a cli/tests/common helper `stub_agent(fleet_root) -> PathBuf` that writes the key and an empty state. fleet-14p8.8 (the check's own arms) and fleet-jymr.7 (CI's offline gate against a known-good adapter) consume them.

**Acceptance.**
- `fleet agent check --adapter target/debug/fleet-agent-stub` passes every offline check (fleet-14p8.8).
- `git grep -n "FLEET_CLAUDE_BIN\|#!/bin/sh" -- cli/tests/drive controller/tests` finds only the in-process adapter's own resolution arms.
- The workspace suite passes on a box whose PATH holds no `claude`, with `FLEET_TEST_HERMETIC=1`.
- Every stub answer decodes through `adapter::exec::answer` and passes fleet-14p8.5's schema.
- A `read` the rig scripts as `blocked`/`permission` publishes the seat prompt-blocked.
- A `launch` scripted to refuse `unsupported` writes one `dispatch.failed` naming the stub's message.

**Reviewer call 2026-09-25.** No `die_after_commit` mode: nothing consumes it yet. It is added the day the run lifecycle's crash re-dispatch has an arm that needs it.

title: An agent adapter can be an executable: [agent] adapter names it by path or by a pack's name, and fleet speaks the agent contract to it one process per call
description:
SPEC (fleet-14p8.6, drafted 2026-09-25). Sites at 2a48e90. Blocked by fleet-14p8.1 (the shared call), fleet-14p8.3 (the trait and `adapter::open`), and fleet-14p8.4 (the lifted `pack::adapter_dir`, if it lands first; otherwise this row lifts it).

**Behaviour.** The agent side gets the store's three pieces (ruling 11): the key, the opener, and an Exec.

- **The key.** `[agent] adapter` in the fleet's own `fleet.toml`, fleet-wide. core/src/policy.rs gains the table and the pair: `TABLES` 20-36 becomes ten, with `"agent"` and its doc line, and `CENSUS` 40-98 takes `("agent", "adapter")` with a comment beside `("store", "adapter")` at 95-97. 
- **The opener.** `adapter::open` (fleet-14p8.3) reads the key as `store::open` does (core/src/store/mod.rs 356-382):
  - absent → the default name `"claude-code"` (`adapter::DEFAULT_NAME`), and `"claude_code"` is an alias of it. Reviewer call 2026-09-25 (E12). The name resolves through the packs like any other, so flight 13's pack at `adapters/agent/claude-code/` wins once it is installed. While claude_code.rs stands, a name that no pack carries falls back to the in-process `ClaudeCode`, and fleet-x93d.2 deletes that fallback. fleet-x93d.1 offers no `none`.
  - an absolute path to an executable file → `AgentExec`.
  - a bare name → `pack::adapter_dir(packs, AdapterKind::Agent, name)`, then `pack::adapter_manifest` (pack.rs 866-945), then its `entry`.
  - anything else → refused.
  Every refusal is worded once, in a `Unopened` twin of store/mod.rs 430-469, naming `[agent] adapter` or `--adapter` and, for a name nowhere, `fleet pack add <repo>//adapters/agent/<name> --version <version>`. `AGENT_CLAUDE_CODE = "claude_code"` (controller/src/policy.rs 534-540) survives only as the `[substrate]` key until fleet-x93d.2.
- **AgentExec.** `controller/src/adapter/exec.rs` (new): `AgentExec::at(entry, root).with_timeout(d)`, one `fleet_core::adapter::exec::run` per verb, with the request built by `adapter::exec::envelope(fields, root, agent::types::CONTRACT_VERSION)`. The exit table maps as fleet-14p8.2 writes it: 1 → `AgentError::Refused(Refusal)`; 2, 3, off-table and signal → `Unreadable`, worded "the agent contract" and carrying stderr's last line. The bound is `timeout_from(FLEET_AGENT_TIMEOUT_MS)` (claude_code.rs 364-384), 20 s by default. `capabilities` is validated before it is used, as store exec.rs 359-368 does. `context` is asked only where declared, as exec.rs 377-389 asks `export`. `read` and `context` send all seats in one call.
- **The effects gate.** For an exec adapter, `Opened.effects_off` is the cause when `capabilities` or `version` does not answer or `version.version` is null: the twin of today's `resolve_effect_bin` failure (claude_code.rs 132-155). `fleet start` (cli/src/lifecycle.rs 582-591) refuses on it with exit 3, as it does today.
- **Hermetic.** Under `FLEET_TEST_HERMETIC` (claude_code.rs 331-362), an unset `[agent] adapter` with no `FLEET_CLAUDE_BIN` still refuses, so a suite never falls through to a live `claude`.

**Sites.** core/src/policy.rs 20-98 and its census arms; core/src/pack.rs (`adapter_dir`, lifted from core/src/store/mod.rs 403-428 unless fleet-14p8.4 did); controller/src/adapter/mod.rs (the opener arms and `Unopened`); controller/src/adapter/exec.rs (new); controller/src/run.rs 116-149 (`Wiring::resolve` hands the fleet's policy table and the machine's `PackDirs` to `open`); cli/src/item.rs, routines.rs, transient.rs and lifecycle.rs (the `open` sites fleet-14p8.3 made, now handed packs); docs/agent.md "Choosing an adapter" (as docs/store.md 19-52 and 584-599) and docs/packs.md 392-393 ("an agent adapter a pack carries is one a fleet can name in `[agent] adapter`"), through the docs skill.

**Interfaces produced.** `AgentExec`, the `[agent] adapter` key, `pack::adapter_dir`. fleet-14p8.7 (the stub is opened through a path), fleet-14p8.8 (`--adapter` on the check) and fleet-x93d.1 (create writes the key) consume them.

**Acceptance.** Arms in controller/src/adapter/exec.rs over a `#!/bin/sh` stub, the rig of store exec.rs 446-512:
- one `read` for three seats is one process whose stdin holds all three and `schema_version: 1`;
- exits 1 (`unsupported`), 2, 3 and 9 read by their rows;
- a 300 ms bound kills a sleeping stub's group;
- stderr's last line appears in the refusal;
- `context` is never run for `context: false`;
- a `capabilities` with empty `postures` refuses the open, naming the field.
Opener arms: `[agent] adapter = "nowhere"` refuses with the `fleet pack add` line; a fixture pack's `adapters/agent/x/` resolves to its entry; a non-executable entry is the pack defect line; an absent key, `"claude-code"` and `"claude_code"` open the in-process adapter when no pack carries the name, and a fixture pack's `adapters/agent/claude-code/` when one does. `fleet start` in a fleet whose adapter path is a stub that exits 3 on `capabilities` exits 3, naming the stub.

**Reviewer calls 2026-09-25.** (1) `[agent] adapter` resolves through the machine's installed packs, as drafted: the key is the fleet's, not a project's. (2) A null `version` turns effects off with the cause published, as drafted: it is today's behaviour when the agent binary does not resolve, and a fleet with no agent binary can start no seat anyway.

title: fleet agent schema prints the agent contract as one JSON Schema document, generated from its Rust types and committed with a drift test
description:
SPEC (fleet-14p8.5, drafted 2026-09-25). Sites at 2a48e90. Blocked by fleet-14p8.2 (the types). Precedent: fleet-wpf0.5 (landed 2a48e90), whose shape this copies verb for verb.

**Behaviour.** `fleet agent schema` prints the agent contract as one draft 2020-12 JSON Schema document on stdout and exits 0. It reads no fleet and runs no adapter. An adapter author fetches the contract from the binary they target, and flight 13's TypeScript pack generates `contract.d.ts` from it (fleet-jymr.1: a hand-edited type there is a defect).

- **The document.** `{"$schema", "schema_version": 1, "verbs": {"capabilities"|"version"|"launch"|"resume"|"read"|"context": {"request", "response"}}, "refusal", "error", "$defs"}`. It is the store document's shape (core/src/store/schema.rs 50-213; docs/store.md 519-535). A request is the envelope's `schema_version` and `root` plus the verb's fields, and stays open to keys it does not name (additions are optional within version 1). A response is `schema_version` plus the body. `refusal` is exit 1's answer and `error` is exit 3's. Every `$ref` points into the document's own `$defs`. Doc-comment descriptions are stripped, as schema.rs 22-26 rules for the store.
- **Enumerations are closed.** `Posture`, `activity`, `blocked_on` and `evidence` are `enum` lists, so an adapter author's generated types name the words.
- **Committed.** The document lives at `core/src/agent/agent.schema.json`. A drift arm regenerates and compares byte for byte, failing with `cargo run -p fleet-cli -- agent schema > core/src/agent/agent.schema.json`, as `the_committed_document_is_the_one_the_types_generate` (schema.rs 536-555) does. The binary prints `schema::text()` generated at run time, not `include_str!`, for the reason fleet-wpf0.5's landing note gives: the regeneration command redirects over the file.
- **Shared generation.** schema.rs's helpers are store-private today: `refer` 225-227, `generated` 230-237, the field and describe builders after 239, `strip`, and the validator `check` 332-338 with its `passes`/`KEYWORDS` (test-support only, regex-lite). They are lifted into `core/src/schema.rs` (new), and both documents build on them. The store's committed document must come out byte-identical after the lift, and its drift arm is the proof.

**Sites.** core/src/schema.rs (new, the lifted helpers); core/src/store/schema.rs (calls them, and its tests stay); core/src/agent/schema.rs (new: `document()`, `text()`) and agent.schema.json (new); core/src/agent/mod.rs (`pub mod schema;`); cli/src/agent.rs (new: `enum Verb { Schema }` now, which fleet-14p8.8 grows with `Check`, as cli/src/store.rs 36-73 is shaped); cli/src/main.rs (a `Family::Agent { verb }` beside `Store` at 138-142, with its dispatch arm beside 646, and the family's help); cli/tests/agent_schema.rs (new, a copy of cli/tests/store_schema.rs's arms); docs/agent.md gains `## The schema` before its checking section, through the docs skill, as docs/store.md 496-535.

**Interfaces produced.** `fleet_core::agent::schema::{document, text}`, `fleet_core::schema::{check, …}`, the file `core/src/agent/agent.schema.json`, and the verb `fleet agent schema`. fleet-jymr.1 consumes the file. fleet-14p8.7's stub arms and fleet-14p8.8's offline check validate answers with `fleet_core::schema::check`.

**Acceptance.**
- `fleet agent schema | jq '.verbs | keys'` prints exactly `["capabilities","context","launch","read","resume","version"]`, and the cli arm holds the binary's stdout to the committed file byte for byte.
- Adding a field to `Capabilities` without regenerating reds the drift arm with the regeneration command in its message.
- Every JSON example in docs/agent.md passes its verb's schema through `schema::check`, one arm per example, as schema.rs 679 does for the store.
- `jq '."$defs".Posture.enum'` answers `["ask","auto","unattended"]`.
- `core/src/store/store.schema.json` is unchanged by the lift: `git diff 2a48e90 -- core/src/store/store.schema.json` is empty.
- An arm walks the agent document for any keyword outside `KEYWORDS`, as `every_keyword_the_document_uses_is_one_the_check_knows` (schema.rs 557) does.

**Reviewer calls 2026-09-25.** (1) The family name is Alberto's and is ruled at the end of the spec pass; this row and fleet-14p8.8 and fleet-jymr.7 are written with `fleet agent` and are renamed if the ruling differs. (2) The schema helpers' lift stays inside this row: the store's committed document coming out byte-identical is its proof, and it keeps the two documents' shapes from drifting in separate landings.

title: fleet guard reads a provider's hook payload and writes its refusal through the agent adapter's declared [hook] mapping, and cli/src/claude.rs is gone
description:
SPEC (fleet-14p8.4, drafted 2026-09-25). Sites at 2a48e90. Blocked by fleet-14p8.2 (the agent adapter's manifest is the contract's).

**Behaviour.** Where a hook payload's fields sit, and what a refusal looks like, become data in the agent adapter's `adapter.toml` (ruling 5). No process is spawned per tool call: `fleet guard` reads one TOML file and applies core's provider-neutral policy.

- **The mapping.** An `adapter.toml` of kind `agent` may carry a `[hook]` table:
  ```toml
  [hook]
  shell_tool = "Bash"                    # the provider's name for its shell tool
  tool = "/tool_name"                    # JSON pointers into the payload
  command = "/tool_input/command"
    cwd = "/cwd"                           # optional
  deny = '{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PreToolUse","permissionDecision":"deny","permissionDecisionReason":{reason}}}'
  ```
  `{reason}` is replaced by the reason as a JSON string literal (quoted and escaped), and the template must parse as JSON after a test fill. core/src/pack.rs today refuses every table but `[adapter]` (889-891; ADAPTER_KEYS 40; docs/packs.md 384 says so). It takes `[hook]` on kind `agent` only, holds each key to its shape, and makes a `[hook]` on a store adapter a defect.
- **The reader.** `core/src/guard/hook.rs` (new): `HookMap::parse(&toml::Table) -> Result<HookMap, String>`, `HookMap::payload(&self, body: &str) -> Option<Payload { tool, command, paths, cwd }>` and `HookMap::deny(&self, reason: &str) -> String`. Its silence rules are cli/src/claude.rs 16-44 restated over pointers: not JSON, tool ≠ `shell_tool`, no tool, command absent/non-string/blank → `None`. The module states no decision value itself; the template is the adapter's, so guard/mod.rs's rule at 15-18 and 25-31 still holds.
- **The verb.** `fleet guard <CLASS> [--adapter <name|path>]` (main.rs 338-352). `guard_run` 1149-1167 swaps `claude::payload`/`claude::refusal` for the map. An absolute path names an adapter directory, and a bare name resolves `adapters/agent/<name>/adapter.toml` through the machine's packs over its defaults (the dirs main.rs 1373-1384 already builds), by the slot lookup store/mod.rs 403-428 makes. That lookup is lifted into `pack::adapter_dir(packs, AdapterKind, name)`, which fleet-14p8.6 reuses.
- **The built-in.** With no `--adapter`, or with `claude-code` (and its alias `claude_code`, Reviewer call 2026-09-25, E12) when no pack carries it, the map is Claude Code's built-in manifest, `controller/src/adapter/claude_code.hook.toml`, `include_str!`'d as `claude_code::HOOK_MANIFEST`. It lives beside the in-process adapter, per the brief's constraint, until fleet-x93d.2 deletes both. Every wired hook today — hooks/hooks.json 7-22, core/defaults/overlay/per-provider/claude/hooks.json and tiny's — keeps working unchanged. Moving the wiring to `--adapter claude-code` is fleet-jymr.5's.
- **Deleted.** cli/src/claude.rs (56 lines) and main.rs:11.

**Sites.** core/src/pack.rs 40, 68-80 (`AdapterManifest` gains `hook: Option<toml::Table>`), 866-945; core/src/store/mod.rs 403-428 (onto the lifted lookup); core/src/guard/mod.rs:33-37 (`pub mod hook;`) and the header prose; cli/src/main.rs 11, 338-352, 1142-1167; cli/src/claude.rs (deleted); controller/src/adapter/claude_code.rs (the const) and the new .toml; docs/guards.md 24-43 and 369-378, and docs/packs.md 373-393, through the docs skill.

**Interfaces produced.** `fleet_core::guard::hook::{HookMap, Payload}`, `fleet_core::pack::adapter_dir`, `AdapterManifest.hook`, `claude_code::HOOK_MANIFEST`. fleet-14p8.6 (lookup and the name `claude-code`), fleet-14p8.9 (the `fleet guard --adapter` path it runs declared classes through), fleet-jymr.1 (the pack's own `[hook]`) and fleet-x93d.2 (deletes the const) consume them.

**Acceptance.**
- cli/tests/guard.rs's 18 arms pass unchanged.
- The docs/guards.md:36-37 example prints byte-identical output with and without `--adapter claude-code`.
- A fixture pack `adapters/agent/other/` with `shell_tool = "shell"`, `command = "/input/cmd"` and a plain-text template makes `fleet guard shell-trap --adapter other` refuse a trapped command in that template, and stay silent on a Claude Code payload.

title: The Agent trait is the six contract verbs, the in-process Claude Code answers them, and every caller opens the agent through agent::open
description:
SPEC (fleet-14p8.3, drafted 2026-09-25). Sites at 2a48e90 (re-read each on flight 11's tip, which rewrites several). Blocked by fleet-14p8.2 (the types) and flight 11 (tmux owns the session: short ids, `daemon()`, `DaemonRead`, `nudge` and the stopped-row window are already gone).

**First step (E14).** `read`'s mapping rests on B10, which was measured on 2.1.282. Unless fleet-rge6.3 already recorded it, re-measure on the pinned 2.1.280 (interactive row `status` idle/busy/waiting, `waitingFor` at a dialog) and record the version.

**Behaviour.** The trait in `controller/src/adapter/mod.rs` (74-163 today) becomes the contract's six verbs over fleet-14p8.2's types:
- `capabilities()`, `version()`
- `launch(&Launch) -> Result<Argv, AgentError>`
- `resume(&Resume) -> Result<Argv, AgentError>`
- `read(&[SeatRef]) -> Result<Vec<Activity>, AgentError>`
- `context(&[SeatRef]) -> Result<Vec<SeatContext>, AgentError>`

`AgentError` is `{Refused(Refusal), Unreadable(String)}`. The adapter never touches tmux (ruling 2). Reviewer call 2026-09-25 (E2): the agent is the pane's own process. Core's fleet-rge6.1 host makes a session on `tmux -L fleet` (E1), named by seat id, whose command is `launch`'s argv (`resume`'s for a revive), environment set exactly (D1), and captures the `screen` `read` is handed.

`ClaudeCode` (claude_code.rs) implements the trait, and every Claude Code fact moves inside it:
- **launch.** The argv is fleet-rge6.2's interactive one: `--name`, `--model`, `--permission-mode` (453-461), the plugin dir (465-467) and the first turn (468). The answered env is `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` and `CLAUDE_SECURESTORAGE_CONFIG_DIR` (179-201, A11). Core adds the constructed `PATH`, `PASSED_THROUGH` (286), `FLEET_BIN` and `FLEET_ACTOR` (315-319; D1, D7). Inside the scoped config dir it seeds the onboarding keys (D8). Ruled 2026-09-25 (ruling 13): it also seeds the trust acceptance for the seat's own worktree, using the key fleet-rge6.2 measured.
- **launch permissions.** The request's neutral `permissions` are rendered into the worktree's `.claude/settings.local.json`, the write controller/src/transient.rs:703 makes today through `local_settings` (adapter/mod.rs:86, claude_code.rs 421-423), which leaves the trait. Until fleet-jymr.5 the template is still the layers' `overlay/per-provider/claude/permissions.json` (cli/src/transient.rs 615, 647-706, 758), handed to the in-process adapter at `open`. The plugin dir is the adapter's own (E8): for the in-process adapter that is policy.rs 118-126's `plugin_dir`, also handed at `open`, and fleet-x93d.2 deletes the key.
- **resume.** The full-id resume carries the start's flags (E3, as fleet-rge6.4 measured).
- **read.** One `agents --json --all` per distinct config dir, which is `Rosters::gather` (observe.rs 156-179) moved inside. Rows are matched by session_id, else by the request's `pid` (the pane's, fleet-14p8.2), exactly the attribution fleet-rge6.3 made; the cwd match (observe.rs 239-251) is already gone with fleet-rge6.3 and does not come back. `status`/`waitingFor` map to activity and `blocked_on` with evidence `typed` (B8, B10). The logged-out transcript reading (observe.rs 455-495, A11) becomes `blocked_on: logged_out`. E6: `AgentRow`, `RosterRead`, `parse_roster` and `BUSY/DONE/STOPPED/FAILED` (adapter/mod.rs 169-284; claude_code.rs 802-814) go private, so no short id leaves the adapter.
- **context.** From observe.rs: `context_tokens_in` 439-453, `turns_in` 540-548 and the transcript structs 386-418. From adapter/mod.rs: `encode_project_dir`/`transcript_path` 346-358 (C1). The transcript mtime (`ended_at` 627-642, C4) becomes `last_write`.
- **capabilities.** `default_model` comes from policy.rs:39 and `first_turn` from :60. The postures and `posture_models` come from 47-55 (D3). `measured` is `[PINNED_CLAUDE_CODE]` (supported.rs:35), and `context` is true.
- **version.** `parse_version` 855-857.

**Core, after.**
- observe (fleet-rge6.3's) takes activity from `read`.
- run.rs 668-676 and transient.rs 1687-1708 take tokens and turns from `context`, and the recency fallback reads `last_write`.
- `logged_out_dispatch` (observe.rs 512-522) keeps its policy terms and reads `blocked_on == logged_out`.
- `model_for` 359-361 and `first_turn_for` 336-338 fall back to capabilities.
- `claude_code_expected` 375-380 is the `[substrate]` pin, else `capabilities.measured`, feeding run.rs 928 and 1129-1131.
- Posture crosses as `Posture`. Until fleet-1jr1e lands, the two stored defaults (`auto`, `dontAsk`) convert through a two-word reader, which fleet-1jr1e replaces.
- **Projection (E13).** `Projection` (projection.rs 24-34) gains a neutral `agent` block: `{adapter, name, version, expected, postures}`. `agent_version`/`agent_version_expected` stay as mirrors; `fleet.claude_code` (178) is fleet-x93d.2's; docs/status.md via the docs skill.

**One opener.** `fleet_controller::adapter::open(&Opening) -> Result<Opened, String>`, where `Opened { agent: Box<dyn Agent>, effects_off: Option<String> }` carries today's gate. `resolve_effect_bin` 132-155 and `configured_bin` 344-355 become private to it. It replaces the five `ClaudeCode::new` sites:
- run.rs 119-149
- item.rs 1313/1351-1358
- routines.rs 186-192 and 412-424
- transient.rs 807-816

Also the gate at lifecycle.rs 582-591.

**Sites.** Those named above, plus:
- controller/src/test_support.rs 91-305: `StubAgent` answers the six verbs and keeps its call log.
- controller/tests/observe.rs 12, 160-525 and 1097-1239: the transcript arms move to claude_code.rs's tests.
- effects.rs:146, transient.rs:330 and cli/tests/drive/rig.rs 1729-1739 (`with_seams`).

**Interfaces produced.** The trait, `adapter::open`, `Opening`, `Opened` and the projection's `agent` block. fleet-1jr1e, fleet-14p8.6, fleet-14p8.7 and fleet-14p8.8 consume them, and fleet-x93d.2 removes the mirror fields.

**Acceptance.**

- cli/tests/drive_effects.rs:1824 still writes one `dispatch.failed`.
