title: The agent contract is written down: six verbs, their request and answer types in core, the envelope and exit table, and docs/agent.md
description:
SPEC (fleet-14p8.2, drafted 2026-09-25). Sites at 2a48e90. Blocked by fleet-14p8.1 (the envelope and `answer` it reuses).

**Behaviour.** The agent contract exists as fleet's own types and as a page. Nothing calls it yet: fleet-14p8.3 moves the trait onto it and fleet-14p8.6 speaks it to a process.

- **Types.** `core/src/agent/mod.rs` and `core/src/agent/types.rs` (new). Reviewer call 2026-09-25 (E10): types in core; trait and conformance in the controller. `CONTRACT_VERSION: u64 = 1`. Types derive Serialize, Deserialize and JsonSchema (store/types.rs 640-656); later request fields are optional, later response fields defaulted.
- **Envelope.** `adapter::exec::envelope(fields, root, 1)`: `schema_version` and `root`, where `root` is the directory of the fleet's own `fleet.toml`. Answers carry `schema_version: 1` and are read through `adapter::exec::answer`.
- **Exit table.** The store's four rows (docs/store.md 89-101):
  - 0: answered.
  - 1: refused, `{"refused":{"reason","message"}}`. The reasons are `unsupported` (a posture or model this agent will not take) and `missing` (a `resume` of a session it does not have).
  - 2: usage — an unknown verb, a bad request, another schema_version, or `context` when it is not declared.
  - 3: could not tell, `{"error"}`. Any other code, or a signal, also reads as 3.
- **Bound.** 20 s per call. This is `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT` (claude_code.rs:66), overridable by `FLEET_AGENT_TIMEOUT_MS` as 376-384 read it.
- **Verbs.** `config_dir` is optional wherever it appears: a named seat has none (sessions.rs 52-60).
  - `capabilities` → `{postures: [Posture], default_model, first_turn /* holds {seat} */, context: bool, measured: [String], posture_models: {Posture: [model prefix]} /* default empty: no gate */}`.
    - `Posture` is `ask | auto | unattended`. Ruled 2026-09-25 (ruling 14): three words.
    - `posture_models` is the D3 gate, moved out of policy.rs 51-55 (E9).
    - `validate()` demands non-empty `postures` and `measured`, and a non-blank `first_turn`.
  - `version` → `{name, version: Option<String>}`. Null means no binary is installed.
  - `launch` takes `{seat, worktree, name, model, posture, first_turn, config_dir?, env: {String:String}, permissions: {commands: [String], touched?: String}}` and answers `{argv: [String], env: {String:String}}`.
    - `permissions` states neutrally what cli/src/transient.rs 647-665 and 715-736 assemble today:
      - `commands`: the project's `[permissions] tool_commands` words, each one command word (`is_command_word` 742-748).
      - `touched`: the builder's checks command.
      The adapter renders them into its own format.
    - Reviewer call 2026-09-25 (E8): launch may write inside `config_dir` and inside the seat's `worktree`, and nowhere else. The transient permission file lands in the worktree today (controller/src/transient.rs:703).
    - The plugin dir is the adapter's own and is never in the request.
    - Ruled 2026-09-25 (ruling 13): launch seeds the trust acceptance for its own `worktree` in the scoped config dir beside the onboarding seed (D8, A15). fleet only launches into worktrees it created.
  - `resume` takes `{session_id, worktree, config_dir?, model, posture}` and answers `{argv, env}`. Reviewer call 2026-09-25 (E3): the argv carries the start's flags with the full session id. fleet-rge6.4 measures that this keeps plugin, model and posture on an interactive session; A9 was measured on background sessions only.
  - `read` takes `{seats: [{seat, session_id?, pid?, config_dir?, worktree, screen?}]}`, where `pid` is the pane's process id from core's host (fleet-rge6.1), the one attribution fleet-rge6.3 keeps, and answers `{seats: [{seat, activity, blocked_on?, evidence, session_id?, cause?}]}`.
    - `activity` is `starting|busy|idle|blocked|unknown`.
    - `blocked_on` is `permission|question|logged_out|usage_limit`.
    - `evidence` is `typed|screen`.
    - `blocked` without `blocked_on` is legal: B8 keys the stop on presence.
  - `context` takes `{seats: […]}` and answers `{seats: [{seat, tokens?, window?, turns?, last_write?}]}`. `last_write` is a Stamp (store types.rs 216). It is asked only where `capabilities.context` is true.
  - `read` and `context` batch every seat, so a poll runs one process per verb.

**Sites.**
- core/src/lib.rs 104-123 (`pub mod agent;`).
- core/src/agent/{mod,types}.rs (new).
- docs/agent.md (new, through the docs skill), headed as docs/store.md 1-121 and 376-430. "Choosing an adapter" is left for fleet-14p8.6 to fill. Its semantics section says:
  - Liveness keys on fleet's record and on `until` timeouts, never on `idle`.
  - Presence is fleet's (tmux), and activity is the adapter's.
- docs/README.md: an index line.
- Arms in types.rs (as store/types.rs 945+): every docs/agent.md example round-trips.

**Interfaces produced.** `fleet_core::agent::types::{CONTRACT_VERSION, Posture, Capabilities, Version, Launch, Permissions, Resume, Argv, SeatRef, Activity, BlockedOn, Evidence, SeatContext, Refusal}`. fleet-14p8.3–fleet-14p8.8 consume them, and fleet-jymr.1 through fleet-14p8.5. fleet-jymr.5 renders `Permissions`.

**Acceptance.**
- `cargo nextest run -p fleet-core agent::` passes, and each doc example round-trips.
- `activity: "napping"` fails to decode, naming the field.
- `capabilities` with no `postures` fails `validate`.
- A request with an unknown extra key decodes (requests stay open).
- A launch request with no `config_dir` decodes.
- `git grep -n -i claude -- core/src/agent docs/agent.md` finds only prose marked as one adapter's example.

**Reviewer call 2026-09-25.** `root` means exactly what the store contract's `root` means (docs/store.md 68-87: the absolute project root), so one envelope serves both contracts.

title: One copy of the adapter call machinery serves the store and the agent: spawn, bound, group kill, exit table and stderr's last line live in adapter::exec
description:
SPEC (fleet-14p8.1, drafted 2026-09-25). Sites at 2a48e90. Blocked by fleet-wpf0 (flight 8: the other session is editing core/src/store/exec.rs and core/tests; ruling 12 — this row starts only after flight 8's last child lands).

**Behaviour.** The half of `store::exec` that knows nothing about stores moves into `core/src/adapter/exec.rs`, and `store::exec::Exec` calls it. Nothing an adapter or a person sees changes: every refusal the store prints today prints word for word after.

- **Moves.** From core/src/store/exec.rs `Exec::call` 106-167: building the request bytes, `Command::new(adapter).arg(verb)`, `run_bounded_fed` (the bound and the process-group kill are already core/src/process.rs 192-214, and stay there), the deadline test against `deadline_cause` 122, and the exit reading 135-164 as a typed answer: `Exited::{Answered(stdout), Refused(stdout), Usage, CouldNotTell(error: Option<String>), OffTable(i32), Signalled}`. `carrying_stderr` 205-222 becomes `adapter::exec::carrying(text, &Ran) -> String` over plain text. From core/src/store/mod.rs: `tail` 580-594 and `first_value` 600-603 (both re-exported from `store` under their names, so bd/mod.rs:27, bd_cli.rs:62, conformance.rs:1515, test_support.rs:212 and item/land.rs are untouched). From types.rs: `request` 905-918 and `answer` 924-942 become `adapter::exec::envelope(fields, root, version)` and `adapter::exec::answer::<T>(text, version)`, with `CONTRACT_VERSION` 35 passed in, so each contract states its own version; `store::types::{request, answer}` stay as one-line wrappers.
- **Stays store-side.** `WRITES` 47-57 and `UNTOLD` 62-63 (a write whose effect cannot be told is a store idea), `on_the_record` 174-201 (the store's refusal reasons), and every trait method 232-411. `Exec::call` becomes: `exec::run(...)` → map `Exited` to `StoreError` exactly as 135-164 do today.
- **The words.** The sentences at 123-125, 137, 141-143, 145-148, 152-155, 157-160 and 161-163 are the store's today and name "the store contract". The shared function returns the typed answer and the caller words it, so the store keeps these sentences and fleet-14p8.6 words the agent's own ("the agent contract").

**Sites.** core/src/lib.rs (a `pub mod adapter;` beside `store` at 122); core/src/adapter/mod.rs and exec.rs (new); core/src/store/exec.rs 24-43, 106-167, 205-222; core/src/store/mod.rs 580-603; core/src/store/types.rs 903-942. Tests: exec.rs arms `an_exit_1_is_refused_by_its_reason` 579, `exits_2_3_and_one_off_the_table_are_unreadable_by_their_row` 625, `an_answer_at_no_schema_version_or_another_is_unreadable` 668, `a_call_that_outruns_its_bound_is_killed_and_unreadable` 691 and `the_adapters_stderr_is_carried_into_the_refusal` 738 keep their store-level assertions; the `Stub` rig 446-512 moves to adapter/exec.rs's tests and gains verb-agnostic arms (any verb, any answer object) that the store arms then reuse through a `pub(crate)` path.

**Interfaces produced.** `fleet_core::adapter::exec::{run, Ran, Exited, Unrun, envelope, answer, tail, first_value, carrying}`:
`pub fn run(adapter: &Path, verb: &str, request: &serde_json::Value, timeout: Duration) -> Result<Ran, Unrun>` where `Unrun::{CouldNotRun(String), Deadline(String)}` and `Ran { exited: Exited, stdout: String, said: String, stderr_blank: bool }`. fleet-14p8.6 (the agent's Exec), fleet-14p8.7 (the stub's answers decode through `answer`) and fleet-14p8.8 consume them.

**Acceptance.**
- `cargo nextest run -p fleet-core` passes with the store arms byte-identical in their asserted texts. A grep of the diff for changed string literals in exec.rs finds none.
- `git grep -n 'run_bounded_fed' -- core/src/store` finds nothing. The store reaches the process only through `adapter::exec::run`.
- New arms in core/src/adapter/exec.rs: a verb named `read` with an answer object of unknown shape comes back `Answered` with stdout whole; exits 1, 2, 3, 7 and a signal each map to their `Exited` row; a 200 ms bound kills a `sleep 5` stub's whole group (the pid file's process is gone, as arm 691 checks); `answer::<T>(text, 2)` refuses a `schema_version: 1` answer, naming both numbers.
- `fleet store check --adapter <stub>` output is unchanged (cli/tests/store_check.rs passes untouched).

**Reviewer call 2026-09-25.** `tail` and `first_value` move physically into adapter/exec.rs with `store::` re-exporting them, as assumed: the adapter module never depends on `store`. If fleet-wpf0.7's stub lands first, its arms join the unchanged list.

title: A controller refuses to start over seats the Claude Code daemon still hosts, doctor checks tmux, and the docs describe the tmux model
description:
SPEC (fleet-rge6.6, drafted 2026-09-25, revised 2026-09-25). Sites at 2a48e90. Blocked by fleet-rge6.2–fleet-2u3.13. The docs describe all five, and the refusal relies on fleet-rge6.4 keeping short ids inside the adapter.

**Behaviour.**

- **The upgrade refusal (ruling 10).** There is no adoption code.
  - **When it runs.** Before the first tick, the controller reads the listing under the fleet's config dir and under every config dir the session table records. That is the same set the poll reads (run.rs:538-557).
  - **What it refuses.** It refuses to start when any row standing in a configured seat's worktree is daemon-hosted. The test is the one B10 measured: an interactive row never carries a short id `id`, and a background row always does (A6).
  - **Where the check lives.** Reviewer call 2026-09-25 (E6): the check is `ClaudeCode::daemon_hosted(&self, config_dir) -> Result<Vec<Hosted>, String>`. It parses the listing through the adapter's own private row type. It sits on the concrete type, not on `Agent`, because the v1 contract carries no daemon verb (ruling 1). fleet-x93d.2 deletes it along with claude_code.rs.
  - **Who calls it.** `observe_clocked` calls it after `Wiring::resolve` (run.rs:90-103), where the concrete `ClaudeCode` is held (111). `fleet start` calls it too, as a fourth refusal beside the three (cli/src/lifecycle.rs:573-591), so the person meets it at the terminal rather than in the service's log.
  - **Exit and message.** The exit is `EXIT_DAEMON_HOSTED = 1`, a new constant beside `EXIT_NO_POLICY` (run.rs:21-23). The message has one line per seat: "`<machine name>` is hosted by the Claude Code daemon: session <id>, short id <x>, in <worktree>". The remedy follows: stop each with `claude stop <x>` under its config dir, then start again.
  - **Unreadable listing.** A listing that cannot be read is said once and the start proceeds. Every live seat then reads Unknown, and nothing is spawned over it.
- **Doctor and the dependency.**
  - **The check.** `core/defaults/doctor/tmux-version/{doctor.toml, run.sh}` is new and embedded by core/build.rs. It is built on shell builtins, like `claude-code-version/run.sh`, and `FLEET_TMUX_BIN` names the binary.
  - **Holds.** It holds when `tmux -V` reports a version at or above `MINIMUM=3.7b`. It reports whether a server is running on socket `fleet`, and with how many sessions; either state passes.
  - **Broken.** It is broken when tmux is absent (the install line is `brew install tmux` on macOS, or the distribution's `tmux` package) or older than the minimum.
  - **The minimum.** It is `fleet_core::supported::MINIMUM_TMUX = "3.7b"`, in core/src/supported.rs beside `PINNED_CLAUDE_CODE` (35). An arm modelled on core/tests/pack.rs:953-972 holds the script's copy to that constant.
  - **Default-check lists.** They grow to seven (cli/tests/doctor.rs:39-46; core/tests/doctor.rs:93-101).
  - **fleet start.** It also refuses when no tmux resolves, beside the agent-binary refusal (lifecycle.rs:582-591).
- **The docs pass.** It goes through the docs skill, with every claim verified and the citations in a review note on the bead.
  - docs/seats.md:
    - "What the controller does each poll" (370-434): presence from tmux, activity from the listing, Unknown on disagreement, a start believed on its row, and stopped as an ended pane.
    - "Tuning the controller" (477-517): the `stopped_recency_hours` and `nudge_model` rows go, and `nudge_timeout_seconds` is restated.
    - "Nudging a seat" (605-634): a paste; a blocked seat refused; the outcomes sent, queued and failed.
    - "Feeding a transient seat" (695-711) and "Retiring a transient seat" (713-757).
    - A new "Attaching to a seat" section (fleet-2u3.13 = fleet-2u3.13).
    - "When it refuses" (759-801).
  - docs/getting-started.md:
    - "What fleet runs on" (62-82): tmux, with 3.7b as the minimum, and the `tmux-version` check. Windows is unsupported; the controller already refuses to compile there (controller/src/platform/mod.rs:57-58).
    - "Running a doctor check" (83-133).
    - "The sessions the controller starts" (381-392): each seat is a tmux session on socket `fleet`, named by its seat id, under a config dir seeded with onboarding and trust (ruling 13).
    - "When it refuses" (394-416).
  - docs/status.md, "The roster" (120-142): the Unknown cause, the exit status and end time of a stopped seat, and `session.ended`.
  - controller/README.md: its eight daemon mentions.

**Lessons (Ruled 2026-09-25, ruling 15).** This row lands the split's brain/ half. Two things go into brain/lessons/claude-code.md:
- The retired entries, each marked with the bead that retired it: A2, A3, A4, A10 (fleet-rge6.3); A6, A7, A8 (fleet-rge6.4); A14, D2 (fleet-rge6.2); B9 (fleet-rge6.5). This row verifies those markings and the Test inventory.
- The one-line pointer to the pack's lessons file, once fleet-jymr.6 has moved the kept entries.

**Sites.**
- controller/src/adapter/claude_code.rs (the predicate)
- run.rs 21-23, 90-111
- cli/src/lifecycle.rs 569-591
- core/src/supported.rs
- core/defaults/doctor/tmux-version/ (new)
- cli/tests/doctor.rs, core/tests/doctor.rs, core/tests/pack.rs
- docs/seats.md, docs/getting-started.md, docs/status.md
- controller/README.md
- brain/lessons/claude-code.md (the markings)

**Interfaces consumed:** fleet-rge6.1–fleet-2u3.13. **Produced:** `MINIMUM_TMUX`, the `tmux-version` check and `EXIT_DAEMON_HOSTED`.

**Acceptance.**
- Over StubAgent, a listing with an `id`-carrying row in a seat worktree makes observe exit 1, name the seat and short id, and make no host call. A listing of interactive rows only lets observe start.
- A cli arm with a stub claude listing a background row: `fleet start` refuses with the same lines before anything loads.
- Doctor arms: `fleet-tmux-stub` answering `tmux 3.7b` holds; a stub answering `tmux 3.4` is broken and names the minimum; an absent tmux is broken and names the install line. `fleet doctor` runs seven defaults.
- `git grep -n -i -E 'daemon|--bg|hibernat|nudge_model|stopped_recency|print-mode' -- docs/` finds only the refusal's paragraph.

**Reviewer calls 2026-09-25.** (1) The exit is 1, `EXIT_DAEMON_HOSTED`, as drafted. (2) An unreadable listing at startup is said once and the start proceeds, as drafted: every live seat then reads Unknown and nothing is spawned over it, while refusing would leave a fleet whose agent listing breaks unable to start at all. (3) The version compare reads a trailing letter as a patch level (3.7b > 3.7a > 3.7) and holds a build with no release number (`next-3.8`, `master`) with a note. (4) 3.7b, the one version measured, is the floor until another is measured.

title: A nudge and a feed are pasted into the seat's pane and believed only when the listing turns busy, a blocked seat is refused before any byte, and nudge_model is gone
description:
SPEC (fleet-rge6.5, drafted 2026-09-25, revised 2026-09-25). Sites at 2a48e90. Blocked by fleet-rge6.2, which threads the host through the loop, the verbs and the cli. This row CLOSES fleet-nrl and fleet-fmver (E17).

**First step, a measurement (E14).** D8's submit was measured on 2.1.282. On 2.1.280, under a scratch config dir and socket, record five things:
1. A bracketed paste of a two-line text, followed by a separate `C-m`, submits as ONE turn and the row reads `busy`, including how long that takes.
2. A paste plus submit into a session that is already busy queues, or drops.
3. What happens to a paste sent while a permission dialog is up.

**Behaviour.** A turn for a live seat is pasted into its pane. No relay turn runs and no model is spent.
- One core path, `effect::type_turn(agent, host, target: &TurnTarget {seat, config_dir}, text, bound) -> Typed`, serves four callers: the controller's suggest-rest nudge (effect.rs:538-588), `fleet seat nudge` through `SeatRing::ring_with` (cli/src/item.rs:1275-1371), a routine's nudge (controller/src/routines/action.rs:241-268) and `fleet seat feed` (controller/src/transient.rs:1218-1226). It runs in order:
  1. Read the pane (`host.list`) and the pid-attributed row (`agent.status` under the seat's config dir, fleet-rge6.3) FRESH. A dead pane or no row is `Absent`, and nothing is sent.
  2. A row with `waitingFor`, or with `status: waiting`, is `Blocked(cause)` and is refused BEFORE ANY BYTE. The precedent is herdr `src/app/api/agents.rs:146-161` at 8d95e9b, cited from the adapters-and-sessions note. Keys sent at a dialog answer it (B8, B10).
  3. `host.send(text)`: a paste, then `SUBMIT_GAP`, then `C-m` (fleet-rge6.1, E4).
  4. If the row was idle, poll every 250 ms for `status: busy` on the same pid, up to `bound`. Busy is `Delivered`; anything else is `Failed("typed and not taken: still <status> after Ns")`. If the row was already busy, the send is `Queued` and is never called delivered (reviewer call 2026-09-25, E5).
- These go: `Agent::nudge` (adapter/mod.rs:114-125), `ClaudeCode::nudge` (claude_code.rs:542-582), `NUDGES_DIR` and `nudge_log_path` (258-261, 691-693), and `effect::nudge_prompt` (174-187). `nudge_text` (157-172) stays and is the text that gets typed.
- `nudge_model` goes (ruling 7):
  - `DEFAULT_NUDGE_MODEL` (policy.rs:62-64), `Policy.nudge_model` (105), `RawController.nudge_model` (181-182), the parse (294-297), `CONTROLLER_KEYS` (461-476, 14 → 13) and `overlaid` (511);
  - the test `every_effect_key_is_read_from_the_file` loses lines 579 and 595 only. Its posture lines 575-576 and 591-592 are fleet-1jr1e's to fix under ruling 14 (Ruled 2026-09-25), so the two rows do not collide;
  - controller/fleet.example.toml:44, controller/src/lifecycle.rs:845, and docs/seats.md:494, 505, 615 and 705.

  A fleet.toml that still carries the key parses. A `config.json` override naming it is reported once by `Overrides::ignored` (policy.rs:403-415). `nudge_timeout_seconds` stays as `bound`, and its default (33-34) drops from 90 to 10 s, set by the measurement.
- Outcomes:
  - `session.nudged` records `sent` only when the send is witnessed, else `queued: the seat was mid-turn`, `refused: blocked on <cause>`, or `failed: <why>`.
  - `fleet seat nudge` (cli/src/nudge.rs:84-104) exits 0 on sent or queued, 1 on refused or failed, and 4 on Absent. The published-row check (80-82) stays.
  - Feed already refuses a busy seat (controller/src/transient.rs:1191-1198). It believes only `Delivered`, and any other outcome puts the marker back (1246-1270).
  - The controller's nudge marks the session whatever the outcome (571-572).

**The folds (E17).**
- **fleet-nrl.** Feed pastes the brief into the seat's own pane, so the session receives it. The bead's "arm on the argv" becomes an arm on FakeHost's sends: one paste of the brief, then one submit, to `session_for(seat)`.
- **fleet-fmver, defect 1** (addressing). The address is the seat's tmux session, which fleet names. No name the agent registered is used. The `chosen_name` half was already gone at HEAD (config.rs:417-423; cli/src/item.rs:1323-1329).
- **fleet-fmver, defect 2** ("sent" on a failed send). There is no print turn left to misread. AC2 becomes this arm: a paste whose row never turns busy writes `failed`, and a mutant that believes `host.send`'s `Ok` turns it red.

**Lessons (Ruled 2026-09-25, ruling 15).** This row retires B9: resuming a running background session, and the print-mode relay nudge it justified. It is marked `Retired by <this bead> (fleet-rge6.5)`, and `a_live_session_is_reached_without_a_resume` (effects.rs:1053) is retired. D8's submit half is kept for the pack and restated from the measurement.

**Sites.**
- controller/src/effect.rs 157-187, 538-588
- adapter/mod.rs 114-125
- claude_code.rs 258-261, 542-582, 684-693
- routines/action.rs 241-268
- controller/src/transient.rs 1164-1278
- cli/src/item.rs 1243-1371
- cli/src/nudge.rs 84-131
- policy.rs, as above, and 567-596
- controller/src/lifecycle.rs:845
- test_support.rs 98, 141, 257-268

**Interfaces produced.** `effect::type_turn`, `TurnTarget`, and `Typed { Delivered, Queued, Blocked(String), Absent, Failed(String) }`. fleet-rge6.6 documents them.

**Acceptance.**
- The measurement is recorded on the bead.
- A nudge makes no launch or resume call, and exactly one paste plus one submit.
- There is one arm per outcome: blocked (zero sends), idle to busy (sent), idle and staying idle (failed), and busy before the send (queued).
- `a_nudge_marks_its_session_and_states_what_it_carried` (1491) passes.
- The nrl feed arm passes, and a cli nudge arm over `fleet-tmux-stub` passes.
- `git grep -n -E 'nudge_model|nudge_prompt|claude-haiku|NUDGES_DIR' -- controller cli core docs` finds nothing.

**Reviewer call 2026-09-25.** fleet-fmver's docs-pass note st#18 (`fleet status --seat Orla` failing where the name is stored lowercased) is not this row's: the builder runs it once at HEAD through the seat list's resolver (cli/src/status.rs:708-720) and records the answer on the bead; if it still fails, the reviewer files it as its own bug, and fleet-fmver closes with this row either way.

title: Stop, revive and remove act on the seat's tmux session, revive is a new session resuming the full id with the start's flags, and short ids stay inside the adapter
description:
SPEC (fleet-rge6.4, drafted 2026-09-25, revised 2026-09-25). Sites at 2a48e90. Blocked by fleet-rge6.2 (the launch and the watch that revive reuses) and fleet-rge6.3 (Stopped means a dead pane). **First step, a measurement.** Reviewer call 2026-09-25 (E3): A9 was measured on background sessions only. Do this on Claude Code 2.1.280 and tmux 3.7b, under a scratch config dir and socket. 1. Start an interactive session with `--plugin-dir`, `--model` and `--permission-mode`. 2. Take a turn, then kill it. 3. Start a new session whose command is `claude --resume ` with the same three flags. 4. Record whether the listing shows the SAME `sessionId`, whether the plugin's hook fires, and what model and posture come up. 5. Record, in the same run, what one `C-c` does to an idle session and to a busy one. If the flagged resume forks, revive becomes a fresh spawn (a SpawnWoken outcome), and the bead says so. **Behaviour.** A session is addressed by its seat, `session_for(seat)` on socket `fleet`, and never by an address the agent issued. - **Stop.** `effect::stop_session(host, name)` is new, in core, and agent-neutral: 1. `host.keys(["C-c"])`; 2. wait up to `STOP_GRACE` (5 s) for the pane to read Dead or the session to be gone; 3. `host.kill`. It returns `Ok` only when a following `host.list` names no session for the seat. The witness is the host, not the act's return (the rule A6 and A7 taught). D8 measured `kill-session` ending the session. - **Revive.** Reviewer call (E2, E3): a revive is a new session whose command is the resume argv. - A dead pane has no listed row (B10), so the session id comes from the table (`newest_sighted_for`, sessions.rs:345). - A new trait verb, `Agent::resume(&self, session_id, spec: &StartSpec) -> Result`, is answered by `ClaudeCode::resume` with `[, --resume, , --model, , --permission-mode,

, (--plugin-dir )?]`, using `launch`'s env. - `effect::revive` (effect.rs:351-419) kills the dead session, then runs `host.new_session` under fleet-rge6.2's watch. - Started means the pane's pid carries the resumed `sessionId`. A different id is a fork: the revive is Failed and the session killed. - `session.revived` drops `address` (388). - **Rest** (294-349) becomes `stop_session` followed by `start_once`. There is no removal, because no daemon row is left. `Rested::NoAddress` (201-203; run.rs:1328-1335) goes, and so do the payload's `predecessor_address` and `removed` (328-332, 343-345). - **Remove.** The retire is controller/src/transient.rs:1348-1572. - It stops by seat, replacing `agent.stop(short_id)` (1384-1436). - `cleared` (1770-1783) reads `host.list` until the session is gone. - `agent.remove` and its answer (1438-1454) go. The worktree removal was always fleet's own `git worktree remove --force` (1456-1482). - `verify_from_outside` (1791-1857) gains a host probe, and its pid probe reads the pane pid taken before the stop (1382). - The `removal` key reads `"killed "`. - **Short ids stay inside the adapter** (reviewer call, E6). Removed: - `AgentRow.id` (adapter/mod.rs:173-177); - `Agent::stop`, `remove` and `revive` (88-105), and `RemoveAnswer` (60-72); - `ClaudeCode::stop`, `revive`, `remove` and `answered`, and `worktree_path_in` (494-504, 530-540, 655-682, 782-794); - `SeatObservation.short_id` (observe.rs:105-109, 349, 372); - `Target.short_id` (effect.rs:96-98; run.rs:1428; controller/src/transient.rs:772); - `SessionRow.short_id` and `Table::sight`'s parameter (sessions.rs:79-83, 380-415, 442, 546-557). Old rows still read, because the key is ignored. - adopt's copy of it (effect.rs:477-479, 492); - StubAgent's `STOP`, `REMOVE` and `REVIVE` (test_support.rs:136-139, 237-250). The only short-id reader left is fleet-rge6.6's private listing parse, in claude_code.rs. The seat's own `-` (docs/seats.md:24) is a different thing. **Lessons (Ruled 2026-09-25, ruling 15).** This row retires A6, A7 and A8, the daemon's address, attach and removal. Each is marked `Retired by (fleet-rge6.4)`. Their tests are retired: `stop_takes_the_short_id` (effects.rs:480), `attach_exit_is_not_a_witness` (954), `a_removal_that_printed_a_path_is_told_from_one_that_did_not` (1372) and `remove_answers_three_ways` (controller/tests/transient.rs:2677). A9 is kept for the pack and restated from the measurement above. **Sites.** - controller/src/adapter/mod.rs 60-105, 165-201 - claude_code.rs 494-540, 655-682, 782-794 - effect.rs 58-108, 189-204, 294-419, 455-505 - run.rs 1291-1336, 1389-1431 - controller/src/transient.rs 1343-1572, 1765-1857 - observe.rs - sessions.rs - test_support.rs **Interfaces produced.** `effect::stop_session(host, name) -> Result<(), String>`, `Agent::resume`, and `effect::revive(agent, host, policy, target, events_log, table, now_ms)`. fleet-rge6.6 documents them. fleet-14p8.3 rebuilds `resume` onto the contract. **Acceptance.** - The measurement is recorded on the bead. - `lessons::resume_continues_only_a_flagless_full_id` (effects.rs:996) is renamed to `a_resume_by_full_id_keeps_the_session`, and asserts the argv above and a Failed and killed fork. - A stop whose `C-c` leaves the pane alive is killed after the grace. - A rest writes no `removed` key. - A retire on FakeHost leaves no session, no worktree and no rows, and a surviving session fails its host probe. - `git grep -n -E 'short_id|RemoveAnswer|\["(stop|rm|attach)", ' -- controller/src cli/src` finds nothing outside claude_code.rs's private parse. **Open for the reviewer.** None; the measurement settles the fork question.

title: A seat's presence is read from tmux and its activity from the listing, a disagreement is Unknown with both evidences, and the daemon's windows are gone
description:
SPEC (fleet-rge6.3, drafted 2026-09-25, revised 2026-09-25). Sites at 2a48e90. Blocked by fleet-rge6.1 (`Host::list`). It also needs the host threaded through `Seams` and `Wiring`; fleet-rge6.2 describes that threading, and whichever of the two rows lands first does it.

**First step, a measurement (E14).** B10 was measured on 2.1.282. On 2.1.280, record an interactive listing at idle, busy and waiting, a `waitingFor` at a dialog, the row's `pid` against `pane_pid`, and the row gone after `kill-session`. The recording becomes the B10 fixture.

**Behaviour.** Presence is core's and comes from tmux. Activity is the listing's (ruling 3). Liveness never keys on the idle word.
- Each poll makes one `host.list()` on socket `fleet` (E1), beside `Rosters::gather` (observe.rs:142-211). That keeps one listing per distinct config dir (A11, B10).
- `observe_seat` (observe.rs:220-332) decides a seat from its pane (`session_for(&seat.id)`) and its listing:
  - host Unreadable → **Unknown**, with the host's cause;
  - no session, and no live row in the seat's worktrees → **Absent**;
  - no session, but a live row in a seat worktree → **Unknown**: "no tmux session <name> on fleet; the listing names session <id>, pid <n>, in <worktree>". A session fleet does not host is not the seat's (B5).
  - pane Dead → **Stopped**, with the exit status;
  - pane Alive, listing Unreadable → **Unknown**, naming both;
  - pane Alive, and a row whose `pid` is the pane's → **PromptBlocked** when `waitingFor` is present (B8, B10), else **Present**, with `status` carried as the activity;
  - pane Alive, no such row, and the session younger than `STARTING_GRACE_MS` (17, kept) → **Starting**;
  - older than that → **Unknown**: "tmux holds pid <n> alive for <seat>; the listing names no row with that pid".
- Rows are attributed by pid. The cwd match (239-251) and the two-live-rows Unknown (253-277) go. `RosterState`'s six strings (69-81) stay.
- **End time (ruling 3).** The first poll that reads a pane Dead appends `session.ended {session, status, at: now, source: "observed"}`, latched per session id on the table. A dead pane met at startup takes `at` from `agent.ended_at`, the transcript's mtime (C4), with `source: "transcript"`, or null. `events::SESSION_ENDED` joins `CONTROLLER_TYPES` (events.rs:184). `SeatRow` gains `exit_status` and `ended_at`, which are provider-neutral. `roster_recency_fallback` goes (projection.rs:196-202, 234, 392). Reviewer call 2026-09-25 (E13): the neutral `agent` block is fleet-14p8.3's.
- **Deleted: the stopped-row window.**
  - `Recency`, `FELL_BACK_TO_START`, `recency_fallback`, `pidless_row` and `state_names_an_end` (observe.rs:19-49, 100-126, 288-331).
  - cli/src/routines.rs:209-219.
  - `stopped_recency_hours` (policy.rs:12-15, 106-109, 161-162, 243-247, 298, 463, 512).
  - `AgentRow`'s `is_starting`, `marked_done`, `names_an_end` and `DONE`/`STOPPED`/`FAILED` (adapter/mod.rs:208-253).
- **Deleted: the daemon read.**
  - `Agent::daemon`, `DaemonRead` and `DaemonStatus` (adapter/mod.rs:107-112, 286-326).
  - `ClaudeCode::daemon`, `duration_token_ms` and `parse_daemon_status` (claude_code.rs:506-528, 816-851).
  - `Table.daemon_pid` (sessions.rs:128-131, 143, 248-256, 502-505). An old table still reads, because serde ignores the key.
  - run.rs:569-587.
- **Deleted: the replacement window (A10), and with it the re-host hold and arm 5b, both answers to daemon behaviour.**
  - decide.rs 4b and 4c (192-214), and 298-431.
  - `SeatInput`'s five hold fields (102-134).
  - `adopted_and_listed` (86-96, 227-243; run.rs:846-858).
  - The Observer's `held`, `live_seen` and `pidless_since` (run.rs:275-298, 706-743, 862-886).

  A dead pane is an end: hibernation (A3) and a re-host (A10) cannot happen to a session tmux holds.
- `FleetShape::describe` (decide.rs:500-510) is reworded: every seat Absent at once is the tmux server gone. `adopt` (effect.rs:455-505) still claims a live row by session id.
- `fleet status` prints `unknown — <cause>` on the seat's line (cli/src/status.rs:472-491 prints none today).

**Lessons (Ruled 2026-09-25, ruling 15).** This row retires A2, A3, A4 and A10, the `--bg` lifecycle and the daemon. Each is marked `Retired by <this bead> (fleet-rge6.3)` in brain/lessons/claude-code.md. Their tests are retired: `pid_null_is_two_states` (controller/tests/observe.rs:321), `hibernation_reads_as_a_deliberate_stop` (effects.rs:340) and `a_newer_client_replaces_the_daemon_and_rehosts` (effects.rs:900); A4's test was never written. B8, B10 and C4 are kept for the pack.

**Sites.**
- controller/src/observe.rs
- decide.rs 56-135, 186-243, 298-431, 487-538
- run.rs 234-303, 390-398, 538-752, 821-891
- adapter/mod.rs 1-7, 107-112, 169-259, 274-326
- claude_code.rs 3-6, 506-528, 816-851
- sessions.rs
- projection.rs 185-240, 300-400
- events.rs 128-190
- policy.rs, as above
- cli/src/routines.rs 184-229
- cli/src/status.rs 472-491
- test_support.rs 91-120, 140, 252-255
- controller/tests/rehost.rs (deleted), decide.rs, adoption.rs 497-791

**Interfaces produced.**
- `observe::observe_seat(read: &RosterRead, host: &HostRead, seat, now_ms) -> SeatObservation`, carrying `exit_status` and the pane pid
- `events::SESSION_ENDED`

fleet-rge6.4 consumes Stopped. fleet-rge6.5 consumes the pid-attributed row. fleet-rge6.6 documents them.

**Acceptance.**
- controller/tests/observe.rs has one arm per case above, over FakeHost and the recorded listing.
- `lessons::an_interactive_row_is_listed_without_an_address` (B10) is new.
- `waiting_for_names_the_block` (281) passes on an interactive row.
- A pane dying between two ticks writes one `session.ended`.
- The adoption arms are rewritten onto a dead pane.
- `git grep -n -i daemon -- controller/src cli/src` finds only prose about the agent's listing, plus fleet-rge6.6's refusal.

**Reviewer calls 2026-09-25.** (1) A live pane with an unreadable listing reads Unknown, never Present: nothing is spawned or revived on it, as today. (2) After a tmux server loss a seat is Absent; a named seat whose table row still holds a session id whose transcript exists (C4) is revived through fleet-rge6.4's resume, so a reboot does not throw away a role's conversation; with no id or no transcript it is spawned fresh. This reads the table, not the daemon's listing, so it is not the stopped-row window back.

title: A seat's session starts interactively as its own tmux session under a config dir seeded with onboarding and trust, and a start is believed only when the listing shows its row
description:
SPEC (fleet-rge6.2, drafted 2026-09-25, revised 2026-09-25). Sites at 2a48e90. Blocked by fleet-rge6.1 (the host).

**Ruled 2026-09-25 (ruling 13):** fleet seeds the trust acceptance for a seat's own worktree, and it measures first.

**First step, a measurement.** On Claude Code 2.1.280, tmux 3.7b, a scratch config dir and a scratch socket, record the key and the command in the bead. Per E14, B10 and D8 were measured on 2.1.282, so this step re-measures on the pin.
1. An interactive start under a `.claude.json` seeded with the four onboarding keys (D8) and `projects["<worktree>"].hasTrustDialogAccepted = true` (the candidate key) comes up with no theme picker, no login menu and no A15 dialog.
2. The row is listed with `status` and no `id` (B10).
3. `--name` is accepted, and a positional first turn submits.
4. The listing's `pid` equals `pane_pid`.
5. The time from `new-session` to the row being listed is recorded, to size `start_watch_seconds` (default 5 s, sized for A14's 0.01 s exit).

If the seeded trust does not hold, the fallback is answering the dialog from the captured screen: the start sees A15's text, sends `Down` then `C-m` (D8), and records that it did. fleet only ever trusts worktrees it created: a spawned seat's worktree under `worktrees_dir`, never a named seat's configured one. If the positional turn does not submit, the first turn is `host.send` once the row reads idle.

**Behaviour.** The adapter answers what to run, and core runs it (ruling 2).
- `Agent::start` (adapter/mod.rs:74-77) becomes `fn launch(&self, spec: &StartSpec) -> Result<Launch, String>`, with `Launch { argv: Vec<String>, env: Vec<(String, String)> }`.
- `ClaudeCode::launch` replaces `start` (claude_code.rs:425-492).
  - The argv is `[<effect bin>, --name, <name>, --model, <model>, --permission-mode, <posture>, (--plugin-dir <dir>)?, <first turn>]`, which is today's minus `--bg` (A5, D3, D5).
  - The posture is passed as the policy's word, unchanged. Ruled 2026-09-25 (ruling 14): fleet's three words `ask`, `auto` and `unattended` are fleet-1jr1e's.
  - The env is `with_environment`'s pairs (179-201), lifted into `fn environment(&self, config_dir) -> Vec<(String, String)>`, which the Command builders (211-237) also use, plus `FLEET_ACTOR` (449-452).
- The seed runs when `spec.config_dir` is Some. `launch` writes the following into `<config_dir>/.claude.json`, merged into any `.claude.json` the overlay already put there:
  - `hasCompletedOnboarding`, `lastOnboardingVersion`, `theme` and `oauthAccount`, copied from the operator's `.claude.json`. That file is `<configured dir>/.claude.json` when `credential_dir` (27-36) is non-empty, else `<home>/.claude.json`. A missing key is `Err` naming it.
  - The measured trust entry for `spec.worktree`.

  The write lands after `make_config_dir`'s read-back (controller/src/transient.rs:891-918). Named seats (config_dir None) get no seed.
- `effect::start_once` (effect.rs:234-292) takes `host: &dyn Host`. It calls `launch`, then `host.new_session(session_for(seat), worktree, argv, env)`. Then, every 250 ms until `start_watch_seconds`, it checks the pane and the listing:
  - a Dead pane is Failed, carrying the status and the capture;
  - a row whose `pid` is the pane's and which carries `status` (B10) is Started;
  - if neither happens, it captures, kills the session and returns Failed "no listed row within Ns".

  Every Failed kills the session, so a failed spawn's rollback (controller/src/transient.rs:788-800) leaves nothing on the socket. Captures go to `<machine>/starts/<name>-<ms>.log`, because `STARTS_DIR` and the log paths (claude_code.rs:258-261, 684-707) move to core. `session.spawned`'s `output` is `-L fleet -t <session>`.
- These go with `--bg`: `spawned_to_file`, `wait_within`, `sweep_adopted` and `adopted` (57-60, 248-255, 709-780).
- Threading: `Wiring` (run.rs:110-149) resolves `TmuxHost` beside `resolve_effect_bin` (136-142). An unresolved host means effects are off, and the cause is published. `Seams` (187-198) and `transient::Machine` (controller/src/transient.rs:89-109) carry `host`. The cli builds a host beside `effect_agent` (cli/src/transient.rs:550-572, 804-816) and at cli/src/runs.rs:256. If fleet-rge6.3 lands first, it does this threading instead.

**Lessons (Ruled 2026-09-25, ruling 15).** This row retires A14 (a `--bg` start's in-band failure; the pane's exit status replaces it) and D2 (a start's output to a file; the pane holds it). Each is marked `Retired by <this bead> (fleet-rge6.2)` in brain/lessons/claude-code.md, and their tests `a_failed_start_exits_inside_the_watch_window` (effects.rs:528) and `start_output_goes_to_a_file` (805) are retired. `start_names_the_model` (A5) moves onto the argv. D8's `an_interactive_start_under_tmux` and A15's `a_first_run_meets_the_trust_dialog` are kept for the pack.

**Sites.**
- controller/src/adapter/mod.rs 14-58, 74-77
- claude_code.rs 14-61, 179-261, 418-492, 684-780
- effect.rs 110-131, 234-292
- run.rs 105-198
- controller/src/transient.rs 89-109, 735-800
- cli/src/transient.rs 550-572, 804-816
- cli/src/runs.rs:256
- test_support.rs 91-231
- cli/tests/drive_effects.rs and drive_causes.rs, which move onto `fleet-tmux-stub` (fleet-rge6.1)

title: The controller owns a tmux host behind one Host seam on the socket `fleet`, with a fake for the in-process suites and a stub binary for the cli's
description:
SPEC (fleet-rge6.1, drafted 2026-09-25, revised 2026-09-25). Sites at 2a48e90. Blocked by nothing: this is flight 11's first row, and fleet-rge6.2 is its first caller.

**Behaviour.** A module the controller owns, and the only code in the workspace that spells `tmux`. Reviewer call 2026-09-25 (E1): there is one socket per controller, `tmux -L fleet`, because the controller runs per machine and its seats span projects. A seat's session is named by the seat's id.

- `controller/src/host/mod.rs` is new, added as `pub mod host;` beside `pub mod adapter;` (lib.rs:77). It holds `pub const SOCKET: &str = "fleet"` and `pub trait Host`, whose verbs each take a session name:
  - `new_session(name, cwd, argv, env)`. The agent is the pane's own process (E2).
  - `send(name, text)` (E4). The text is loaded as a bracketed paste, fed on stdin through `run_bounded_fed` (core/src/process.rs:209): `load-buffer -b fleet-<name> -`, then `paste-buffer -p -d`. After a pause of `SUBMIT_GAP` (300 ms, herdr's spacing, lessons D8), a separate `send-keys C-m` submits it. A burst of text plus Enter did not submit (D8), and newlines sent as keys would submit a brief's first line on its own.
  - `keys(name, &[&str])`, for named keys.
  - `capture(name) -> Result<String, String>`.
  - `kill(name)`, which answers `Ok` when the session is already gone.
  - `list() -> HostRead`.
  - `attach(name, write) -> Command`. It is built here and never run or bounded here, because the terminal belongs to the person.
  - `version() -> Option<String>`.

  The types are `Pane { session, pid: Option<u32>, state: PaneState, path, created_ms: Option<u64> }`, `PaneState { Alive, Dead { status: Option<i32> } }` and `HostRead { Readable(Vec<Pane>), Unreadable { cause } }`. `session_for(&SeatId)` returns the hyphenated id. That survives a rename and is only `[0-9a-f-]`.
- `controller/src/host/tmux.rs` is new and holds `TmuxHost`.
  - Every call is `tmux -L fleet -f /dev/null …`, so the person's `~/.tmux.conf` never shapes fleet's server.
  - Calls run under the constructed PATH (`platform::child_path`, D1) and are bounded by `platform::run_bounded` (platform/mod.rs:28-31) at 20 s.
  - `new_session` is ONE client invocation: `set-option -g remain-on-exit on \; new-session -d -s <name> -c <cwd> -- /usr/bin/env -i <K=V…> TERM=tmux-256color <argv…>`. Setting remain-on-exit before the pane exists means an argv that exits at once still leaves a dead pane holding its status. There is no shell between tmux and the agent, so the pane dies when the agent does, and its environment is exactly the one handed in.
  - `list` is `list-panes -a -F` over `session_name`, `pane_pid`, `pane_dead`, `pane_dead_status`, `pane_current_path` and `session_created`.
  - A socket with no server behind it (`no server running on …`, `error connecting to …`) reads `Readable(vec![])`: that is the fleet after a reboot. Any other failure is `Unreadable` and carries stderr's last line.
  - The binary is `FLEET_TMUX_BIN` when that names an absolute path, else `tmux` on the constructed PATH. Under `FLEET_TEST_HERMETIC`, an unnamed binary is refused, as `configured_bin` refuses (claude_code.rs:344-355).
- Test seams, reviewer call 2026-09-25 (E7):
  - `FakeHost` goes in controller/src/test_support.rs, beside `StubAgent` (129-304). It records every call as a `Call` (74-83). `sends(name)` returns the pastes and the submits in order. `end(name, status)` leaves a pane dead with that status.
  - For the binary-driven cli suites, there is a test-only `fleet-tmux-stub`, which mirrors `fleet-store-stub`. It lives at `controller/src/bin/tmux_stub.rs`, declared as `[[bin]] name = "fleet-tmux-stub", required-features = ["test-support"]` in controller/Cargo.toml, where there is no `[[bin]]` today and the feature is declared at 17-18. It answers the subcommands above from a JSON state file named by `FLEET_TMUX_STUB_STATE`, prints `tmux 3.7b` for `-V`, and records `attach-session`'s argv. A test-only `fleet-tmux-stub end <name> <status>` kills a pane.
  - controller/tests/common/hermetic.rs adds `FLEET_TMUX_BIN` to its one list, beside `CLAUDE_BIN` at line 31.

**Sites.**
- controller/src/lib.rs:77-95
- controller/src/host/mod.rs and host/tmux.rs (new)
- controller/src/bin/tmux_stub.rs (new)
- controller/Cargo.toml
- controller/src/test_support.rs
- controller/tests/common/hermetic.rs
- controller/tests/host.rs (new)

**Interfaces produced.**
- `fleet_controller::host::{Host, Pane, PaneState, HostRead, SOCKET, session_for, SUBMIT_GAP}`
- `host::tmux::TmuxHost::resolve(child_path) -> Result<TmuxHost, String>`
- `test_support::FakeHost`
- the `fleet-tmux-stub` binary, with the cli/tests/common helper `stub_tmux(dir) -> PathBuf`, which finds it beside `env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_fleet")`

Consumers: fleet-rge6.2 through fleet-rge6.6, and fleet-14p8.7.

**Acceptance.** controller/tests/host.rs holds the real-tmux arm. It is skipped with a printed reason when no tmux resolves, and it runs on a scratch socket `fleet-test-<pid>-<nanos>`, never `fleet`. In order, it:
1. starts `/bin/sh -c 'read x; exit 3'` and lists it Alive with a pid;
2. `send`s `hi` and reads that back through `capture`;
3. lists the pane Dead with status 3;
4. starts `/usr/bin/false` and lists it Dead with status 1;
5. pastes two lines into `cat` and captures both before the submit;
6. runs `kill-server` in a drop guard.

Unit arms cover the list parser: live, dead, dead with no status, and no server. A stub arm drives the same sequence through `fleet-tmux-stub`. `git grep -n -w tmux -- controller/src cli/src core/src` finds only host/, bin/tmux_stub.rs and prose.

**Open for the reviewer.** `pane_dead_status` and bracketed paste into Claude Code are unmeasured on 3.7b. The real arm measures the first. fleet-rge6.5's first step measures the second.

title: Flight 12: the agent contract complete for an external adapter — six verbs over the shared exec, neutral postures, a declared hook mapping, the schema verb, a stub, and fleet agent check
description:
EPIC — flight 12 of the agent side of the adapters design. Rulings and global constraints as on the flight 11 epic (Alberto, 2026-09-25).

**Goal.** An external agent adapter can do everything the in-process Claude Code adapter does after flight 11, and prove it with one command. The contract (docs/agent.md) shares the store's envelope and exit table through one `adapter::exec`; the `Agent` trait is rebuilt on six verbs (`capabilities`, `version`, `launch`, `resume`, `read`, optional `context`); the controller and cli suites run on a test-only `fleet-agent-stub` through Exec with a fake tmux host; `[agent] adapter` resolves a bare name through the installed packs; `fleet guard` applies provider-neutral policy through a hook mapping declared in adapter.toml; posture is fleet's own word. Claude Code is still the built-in after this flight, behind the new trait, and leaves in flight 14.

title: Flight 11: fleet owns the session — seats run interactively in tmux on fleet's own socket, the daemon verbs go, the nudge is typing, and a seat can be attached
description:
EPIC — flight 11, the first flight of the agent side of the adapters design (fleet-notes/adapters-and-sessions.md, brainstormed and ruled 2026-09-25 in a second sitting). Sites on the children cite HEAD 2a48e90.

**Goal.** Every seat runs as an interactive Claude Code session inside a tmux session fleet starts, on fleet's own socket, and fleet never talks to Claude Code's background daemon again. Presence comes from tmux; activity still comes from Claude Code's listing; the nudge is typed into the pane; `fleet seat attach` opens it. Claude Code stays in-process in `controller/src/adapter/claude_code.rs` for this flight: the contract that moves it out is flight 12, and it is shaped for this world so the v1 contract never carries a daemon verb.

**Rulings the agent flights build under (Alberto, 2026-09-25):**
1. Order: the tmux host first (this flight), then the agent contract (flight 12), then Claude Code as a TypeScript pack in fleet-packs (flight 13), then Claude Code leaves the repository (flight 14).
2. Core drives tmux. An adapter never touches tmux; it answers `capabilities`, `version`, `launch`, `resume`, `read` and an optional `context`.
3. Seat state is split by question. Presence is core's, from tmux: the session exists and its pane is alive; sessions run with `remain-on-exit on`, so a dead pane keeps its exit status, and the end time is when the controller first sees the pane dead (an event), with the transcript's mtime as the fallback. Activity (starting, busy, idle, blocked on what) is the adapter's one answer, from typed state where the agent has it and screen rules where it does not, saying which. When the two disagree, `fleet status` prints Unknown with both pieces of evidence.
4. The adapter reads transcripts (optional `context`); logged-out is a blocked reason in `read`.
5. Guards read a hook mapping the adapter declares as data in adapter.toml; no process per tool call.
6. The provider wiring (plugin, hooks.json, permissions format, onboarding seed, skills) lives in the adapter pack; packs stop writing per-provider overlays; the repo root stops being a Claude Code plugin.
7. Postures are fleet's own vocabulary (`ask`, `auto`, `unattended`) mapped by the adapter; models are the vendor's strings; the nudge model goes; the first turn is a template the adapter declares.
8. Pins and measurements live in the adapter pack; core compares declared against installed and flags a mismatch.
9. Scope: attach is in. A second runtime (fleet-2u3.6), a screen-rule engine in core, and push through tmux control mode are out.
10. The upgrade adopts nothing: a controller that finds seats still hosted by the daemon refuses to start and names them.
11. `[agent] adapter = "<name>"` is fleet-wide for now and resolves through packs like `[store] adapter`.
12. The store's exec machinery becomes one shared `adapter::exec` (flight 12), after flight 8 lands.
13. Trust: the adapter's launch seeds the trust acceptance for the seat's own worktree into the scoped config directory's `.claude.json` beside the onboarding seed, measured first on 2.1.280; answering the dialog from the screen is the fallback only if a seeded entry does not skip it. fleet trusts only worktrees it created.
14. Postures: three words. `ask` ↔ default, `auto` ↔ auto, `unattended` ↔ dontAsk; stored default/auto/dontAsk read as aliases; a policy naming acceptEdits, bypassPermissions or plan is refused at load, naming the three it can use.
15. brain/lessons/claude-code.md is split: the entries the pack rests on move beside its fixtures in fleet-packs; the daemon-era entries flight 11 retires stay in brain/ as history, marked retired; brain/ keeps a pointer.
16. fleet-bz9 folds into flight 13's plugin row with no interim fix: until flight 13 lands, a fresh fleet's seats get the plugin only when set up by hand.

**Global constraints, every child of flights 11–14:**
- The agent contract's `schema_version` is 1 and grows additively: every request addition optional, every response addition defaulted.
- No row adds Claude Code knowledge outside the in-process adapter; after flight 14, `git grep -i claude` over core/, cli/, controller/ and docs/ finds only prose about the claude-code pack.
- Liveness decisions key on the record and `until` timeouts, never on an adapter's idle word.
- tmux is a declared dependency with a minimum version (3.7b measured), checked by doctor; Windows is unsupported, and the docs say so.
- fleet's sessions live on their own socket, `tmux -L fleet-<project>`, never the person's default server.
- Builders never touch .beads/, departure-board.md or the live fleet; measurements use scratch config directories and a scratch tmux socket.
- docs/ changes go through the docs skill, every claim verified. Names per brain/naming.md.
- Measured claims name the version: Claude Code 2.1.280 (the supported version), tmux 3.7b.
- Landing checks per the reviewer's practice: the touched suites per landing, the full workspace suite once at the flight's end.

**Independent of the store flights.** This flight touches no store code and can fly beside flights 9 and 10.

**Sequencing inside the flight.** The host first; then start, and presence, in parallel; then stop/revive/remove, the nudge and attach; the upgrade refusal, doctor check and docs last.
notes:
REVIEWER CALLS E1–E18 from the spec pass, 2026-09-25. The children cite these as "Reviewer call 2026-09-25 (En)"; the drafting found where the design met the code differently, and these settle it for flights 11–14.

E1. One tmux socket per controller: `tmux -L fleet` (the controller runs per
    machine; seats span projects). Replace every `fleet-<project>`. A seat's
    session is named by its seat id.
E2. The agent is the pane's own process: new-session with the argv as its
    command and the environment set exactly (D1); never typed into a shell.
    Revive = a new session whose command is the resume argv.
E3. Resume carries the start flags (plugin dir, model, posture) with the full
    session id; fleet-rge6.4 measures on 2.1.280 that a flagged full-id resume of an
    interactive session keeps plugin, model and posture (A9 was measured on
    background sessions only).
E4. `send` delivers text as a bracketed paste, then a separate submit.
E5. A send to a seat already busy is recorded `queued`, not `sent`.
E6. Short ids never leave the adapter: it parses the listing with its own
    private row type; the upgrade refusal (fleet-rge6.6) uses it.
E7. Test seams: FakeHost for the in-process controller suites; for the
    binary-driven cli suites a `FLEET_TMUX_BIN` seam pointing at a test-only
    `fleet-tmux-stub` (state in a file, required-features test-support,
    mirrors fleet-store-stub), added to the hermetic env list. fleet-rge6.1 produces
    both; fleet-14p8.7 consumes them.
E8. launch may write inside the scoped config dir AND the seat's worktree
    (the transient seat's permission file lands in the worktree today,
    transient.rs:703). The request carries fleet's neutral `permissions`
    (what transient.rs builds today, stated provider-neutrally) and anything
    else fleet-jymr.5 needs from core (name it, e.g. `touched`); the plugin dir is
    the adapter's own (its pack path) and is never in the request; a
    `plugin_dir` policy key goes in fleet-x93d.2.
E9. Accept: capabilities carries `posture_models` (the D3 gate); config_dir
    optional in requests (named seats have none); read carries `cause?`;
    last_write is a Stamp.
E10. Contract types in core/src/agent; the trait and the conformance suite in
    the controller.
E11. fleet-14p8.9 is CLASS DECLARATIONS ONLY: a pack declares which of core's
    compiled guard classes it turns on, in a `[guards]` table in pack.toml
    (no ninth slot); `fleet guard` with no class argument runs the classes
    the layers declare. NO pattern-rule language (no consumer; YAGNI) — cut
    it. The defaults' permissions deny list: say in one line whether it
    becomes class declarations or stays the adapter's permissions format.
E12. `[agent] adapter` missing → the default name "claude-code" resolved
    through packs (as the store's None → "bd"); `claude_code` is accepted as
    an alias of the name. fleet-x93d.1 does not offer `none`.
E13. Projection: fleet-14p8.3 adds a neutral `agent` block to the projection;
    fleet-x93d.2 removes `fleet.claude_code` and says so in docs/status.md.
E14. B10 and D8 were measured on 2.1.282: any row resting on them re-measures
    on the pinned 2.1.280 at its first step and records the version.
E15. fleet-031 is narrowed to the entries the pack keeps, runs after flight
    12, and blocks fleet-jymr.2 and fleet-jymr.6.
E16. Root skills/ are symlinks into packs/tiny: fleet-jymr.5 owns their new home;
    the reviewer flags fleet-rsia.1 separately.
E17. Folds: fleet-nrl and fleet-fmver close with fleet-rge6.5 (fmver's addressing
    and outcome defects are answered by typing into the seat's own session
    and believing busy/queued; if a distinct st#18 defect remains, state it
    in one line under Open for the reviewer so it gets its own bead).
    fleet-78r and fleet-bz9 close with fleet-jymr.5. fleet-2u3.13 IS fleet-2u3.13 (its
    body becomes this row's). fleet-1jr1e IS fleet-1jr1e. fleet-2u3.8 is
    reparented under flight 13 and closes with fleet-jymr.6. fleet-tiz69 and
    fleet-tnkuq.54 stay separate (relate them).
E18. (drafting only: bodies trimmed.)

CORRECTIONS AT REVIEW (2026-09-25): read matches a listing row by session id, else by the pane's pid (fleet-14p8.2 carries `pid?` on read); no cwd match anywhere. The pack's guard classes are `[pack] guard_classes`, not a `[guards]` table. The hook mapping has no `paths` pointer.

FOLDED AND REPARENTED: fleet-2u3.13 is flight 11's attach row (fleet-rge6's child); fleet-nrl and fleet-fmver close with fleet-rge6.5; fleet-1jr1e is flight 12's posture row (fleet-14p8's child); fleet-78r and fleet-bz9 close with fleet-jymr.5; fleet-2u3.8 stays open for its per-platform half, related to fleet-jymr.6. fleet-031 is narrowed and blocks fleet-jymr.2 and fleet-jymr.6. fleet-2u3.6 (a second runtime), fleet-tiz69 and fleet-tnkuq.54 stay separate.

OPEN: the command family's name (`fleet agent` / `fleet runtime` / `fleet harness`) is Alberto's, ruled at the end of the spec pass; the children are written with `fleet agent`.

title: The bd pack's doctor check and CI: bd-version moves into the pack, fleet store check and a smoke ring run on a pinned fleet
description:
SPEC (fleet-rsia.5, drafted 2026-09-25). In fleet-packs. Blocked by fleet-rsia.2, fleet-rsia.3, fleet-rsia.4.

**Behaviour.** The bd pack carries its own doctor check and proves itself in CI.

- `adapters/store/bd/doctor/bd-version/{doctor.toml, run.sh}`: core/defaults/doctor/bd-version at e416304 moved as is (the pin `PINNED=1.3.0` at run.sh:33 becomes the pack's; the doctor.toml comment "THE PIN IS THE BINARY'S, not a pack's" is rewritten: it is the pack's now, and `fleet doctor` finds it through the packs like any pack check, core/src/item/doctor.rs `entries` 130-144). The defaults' copy is deleted in flight 10.
- The `FLEET_BD_BIN` seam is the adapter's and the doctor's, documented in the pack's README: an absolute path to the bd to run.
- CI (GitHub Actions in fleet-packs): install Deno 2.9.7 (runtimes/ts's pin), bd 1.3.0 by beads' own instructions, and fleet at the tag the repo pins (build from source with cargo at that tag, cached; a release binary when fleet publishes one); `deno fmt --check`, `deno lint`, `deno test` in the adapter; `deno task types` and `git diff --exit-code contract.d.ts`; `fleet store check --adapter adapters/store/bd/adapters/store/bd/main.ts` must print no FAIL; a smoke ring on a scratch project: `fleet create` with the pack installed from the checkout, `fleet seat add --agent`, `fleet dispatch`, `fleet deliver --delivery`, `fleet review`, a retire's withdraw, each read back through `fleet item show --json`, so the fenced writes are proven on a real board.
- The pinned fleet tag is one line in the repo (`FLEET_VERSION` in the workflow or a `versions.toml` at the root); moving it is a commit.

**Acceptance.** The workflow is green on the repo's main; a deliberate break (a wrong exit code in `close`) turns the check step red; the doctor check reads `bd-version: pinned bd 1.3.0; …` through `fleet doctor` on a machine with the pack installed and no defaults' copy.
notes:
From fleet-rsia.2's builder (2026-09-25): fleet --version prints 0.1.0 with no commit, so the pinned fleet tag CI builds cannot be confirmed from the binary itself; record the tag/sha the workflow builds from. title: The bd pack's orders, runs, holds, export and scratch: one fenced update for the withdraw, gates for holds, the -o and bd init quirks, foreign keys
description:
SPEC (fleet-rsia.4, drafted 2026-09-25). In fleet-packs. Blocked by fleet-rsia.2.

**Behaviour.** Orders, runs, holds, export and scratch over bd.

- `order.set` and `run.set`: one `--metadata` write of `{"fleet.orders": {…, "v": 1}}` or `{"fleet.run": {…, "v": 1}}`; bd merges at the top level and replaces the one key whole (661), so the other stands; the keys and the `v` stamp are core/src/store/bd/keys.rs at e416304 (`ORDERS` 24, `RUN` 27, `VERSION_FIELD` 30, `versioned` 53; a nested `fleet` object is lost on the next write, keys.rs:13, which is why the keys are flat).
- `order.withdraw` with the fences and `reopen`: ONE `update` carrying `--if-assignee`, `--if-status`, `--assignee ""`, `--unset-metadata fleet.orders` and `--status open` (677, 722-728); exit 13 answers `moved`.
- `hold.raise` is `gate create` (type human by default, 767; the held item leaves the ready set at once); `hold.clear` is `gate resolve`, read first because a second resolve exits 0 (791) and answers `already`; `holds.open` is `gate list -n 0` (never names the blocked item, 811; cap of 50, 815; may answer `null`).
- `export {into}`: `bd export -o <file>` with the path made absolute first, because `-o` resolves against the caller's working directory and not `-C` (999); answers `{file}`. `scratch {into}`: `bd init` in `into` with `--prefix` (957: the prefix stays commented in the config, so write it), on a directory that must exist and be empty (1023); answers `{root}`; `bd init` writes agent-integration files (1030), which the scratch leaves as they are.
- The foreign keys (fleet-urp): every top-level metadata key that is not `fleet.orders` or `fleet.run` is listed on the Item's `foreign`.

**Acceptance.** `fleet store check --adapter` passes checks 13, 14, 15, 17, 19, 20, 23 and every check from fleet-rsia.2 and fleet-rsia.3: 23 PASS and the new fences checks, none SKIP; `deno test` covers each quirk; the whole check runs in the time bd's in-process adapter took plus the spawn (measure and record; fleet-4qpq's per-check printing lands in flight 8, so the run is watchable).
notes:
fleet-rsia.2 (landed fleet-packs 0dfd405) left capabilities' DECLARED = {export: null, scratch: false} in verbs/reads.ts; this row flips it to {export: {file: .beads/issues.jsonl, dir: .beads/}, scratch: true} when it builds the verbs. The whole fleet store check run (checks 1-11 and 16 included) is this row's acceptance: nothing runs before scratch.
Landed fleet-packs 6240086 (main, local; squash of builder branch fleet-rsia.4 9ec36ad, rebased on 8ddc311; not pushed). Files: verbs/orders.ts (order.set, run.set, order.withdraw), verbs/holds.ts (hold.raise, hold.clear, holds.open), verbs/store.ts (export, scratch); DECLARED flipped to {export: {file: .beads/issues.jsonl, dir: .beads/}, scratch: true}; main.ts registers all five handler sets; tests orders_test/holds_test/store_test + a 7-step main_test on a real board; fixtures gate_create, gate_create_missing, gate_list_empty, show_gate_closed. No lib/ changes: uses fleet-rsia.3's lib/write.ts (the builder's own copy deleted at the reviewer's word).
Verified by the reviewer: deno task test 95/95 (29 steps, 1 step ignored: "a verb not built yet" has no verb left); deno fmt --check and deno lint clean; `fleet store check --adapter <fleet-packs>/adapters/store/bd/adapters/store/bd/main.ts` (fleet 7fadcde, bd 1.3.0, Deno 2.9.7, macOS arm64) → 25 passed, 0 failed, 2 skipped, 73 s. title: The bd pack's skeleton, generated contract types, and the read verbs over bd 1.3.0 with their quirks and fixtures
description:
SPEC (fleet-rsia.2, drafted 2026-09-25). In fleet-packs. Blocked by flight 8's schema verb and pack slot, and by the repo's existence (the assumption bead).

**Behaviour.** The bd pack's skeleton and its read verbs.

- `adapters/store/bd/pack.toml`: `[pack] name = "bd", version = "0.1.0", schema = 3, description = "The beads store: bd 1.3.0 behind the store contract."`; `[imports.ts] source = "../../../runtimes/ts", version = …` (Deno pinned by the ts pack; a pack that carries an adapter written for Deno imports the runtime pack rather than pinning its own).
- `adapters/store/bd/adapters/store/bd/adapter.toml`: `[adapter] name = "bd", kind = "store", version = "0.1.0", description = …, entry = "main.ts"` (the keys fleet-wpf0.2 fixed).
- `main.ts`, executable, shebang `#!/usr/bin/env -S deno run --allow-run=bd --allow-read --allow-write --allow-env=FLEET_BD_BIN` (narrow `--allow-read/--allow-write` to the root once the request is read: Deno permissions are static on the shebang, so the pack documents the grant). It reads one JSON value off stdin, dispatches `Deno.args[0]`, prints one JSON value, and exits by the table: an unknown verb or a request that fails the schema is 2; a bd that cannot be run is 3 with `{error}`; stderr's last line is for people.
- `contract.d.ts`: generated from `fleet store schema` by `deno task types` (a script in `adapters/store/bd/scripts/`, using json-schema-to-typescript from a pinned npm specifier or a hand-rolled emitter, the builder's choice recorded on the bead); committed; a CI step regenerates and diffs.
- Reads: `version` (runs `bd version`, answers `{name: "bd", version}`), `capabilities` (`{export: {file: ".beads/issues.jsonl", dir: ".beads/"}, scratch: true, item_prefix, cli: "bd", items: {types, priority}}` as fleet-xpc's ruling shapes it), `resolve`, `show`, `list`, `timeline`, ported from core/src/store/bd/mod.rs at e416304 (`shown` 340, `opened` 300, `item_from` 1076, `order_of` 411, the listing 552-600, the comment shapes 852-882) with the quirks: `BD_JSON_ENVELOPE=1` on every call (121); an empty listing may answer `null` (188); `-n 0` on every listing and `list.limit` caps piped output (552-558); `list -a <seat>` needs `--all` for closed items (565); ambiguity is told on stderr only (365-372); a partial id resolves by prefix of the hash (526, fleet-z5m's rule); `--metadata` merges at the top level (661); a bare error carries `schema_version` and no `data` (318); a missing id is an error with no code (332).
- Fixtures: core/src/store/bd/fixtures/*.json (gate_list, list, list_assigned, ready, show, show_missing, show_unreadable_orders; recorded from bd 1.3.0 with the envelope, bd_cli.rs 46-55) copied into `adapters/store/bd/test/fixtures/` and the decoder tests ported to `deno test`.

**Interfaces produced.** `lib/bd.ts` (run bd with argv, the envelope, the exit and stderr reading), `lib/rows.ts` (bd row → contract Item/ItemSummary/Entry), `lib/answer.ts` (the envelope, the exit table, the refusal shapes). fleet-rsia.3 and fleet-rsia.4 consume them.

**Acceptance.** `fleet store check --adapter <path>/main.ts` passes checks 1-11, 16 (reads) and skips nothing it can answer; `deno test` green on the fixtures; `deno fmt --check` and `deno lint` clean; a `show` of an ambiguous fragment refuses `ambiguous` with the candidates off stderr.
notes:
Landed fleet-packs 0dfd405 (main, local; squash of builder branch fleet-rsia.2 4223f7d; not pushed). Files: adapters/store/bd/pack.toml and adapters/store/bd/adapters/store/bd/{adapter.toml, main.ts, deno.json, deno.lock, contract.json, contract.d.ts, scripts/types.ts, lib/{bd,rows,answer,schema}.ts, verbs/reads.ts, test/*}.
Verified by the reviewer: deno task test 50/50 (main_test's 11 steps on a real bd 1.3.0 board); deno fmt --check and deno lint clean; deno task types + git diff clean; fleet pack check (fleet 7fadcde) clean.
ACCEPTANCE MOVED: fleet store check cannot run any check before scratch exists (it refuses up front: "declares no scratch capability"), and checks 1-11/16 need create/update/append/run.set/holds too; the full check run is fleet-rsia.4's acceptance (23 PASS, none SKIP). The reads are proven instead by main_test on a real board. Ambiguous show verified: refuses ambiguous with candidates off stderr.
REVIEWER CALLS: (D1) main.ts is a two-line sh/TS polyglot, not an env -S shebang: --allow-run must name $FLEET_BD_BIN's absolute value, which a fixed shebang cannot (measured on Deno 2.9.7: --allow-run=bd resolves bd on PATH once at start). --no-config and --no-prompt added. Accepted. (D2) --allow-read/--allow-write stay whole: Deno 2.9.7 cannot narrow a grant after start (measured). Accepted; the epic's "on the root" constraint is not reachable on the pin. (D3) Hand-rolled type generator (scripts/types.ts), no npm; contract.json (fleet store schema's output) committed and read at run time to refuse a request that fails the schema with exit 2. (D4) Unbuilt verbs answer 2; capabilities declares export null and scratch false until fleet-rsia.4 flips DECLARED in verbs/reads.ts. (D5) version runs bd version without -C. (D6) scripts/ and test/ live in the adapter directory (a pack's top level holds only the manifest and the eight slots). (D7) [imports.ts] source "../../../runtimes/ts" confirmed against add.rs locate_import.
Quirks: every spec quirk reproduced with a test except the generated-wire-type arms, the ReadProof assertion, tracker_line/pin line (rsia.5's doctor) and fleet's strict/lenient bd resolution, each dropped with the reason in the code.
Timings (macOS arm64, bd 1.3.0, Deno 2.9.7, fleet 7fadcde): show 522 ms via main.ts vs 460 ms bd alone; version 61 vs 47 ms; capabilities 15 ms (no bd call: the per-hook cost fleet-xpc asked to measure).
SEEN NOT FIXED: (1) core/src/store/exec.rs Exec::call runs the adapter under fleet's own environment, not the search path bd::open resolved bd on — under launchd neither deno nor bd may be found; flight 10 must pass the search path or set FLEET_BD_BIN (noted on fleet-3krx.1). (2) fleet store check cannot exercise a partial adapter (everything needs scratch) — by design. (3) fleet --version prints 0.1.0 with no commit, so "the fleet tag CI pins" cannot be confirmed from the binary (noted on fleet-rsia.5). (4) A person-held item stays exit 3, as core (fleet-herk).

title: fleet-store-stub: a test-only adapter executable answering the contract from the fake, its state in a file, so every Exec path runs with no bd
description:
SPEC (fleet-wpf0.7, drafted 2026-09-25). Sites at e416304. Blocked by fleet-wpf0.4 (the trait) and fleet-wpf0.6 (the fake).

**Behaviour.** A test-only adapter executable that answers the whole contract from the fake, so every Exec path and the conformance suite run with no bd on the box. Because each Exec call is a fresh process, the stub persists the fake between calls in a file.

- `core/src/bin/store_stub.rs`, `[[bin]] name = "fleet-store-stub", required-features = ["test-support"]` in core/Cargo.toml (today no `[[bin]]`, `test-support = []` at 15-16; lib.rs:128-129 gates the module).
- `fleet-store-stub <verb>`: reads the request off stdin, loads `<root>/.store/state.json` (the FakeStore's items, holds, comments, counters, serialized with serde), dispatches the verb to `impl Store for FakeStore` (test_support.rs 621-1009) through the contract's request and response types (types.rs 572-634), writes the state back, prints the answer with `schema_version`, and exits by the table: 0, 1 with `{"refused": {reason, message, candidates}}` for a `StoreError::Refused` (the reason recovered from the text the fake's `refuse` 231 builds: give the fake a typed refusal and derive the text from it, rather than parsing text back), 2 for an unknown verb or a request that does not decode, 3 for `Unreadable`.
- `scratch {into}` makes `<into>/.store/state.json` empty and answers `{root: into}`; `export` writes `EXPORT_FILE` (test_support.rs:30) as the fake does; `capabilities` declares both and `item_prefix: "fx"`; `version` answers `{"name": "stub", "version": "0"}`.
- Failure injection: `FLEET_STUB_DEAF=1` sets `ignore_writes` (172-174) for the call; `FLEET_STUB_SLOW=<secs>` sleeps before answering (for the 60 s bound arms, exec.rs 470-520 today use a `#!/bin/sh` stub for that: keep those where the shell stub is simpler).

**Sites.** core/Cargo.toml; core/src/bin/store_stub.rs (new); core/src/test_support.rs (state (de)serialization, a `Refusal`-typed error); core/tests/contract.rs:105 (a third arm: the suite over `Exec::at(stub, root)`); cli/tests/store_check.rs (an arm: `fleet store check --adapter <stub>` passes every check; the stub's path from `env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_fleet")`'s directory, since cli's tests cannot name core's bin directly).

**Interfaces produced.** The binary `fleet-store-stub` beside `fleet` in target/debug; `fleet_core::test_support::stub_path() -> PathBuf` for core's own tests (`env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_fleet-store-stub")`); a cli/tests/common helper `stub_store(root) -> PathBuf` that writes `[store] adapter = <stub>` into the project's policy and scratches the state. fleet-wpf0.8 and fleet-wpf0.9 consume these.

**Acceptance.** `fleet store check --adapter target/debug/fleet-store-stub` prints 23 PASS lines (none SKIP: export and scratch declared) in under 5 s; the conformance suite passes on the stub through Exec; a write with `FLEET_STUB_DEAF=1` makes the read-back arm fail the way the in-process `ignore_writes` does; every stub answer decodes through `types::answer`.
notes:
Landed a46f7a0 (squash of 8fc68f5 on 3044595; flight 8 wave 5): fleet-store-stub, a test-only adapter executable answering the whole contract from the fake: core/src/bin/store_stub.rs ([[bin]], required-features test-support) is a three-line main over core/src/test_support/stub.rs (decode the envelope and the verb's fields, flock .store/state.lock for up to 30 s, load <root>/.store/state.json into FakeStore::from_state, dispatch, save, answer by the exit table: 0; 1 with {"refused": {reason, message, candidates}} from the fake's new typed refusal field, never parsed text; 2 for an unknown verb, an undecodable request and what docs/store.md calls malformed; 3 for Unreadable); scratch/export/capabilities/version as specified (capabilities answers where no store exists yet — fleet store check asks before it scratches); FLEET_STUB_DEAF and FLEET_STUB_SLOW; a hashed knob mints fx-<3 base-36> so the ambiguity check can pass on the stub; with_state(root, |store| …) for rigs; stub_path() in core (worked out from the running test binary; an arm pins it to CARGO_BIN_EXE_fleet-store-stub) and in cli/tests/common with stub_store(root). fleet store check --adapter <stub> prints 25 PASS, 0 FAIL, 2 SKIP (the two another-writer checks: no contract verb plants another tool's keys). Review calls: accepted the stub's logic in the library; accepted the cli example target cli/examples/fleet-store-stub.rs as how a fleet-cli test build gets a fresh stub (cargo builds no dependency's bin for a test build; a filtered --test run that skips examples panics naming the build command); accepted the lock over a root per suite (review focus 1; RED-PROOF: with the lock removed the 16-caller arm lost writes, 22 distinct ids of 48); accepted state saved after every call, stderr empty except on exit 2 (Exec copies stderr into refusals); the 5 s acceptance missed at 5.56 s wall (1.2 s CPU) — core/src/process.rs:105 WAIT_SLICE 20 ms per Exec call is the floor, not this bead's to change. Landing checks at a46f7a0: build (all targets), clippy, fmt; core stub|contract (both real-bd arms) 46/46; cli store_check 9/9; the builder's run: core lib 100/100, core item_list|show|hold|retire|dispatch 77/77, cli workspace|store_schema 13/13, clippy with and without the feature. SEEN NOT FIXED: core/src/store/conformance.rs another_writers_keys reads metadata off the top level of the read's raw text, which through Exec is the whole answer with the item under "item" — no external adapter can pass it even with a planter handed in (tried on the stub with a with_state planter: 'another writer's keys' fails, '…listed as foreign' passes) — a bead candidate; core/src/process.rs:105 WAIT_SLICE sets the per-call floor for every Exec adapter.
RULING (Alberto 2026-09-25, recommended option): Exec's per-call floor (core/src/process.rs WAIT_SLICE 20 ms) stays on this bead — measure against the bd pack's real cost in flight 9 before changing a slice every bounded call shares.
