title: fleet store schema prints the contract as JSON Schema generated from the Rust types, committed with a drift test
description:
SPEC (fleet-wpf0.5, drafted 2026-09-25). Sites at e416304. Blocked by fleet-wpf0.1 (the fields are final).

**Behaviour.** `fleet store schema` prints the store contract as one JSON Schema document, generated from the Rust types, so an adapter author fetches the contract from the binary they target and the TypeScript adapter (flight 9) generates its types from it.

- The document: `{"schema_version": 1, "verbs": {"<verb>": {"request": <schema>, "response": <schema>}}, "refusal": <schema>, "error": <schema>}`, one entry per row of docs/store.md's verbs table (283-299), request = the envelope (`schema_version`, `root`) plus the verb's fields, response = `schema_version` plus the verb's body type (types.rs 572-634: Resolved, Shown, Listed, Created, Appended, Raised, OpenHolds, Exported, Scratched, Answered).
- Generated with `schemars` (add to the workspace deps, root Cargo.toml `[workspace.dependencies]`; derive `JsonSchema` beside `Serialize` on every type in types.rs 355-634 and on `Entry`/`Body` in core/src/entry.rs, which `append` sends and `timeline` answers).
- Committed at `core/src/store/store.schema.json`; a test regenerates and compares byte for byte, failing with "run `cargo run -p fleet-cli -- store schema > core/src/store/store.schema.json`" when stale (the pattern of bd_wire.schema.json's generator, tools/bd-wire-types, reversed).
- `fleet store schema` exits 0 and prints the committed document (embedded with `include_str!`), so what an author reads is what the tests pinned.

**Sites.** cli/src/store.rs `enum Verb` 31-51 (add `Schema`), `command` 53-57; core/src/store/types.rs; core/src/entry.rs `to_json`/`read_row` (fleet-pjl pins the entry's wire shape first: sequence after it); docs/store.md: a `## The schema` section before `## Checking an adapter` 378 (docs skill).

**Interfaces produced.** `fleet_core::store::schema::document() -> serde_json::Value`; the file `core/src/store/store.schema.json`; the verb `fleet store schema`. fleet-rsia.2 consumes the file.

**Acceptance.** `fleet store schema | jq '.verbs | keys'` lists exactly the verbs of docs/store.md; the drift test fails when a field is added without regenerating; the doc examples in types.rs's drift test validate against their verb's schema (one arm: every example instance passes the generated schema through a validator in the test, or the arm is dropped with the reason noted if no light validator exists in the deps).
notes: Landed 2a48e90 (squash of 9e13903, the rebase of 6c49a6a onto 3742f44; flight 8 wave 4): fleet store schema prints the store contract as one JSON Schema document (draft 2020-12): {$schema, schema_version 1, verbs: 18 × {request, response}, refusal, error, $defs}, generated by fleet_core::store::schema::document() from JsonSchema derived on every contract type (hand-written for Status, Stamp with STAMP_PATTERN, SeatId, Actor, Entry and the append's NewEntry; Update.status const "open"; priorities capped at 4), committed at core/src/store/store.schema.json with a drift arm; the request of each verb is the envelope plus exactly what exec.rs sends (an arm drives all 18 verbs through a stub and holds the request's keys to the schema's properties, the request to its schema, and the answer to its response schema); a hand-written validator (13 keywords of 2020-12, $ref inside the document, refusing any keyword it does not know — an arm walks the document) with regex-lite behind test-support only; schemars exact-pinned =1.2.2 (default features off; fleet-core's normal tree 34 → 51 lines: schemars, schemars_derive, serde_derive_internals, dyn-clone, ref-cast, ref-cast-impl, all MIT or MIT/Apache); docs/store.md gains ## The schema. RED-PROOFs by fault injection on a git archive: a new Version.build fails the drift and cli byte-for-byte arms; exec sending an extra field fails the exec arm naming the verb; removing status's const lets a closed status pass and fails the fence arm; to_json adding a key fails the entry arm; a docs verbs-table row the schema lacks fails the cli verbs arm. Review calls: accepted D1 (the binary prints the document it generates at run time, not include_str! — the spec's own regeneration command pipes the binary onto the file; the drift arm and the cli arm hold the two byte for byte); D2 doc-comment descriptions stripped (only the absent-vs-null texts on update's assignee/if_assignee and order.withdraw's if_assignee kept, an arm checks them); D3 requests accept unnamed keys (only deny_unknown_fields types say additionalProperties false); D4 $schema and $defs at the top; D5 the validator as described; D6 schemas stricter than the readers (SeatId unpadded, status const open, priority ≤ 4); D7 $defs/NewEntry. Rebase on fleet-2tp resolved by the builder: ItemSummary's doc + JsonSchema derive; exec.rs's neighbouring arms kept; the schema regenerated (ItemSummary gains optional assignee and run); the 18-verb arm's list answer carries both. Landing checks at 2a48e90: core lib 100/100; cli store_schema 2/2; the builder's run on the identical tree: core entry 29/29, cli bins 24/24, cli store_schema|store_check 9/9 at -j 2, clippy and fmt clean. SEEN NOT FIXED: core/src/store/types.rs:10-12's module doc still says 'NOTHING READS THESE YET' (the walkthrough's held F3 on fleet-alt.1); $defs/OrderState's none/unreadable branches do not forbid an order key serde refuses; docs/README.md:43's store row mentions neither checking an adapter nor the schema. DOCS REVIEW NOTE: docs/store.md at 6c49a6a, 10 claims, 5 run, 0 left out — § The schema: prints one JSON Schema document draft 2020-12 (cli/src/store.rs, schema.rs; ran fleet store schema > contract.json, exit 0, jq $schema); reads no project and no store (ran from /tmp with an empty FLEET_DIR, identical output); the jq '.verbs | keys' example (ran, 18 verbs; cli store_schema.rs); exits 0 (ran); schema_version 1 (ran jq keys); verbs holds one entry per table row with request/response as described (schema.rs, store_schema.rs, exec.rs's arm; ran jq .verbs.show); refusal and error (schema.rs; ran jq); $defs and $ref (schema.rs take_definitions, check()); additionalProperties false only on the types that refuse unknown keys (types.rs deny_unknown_fields, entry.rs; ran jq $defs.Order.additionalProperties → false); update's status is "open" only (types.rs; ran jq .verbs.update.request.properties.status → const open).

title: The trait slims onto the fences: hand_over, reopen and order_withdraw_from go, order_withdraw takes a WithdrawFence, review and retire call the contract
description:
SPEC (fleet-wpf0.4, drafted 2026-09-25). Sites at e416304. Blocked by fleet-wpf0.1 (the fences).

**Behaviour.** The Store trait has no method an external adapter cannot answer. The three override-only methods go:

- `hand_over(item, from, to, by)` (mod.rs:189-217, default body; bd override 642-657) becomes a plain call: `update(id, &Update { assignee: Some(to), if_assignee: Some(from), ..default }, by)`. Its typed-text checks (a `to` that is no seat id, a `by` that is no typed actor) stay where the caller builds the Update. Caller: core/src/item/review.rs:401 in `retur`.
- `reopen(item, by)` (mod.rs:238; bd 715; Exec 294-300 answers Unreadable) goes; nothing in production calls it (only the test wrappers listed below).
- `order_withdraw_from(id, seat, status, by)` (mod.rs:258-276 default; bd 732-761) goes; `order_withdraw` takes the fence: `fn order_withdraw(&self, id: &ItemId, fence: &WithdrawFence, by: &Actor)`. Caller: core/src/seat/retire.rs:99 in `withdraw`, which sends `WithdrawFence { if_assignee: Some(Some(seat)), if_status: Some(row.status), reopen: true }`; its call budget (retire.rs:15-20, one update per item withdrawn) is unchanged.

**Sites.** core/src/store/mod.rs trait 138-365 and the helpers `moved` 469, `restatused` 479; exec.rs 279-282, 289-300; bd/mod.rs 642-657, 715-761, its `order_withdraw` ~661; test_support.rs FakeStore 729, 761, 771 and the Arc wrapper 1058-1071; the delegating wrappers in core/tests/review.rs:303, dispatch.rs:198, hold.rs:205, land.rs:508, deliver.rs:221, contract.rs:405, cli/tests/run.rs:1840-1874; core/tests/store.rs:923-960 `a_withdrawal_is_one_update_clearing_the_assignee_and_the_order` (rewrite against the fenced `order_withdraw`).

**Remedy.** Delete the three methods; move `hand_over`'s default into review.rs as a private fn building the Update; bd's `order_withdraw` sends the fences it sent in `order_withdraw_from`; Exec sends the fence fields; the fake applies them. Every wrapper follows the trait.

**Acceptance.** `grep -rn 'hand_over\|order_withdraw_from\|fn reopen' core cli controller` is empty; retire over an Exec stub (fleet-wpf0.7) withdraws and reopens in one call, and a moved row refuses `moved` on bd, the fake and the stub (the conformance checks from fleet-wpf0.1); review's return of a held item works over Exec; core/tests/review.rs, retire.rs, store.rs and cli/tests/run.rs green.
notes: Landed 1c099f7 (squash of 023b1f6, the rebase of 4f413ef onto 7401805; flight 8 wave 3): hand_over, reopen and order_withdraw_from leave the trait, bd, Exec, the fake and every wrapper — the Store trait holds nothing an external adapter cannot answer ('NOTHING BESIDE THE TABLE'); review's retur makes ONE update through a private handed_back(holder, builder) fenced on the holder the review read (no read-then-write remains on that path — the walkthrough's F12 on fleet-alt.1, closed); retire sends WithdrawFence { if_assignee: Some(Some(seat)), if_status: Some(row.status), reopen: true }, one call per item as before; bd's order_withdraw already sent the fences, and the measurements of the three deleted overrides move onto Bd::update's doc; the conformance 'fenced writes' check rewritten onto update(if_assignee), update(status open) and order_withdraw(fence) with every assertion kept and one added (the holder unchanged after a Moved hand-over). New: core/tests/common/adapter.rs, a recording sh adapter through Exec; retire and review arms over it (one fenced order.withdraw carrying if_assignee, if_status in_progress and reopen: true; a moved row refused with nothing more sent; a return is one update with assignee and if_assignee; a moved holder writes no verdict). RED-PROOFs on 78811ed (git archive): the retire arms (the default read first: refused as moved / could-not-tell) and the review arms (verbs [show, timeline, show, update]). Review calls: accepted the rename of fleet-wpf0.1's reopen_through_update fn to update_to_open (the acceptance grep matched 'fn reopen'; the table name is unchanged); accepted moved/restatused moving private into test_support (the fake is their only caller); accepted the recording adapter staying beside fleet-wpf0.7's stub; no docs change (grep of docs/ found no removed method or read-then-write default). Landing checks: build; the acceptance grep empty; core retire|review 37/37; the builder's run on the identical tree: core contract|deliver|dispatch|hold|land|retire|review|store 259/260 (the flaky bound arm, 1/1 alone at -j 2), core lib 90/90, cli run 33/33, ring_land 10/10, cli store_check 7/7. SEEN NOT FIXED: core/src/lib.rs:88-90 calls the order_withdrawn entry 'one note'.

title: fleet create asks which store the fleet uses and installs its pack from the fleet-packs source and tag this binary pins
description:
SPEC (fleet-3krx.1, drafted 2026-09-25). Sites at e416304. Blocked by flight 9. Absorbs fleet-2b6's question (the tiny pack) into one prompt; fleet-2b6 stays its own bead for tiny's flags and arms, blocked by this one.

**Behaviour.** `fleet create` asks which store the fleet uses and installs its pack.

- The prompt, after the fleet's name and before the defaults are written: `store: bd (beads) [default] / none — install later`. Non-interactive: `--store bd|none`; no TTY and no flag takes the default.
- On `bd`, create runs the same path as `fleet pack add <fleet-packs>//adapters/store/bd --version <pinned>` (cli/src/main.rs `pack_add` 912-996 → core/src/add.rs `add` 433), pinned in packs.lock, and writes `[store] adapter = "bd"` into the project's file. On `none`, it writes nothing and prints the `fleet pack add` line to run later; a verb that opens the store then refuses with fleet-wpf0.2's text.
- The source and version come from `core/src/supported.rs`: `PINNED_PACKS_SOURCE = "https://github.com/<org>/fleet-packs"` and `PINNED_PACKS = "v0.1.0"` (the tag this fleet release was checked against), beside `PINNED_CLAUDE_CODE` (46). `--packs-from <path>` overrides the source for a checkout (fleet-2b6 AC3's answer), so a developer installs from a local clone.
- The ordering with the item prefix: create reads `capabilities().item_prefix` off the store (cli/src/lifecycle.rs 179-188), so the pack is installed before that read.

**Sites.** cli/src/lifecycle.rs `CreateArgs` 30-43, `create` 62-300 (the pack install after 267's `defaults_into`); core/src/supported.rs; core/src/add.rs (nothing new: a source with `//adapters/store/bd` parses at 244-272); cli/tests/lifecycle or create suites (arms: the default installs and pins, `--store none` installs nothing and prints the line, no TTY takes the default, `--packs-from` a scratch clone of a fixture pack); docs/getting-started.md `## Creating a fleet` 134-222 and the refusals table 389-402, CONTRIBUTING § supported versions, docs/getting-started.md "What fleet runs on" 62-82 (a fleet-packs row), all through the docs skill.

**Acceptance.** A fresh `fleet create` on a machine with network installs the bd pack at the pinned tag and the first `fleet item list` works; `--store none` then `fleet item list` prints the pack add line and exits 3; `fleet doctor` reports the bd-version check from the pack; the docs drift arms pass.
notes: From fleet-rsia.2's builder (2026-09-25, SEEN NOT FIXED): core/src/store/exec.rs Exec::call runs an external adapter under fleet's own environment, not the child PATH (Opening.search_path) that bd::open resolved bd on. Under a launchd service the bd pack's sh/deno entry may find neither deno nor bd. When bd leaves the repo, Exec should pass the search path to the adapter, or fleet should set FLEET_BD_BIN.

title: fleet prime's second line reads the store's version verb through the opener, and supported.rs stops re-exporting bd's pin and tracker line
description:
SPEC (fleet-wpf0.3, drafted 2026-09-25). Sites at e416304. Independent of the other children.

**Behaviour.** `fleet prime`'s second line reads the store through the contract, not bd's pin. Today cli/src/prime.rs:64-67 prints `supported::tracker_line(child_path)`, which is `core/src/store/bd/mod.rs:1186-1200` running `bd version` and comparing with `PINNED_BD` ("bd: 1.3.0, the pinned version" / "bd: X, not the pinned 1.3.0 — …" / "bd: could not be read — …"). After this child the line is the store's own answer: `store: <name> <version> (adapter <adapter name>)`, from the opener's `version()` (types.rs Version 543-548) and the adapter's name (`"bd"`, a pack adapter's `name`, or the path's file name), and when the store cannot be opened or answer, `store: could not be read — <why>`. The pin comparison leaves prime: it is the doctor's (`bd-version` in the defaults today, the bd pack's in flight 9), and the doctor is what `fleet run` and a person consult for it.

**Sites.** cli/src/prime.rs 58-67 (the two lines; the module doc at 10 names PINNED_BD); core/src/supported.rs 23 and 29 (drop both re-exports; `PINNED_BD` and `tracker_line` stay inside bd/mod.rs for the doctor's comment and the bd tests until flight 10; bd_cli.rs 63, 135-147 keep reading `bd::PINNED_BD`); tests reading the line: cli/tests/plugin.rs 1343, 1392, 1399, 1406, cli/tests/doctor.rs:127, core/tests/pack.rs 662-687 (which reference `PINNED_BD` for the doctor: keep those); docs/getting-started.md 330-355 (the prime text and the second-line variants 347-353) through the docs skill; docs/packs.md 258-295 if it quotes the second line.

**Remedy.** prime opens the project's store through `store::open` with `strict: false` and a short timeout (bd's `VERSION_TIMEOUT` 1180 is the precedent), prints the line, and always exits 0 (docs/conventions.md:260). No project resolved: `store: none (no project here)`.

**Acceptance.** `fleet prime` in a project on bd prints `store: bd 1.3.0 (adapter bd)`; on the stub, `store: stub 0 (adapter fleet-store-stub)`; with the adapter unrunnable, the could-not-be-read line and exit 0; `grep -rn 'tracker_line\|PINNED_BD' cli core/src/supported.rs` is empty; plugin.rs and doctor.rs green.
notes: Landed 8055aae (squash of ca81a57, flight 8 wave 1): fleet prime's line 2 is 'store: <name> <version> (adapter <adapter>)', 'store: could not be read — <why>' or 'store: none (no project here)', read through store::open (strict false, a 2 s VERSION_TIMEOUT in prime.rs); prime still exits 0; supported.rs drops the PINNED_BD and tracker_line re-exports. Review calls: accepted Bd::version answering the version token (version_token, shared with named_version) so the line reads 'bd 1.3.0' — nothing else reads Version.version beyond non-empty; accepted store::adapter_name(policy) in core beside the opener (the file name of what [store] adapter names, else bd::NAME) — fleet-wpf0.2 lands bare names through it; accepted [ASSUMED] the project root as the seat's worktree else the walk's found file, not item::resolve_from's machine-fleet.toml fallback (that case prints none); accepted keeping cli/tests/doctor.rs:127's PINNED_BD (the doctor rig's bd stub answers the pin, which the Sites say to keep) — so the acceptance grep's one remaining hit is that line; the stub acceptance covered by a shell adapter named fleet-store-stub until fleet-wpf0.7. Landing checks at 8055aae: build; fleet-core lib 75/75; store|contract|pack 97/97; cli bins 24/24; plugin|lifecycle|doctor 79/80 under load, the one failure plugin::a_listing_that_never_answers_is_its_own_answer_inside_the_bound (a bound arm) passing in two -j 2 re-runs 32/32 — load. SEEN NOT FIXED (builder): store::tail() takes the LAST stderr line, which for bd -C <no .beads> is bd's usage hint ('Use "bd [command] --help"…') not its 'Error: … no beads project found' line, so every bd refusal in a boardless directory reads uselessly (core/src/store/mod.rs tail); Bd::run's could-not-run refusal says 'nothing was written' even for a read like --version (bd/mod.rs:130-137); core/defaults/doctor/bd-version/run.sh:22-23 and core/tests/pack.rs:668-669 call FLEET_BD_BIN 'the seam prime reads the tracker through'; tracker_line (bd/mod.rs) now has no caller and stays pub until flight 10. DOCS REVIEW NOTE (the docs skill's citations, from the builder): docs/getting-started.md and docs/packs.md at ca81a57 — the line-2 forms read in cli/src/prime.rs store_line/store_version and run in scratch projects (bd 1.3.0 board; no project; a non-executable adapter; exit 0 each); 'adapter … bd or the file name' read in store::adapter_name and plugin arm line_two_reads_the_adapter_the_project_names; 'the project is the seat's worktree … else the nearest fleet.toml or .fleet/project.toml' read in prime.rs project_root and main.rs walk_up_config; 'does not compare the version' read in store_line and the plugin arm at 1.2.2; 'within two seconds' read in VERSION_TIMEOUT; 'a project with no bd board gets that line too' measured bd -C <no .beads> --version exit 1 on 1.3.0; the runs-on table's bd row: grep tracker_line finds no caller.

title: adapters is the eighth pack slot, adapters/<kind>/<name>/adapter.toml its entry, and a bare name in [store] adapter resolves through the installed packs
description:
SPEC (fleet-wpf0.2, drafted 2026-09-25). Sites at e416304. Independent of the other children (the built-in "bd" keeps its branch until flight 10).

**Behaviour.** Packs carry adapters, and a bare name in `[store] adapter` resolves to one.

1. `adapters` is the eighth pack slot (pack.rs `SLOTS` 21-29). Its entries are `adapters/<kind>/<name>/`, kind one of `store`, `agent`; each holds `adapter.toml` with `[adapter] name = "<name>"` (must equal the directory), `kind = "store" | "agent"` (must equal the parent), `version = "…"`, `description = "…"` (optional), `entry = "main.ts"` (a file in the directory, executable). `fleet pack check` reports `slot adapters: N entries` and the defects `AdapterWithoutManifest`, `AdapterKind` (an unknown kind directory or a kind key that disagrees), `AdapterEntryMissing`, `AdapterEntryNotExecutable`, `AdapterNameMismatch` (pack.rs `Defect` 135-161, `check_slots` 753-804, `Display` 163-250).
2. The opener (store/mod.rs `open` 409-429) resolves a bare name that is not `bd::NAME` through the layered packs: `resolve::slot_path(resolution, layers, "adapters/store/<name>/adapter.toml")` (resolve.rs 267-271; the highest layer carrying the path wins, defaults last), reads `entry`, checks `executable_file` (460-465), and opens `Exec::at(dir/entry, root)`. `Opening` (380-399) gains the packs: `layers: Option<&[Layer]>`/the `Packs` the doctor module holds (core/src/item/doctor.rs 130-205 shows how a slot is read through `packs.slot`; reuse that type, do not add a second resolver). title: The contract's fences: update takes if_assignee and status open, order.withdraw takes if_assignee, if_status and reopen, moved joins the refusals, show carries description
description:
SPEC (fleet-wpf0.1, drafted 2026-09-25). Folds fleet-j7q (Alberto's ruling of 2026-09-25 on the fenced withdraw and reopen) and adds the two gaps beside it. Sites at e416304.

**Behaviour.** The contract gains what the in-process bd adapter does through trait overrides and nothing else can express:

1. `update` takes an optional fence `if_assignee`: a seat id, or `null` for "unheld"; absent means no fence. A row whose assignee differs refuses `moved` (exit 1) with nothing written. This is `hand_over`'s fence (bd: `--if-assignee`, exit 13, measured 1.3.0 at bd/mod.rs:246, 638).
2. `update` takes an optional `status`, which only takes `"open"`; any other value is usage (exit 2). Same fence. This is the reopen: an item left `in_progress` with nobody holding it comes back to the ready set.
3. `order.withdraw` takes optional `if_assignee` (as above), `if_status` (a Status) and `reopen` (bool, default false). With `reopen: true` the assignee is cleared, the order taken away and the status set to `open` in ONE act; a fence miss refuses `moved` with nothing written (bd: one `update` with `--if-assignee`, `--if-status`, `--assignee ""`, `--unset-metadata fleet.orders`, `--status open`, measured 1.3.0 at bd/mod.rs:722-728).
4. `RefusalReason` gains `moved`; the refusal's `message` names what held the row.
5. `show` answers `description` on the item, and `create` sends it (NewItem already carries it, types.rs:403-414). Exec stops answering `""` (exec.rs:235).

**Sites.** core/src/store/types.rs: Update 427-440 (+ `if_assignee: Option<Option<SeatId>>` with the assignee_out/assignee_in serde at 444-460, + `status: Option<Status>`), Item 355-376 (+ `description: String`, `#[serde(default)]`), RefusalReason 562-570, ITEM_EXAMPLE 686-710, the doc drift test 1101-1225. core/src/store/mod.rs: `moved` 469, `restatused` 479, the in-process Item 43-71. core/src/store/exec.rs: update 262-269, order_withdraw 279-282, show 230-245. core/src/store/bd/mod.rs: update ~614-641 (send `--if-assignee`, `--status`), order_withdraw ~661-700 (the fences and `--status open`), `fenced` at 246. core/src/test_support.rs: update, order_withdraw (739-790), `moving` 239, `held_by` 254, `status_is` 269. core/src/store/conformance.rs: check 15 "order.withdraw clears both" 737, check 22 "fenced writes" 1059; add "fenced update refuses moved", "reopen through update", "fenced withdraw with reopen" (CHECKS 82-106). docs/store.md: Update 237, Item 170, the verbs table 283-299 (`update`, `order.withdraw`), the exit table's refusal example 92, § Orders and runs 349-355.

**Remedy.** Types first with the examples and the doc (docs skill), then Exec, bd and the fake to the same text, then the three conformance checks run against all three. A withdraw with `reopen: true` on a store that cannot do it in one act does not exist here: the fake and bd both can, and the contract page says the act is one.

**Interfaces produced.** `Update { title, assignee, if_assignee, status }`, `Update::fenced(from: Option<SeatId>) -> Update`; `WithdrawFence { if_assignee: Option<Option<SeatId>>, if_status: Option<Status>, reopen: bool }` in types.rs, sent as the verb's optional fields; `RefusalReason::Moved`. fleet-wpf0.4 (the trait) consumes these.

**Acceptance.** The three new checks pass on the fake, on bd through `fleet store check`, and (after fleet-wpf0.7) on the stub; the doc drift test prints every new example; a `status` other than `open` is exit 2 on Exec and refused before any process on bd; `fleet item show` renders the description off an Exec store; fleet-j7q closed as folded here.
notes: Landed 78811ed (squash of 0a59c06 + 0b74ef1, the rebase onto ed1b777; flight 8 wave 2): the contract takes fences — Update gains if_assignee (Option<Option<SeatId>>, null = unheld, absent = no fence) and status (only "open"), Update::fenced(from); WithdrawFence {if_assignee, if_status, reopen} and order_withdraw(id, &WithdrawFence, by) across the trait, Exec, bd and the fake (fleet-wpf0.4 now only deletes hand_over, reopen and order_withdraw_from); RefusalReason::Moved (Exec's exit-1 moved → StoreError::Moved); StoreError::Usage mapped to exit 2 through Stop::usage; store::writable() refuses an update naming no field Unreadable (exit 3) and a status other than open Usage (exit 2) before any process, on Exec, bd and the fake; bd's update sends --if-assignee/--status through fenced (exit 13 → Moved) and order_withdraw sends the fences and --status open in one call; show's description in docs and ITEM_EXAMPLE (kept skip-if-empty); three conformance checks: fenced update refuses moved, reopen through update, fenced withdraw with reopen. Measured on bd 1.3.0 (scratch): --if-assignee "" takes a write on a never-assigned and a cleared item and exits 13 on a held one; --if-status alone exits 13; a holder-fenced --assignee "" --status open reopened an item its holder had closed and bd ready listed it. RED-PROOFs by worktree mutation (the new arms cannot compile on cefd5b1): the derived deserializer for if_assignee turns the null-vs-absent arm red; ignoring held_by in the fake turns the three new checks red; item_json's description arm is a guard (green on base since fleet-run). REVIEW FOCUS (epic): (2) empty and absent assignee read as one against a null fence — covered; (3) a non-open status is exit 2 before any process on Exec and bd — covered. Review calls: accepted changing order_withdraw's signature now; accepted StoreError::Usage (five exhaustive matches, one line each); accepted [ASSUMED] the checks prove reopen from closed (the trait has no in_progress write); accepted Exec::reopen as update {status: open} (was an Unreadable 'no reopen verb'; .4 deletes it). Reconciled at rebase (reviewer's asks): docs/store.md's empty-update line now tells adapter vs fleet apart; fleet-b47's missing classification kept on the fenced path (two new rows in a_write_on_an_item_bd_does_not_hold_is_refused); fleet-pjl's &Actor close and fleet-4qpq's lazy run followed. NEXTEST: .config/nextest.toml's contract-bd override gains its own slow-timeout period 180s × 2, measured on the rebased tree at load 2.6-5.2: every_check_holds_against_bd_too 75.0/70.7/135.9 s, the_bd_adapter_makes_a_scratch_store_every_check_holds_on 78.5/137.6/135.3 s alone, and the contract binary under nextest 168.1 s and 175.2 s. Landing checks at 78811ed: build; core lib 86/86; core store|review|dispatch|hold|deliver|land|retire|contract (both real-bd arms included, under the new period) 254/254; cli item_json|run|store_check 51/51. SEEN NOT FIXED: bd/mod.rs a stray doc paragraph above item_prefix_in belongs to mod opening_tests (the walkthrough's F7 on fleet-alt.1); Refusal always writes "candidates": [], so the doc's moved example carries an empty list. DOCS REVIEW NOTE (docs/store.md at 443494c, 16 claims, 3 run, 0 left out; addendum at 0b74ef1): § What a store is — description on the item (types.rs Item.description); § The exit table — moved (types.rs RefusalReason, exec.rs on_the_record, bd fenced; ran bd update --if-assignee "" and --if-status closed on a held item → exit 13 with the mismatch lines); the moved example (the drift arm); § Item — the example with description (ITEM_EXAMPLE byte-for-byte arm), 'fleet item show prints it' (show.rs, item_json arm), a left-out description reads empty (serde default); § Update — status takes only open (store::writable), if_assignee semantics (types.rs serde, bd update, fake held_by, conformance fenced_update; ran --if-assignee "" on never-assigned and cleared items → exit 0, on held → 13), the examples (drift arm); § Withdrawal fence — fields and defaults (types.rs WithdrawFence), if_status refused as moved (bd order_withdraw, fake status_is, conformance fenced_withdraw), the example (drift arm); § Verbs — update/order.withdraw rows (exec.rs fields sent, on_the_record) and the refused-update story (store::writable, item/mod.rs:81-84, the exit table's usage row); § Orders and runs — reopen:true is one act (bd one argv, the fake one move; ran a holder-fenced --assignee "" --status open on a closed held item → exit 0, open, in bd ready); § Fences — null or left-out assignee meets a null fence (bd holder_of); § Checking an adapter — the output example (ran fleet store check → 25 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped). FINDINGS: none open (the adapter-vs-fleet exit wording resolved at rebase).

title: Flight 8: the store contract complete for an external adapter, the suite hermetic on a stub, a bare adapter name resolved through packs
description:
EPIC — flight 8 of the store side of the adapters design (fleet-notes/adapters-and-sessions.md, brainstormed and ruled 2026-09-25). Sites on the children cite HEAD e416304.

**Goal.** The store contract is complete enough that an EXTERNAL adapter can do everything the in-process bd adapter does today, fleet's own suite runs with no bd on the box, and a bare name in `[store] adapter` resolves through the installed packs. After this flight the Rust bd adapter is still the built-in, patched only enough to keep the suite green: its bd-side work moves to the TypeScript port (flight 9, fleet-packs) and the module is deleted in flight 10.

**Rulings this flight builds under (Alberto, 2026-09-25):**
1. bd leaves core entirely; the only stores left in core are Exec, the fake and the test stub.
2. Adapters ship in packs, in an `adapters/` slot keyed by kind: `adapters/store/<name>/`, `adapters/agent/<name>/`.
3. The bd adapter is TypeScript on Deno, one pack per adapter in the fleet-packs repo (`runtimes/ts`, `tiny`, `adapters/store/bd`, `adapters/agent/…`); `fleet create` asks which store and installs its pack.
4. Contract side first in Rust, bd side in the port: the open contract beads (fleet-run, pjl, b47, urp, 2tp, xpc, z5m, vqre, 4qpq; fleet-j7q folded into the fences child) are children of this epic and land their contract halves here.
5. The suite turns hermetic on a stub adapter over the fake; real bd is tested in fleet-packs.

**Global constraints, every child:**
- `schema_version` stays 1. Every addition to a request is optional and every addition to a response has a default, so an adapter written to today's page still answers.
- Nothing outside `core/src/store/bd/` gains bd knowledge; what leaves the adapter leaves for a pack.
- docs/ changes go through the docs skill, every claim verified; the contract page is docs/store.md.
- Names per brain/naming.md: plain conventional words.
- Measured claims name the version they were measured on.
- Builders never touch .beads/, departure-board.md or the repo's own board; measurements use scratch `bd init` boards.
- Landing checks per the reviewer's practice: the touched suites per landing, the full workspace suite once at the flight's end.

**Sequencing inside the flight.** fleet-run first (the assignee retyping every seam sits on), then the fences child, then the trait, the schema verb, the fake, the stub, the two suite moves, the pack slot and prime's line. The reparented beads are independent of each other except where their own text says.

title: Measure the daemon listing for an interactive Claude Code session under tmux: fields, waiting_for, state vocabulary, scoped config dir
description:
MEASUREMENT, filed 2026-09-24 from the adapters-and-sessions design note (fleet-notes vault): before fleet owns the session under tmux, the design assumes the agent adapter keeps reading Claude Code's own listing (`claude agents --json --all`) for an INTERACTIVE session, minus the short-id address. Lessons B1 says interactive rows are listed with a kind-dependent field set; B8's waiting_for measurement was taken on BACKGROUND sessions only. Nothing has measured an interactive row at the pin.

Measure, at the pinned Claude Code release, an interactive `claude` started inside a tmux session fleet controls:

1. Which listing fields an interactive row carries (id, sessionId, cwd, kind, pid, state, status, name, startedAt, waitingFor), idle and mid-turn.
2. Whether `waitingFor` appears on an interactive row stopped at a permission dialog, and whether it clears when the dialog is answered.
3. Whether the state/status vocabulary matches the background one (working/blocked/done/stopped/failed; idle/busy).
4. Whether a session started under a scoped config directory (CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR) is listed by that directory's daemon when interactive, and not by the default one.
5. Whether the row disappears when the tmux pane is killed, and how fast.

Record as a lessons entry in brain/lessons/claude-code.md (version-scoped, dated, Test field), and note what each answer decides for the adapters-and-sessions design: if waitingFor holds on interactive rows, blocked stays a typed read and the screen is a second source; if not, blocked becomes a screen rule per pin.
notes: Measured 2026-09-24 on Claude Code 2.1.282 and tmux 3.7b, written as lessons B10 and D8 in brain/lessons/claude-code.md (worktree-brain-herdr-comparison, bc6f5f5). All five answered: interactive rows carry status idle/busy/waiting and a typed waitingFor at a dialog, never id or state; a scoped config dir daemon lists them and the default does not; the row vanishes within 1 s of the end with no pid-less row. Unmeasured: a scoped interactive transcript location; whether the swallowed Enter was timing or keysym. See fleet-notes/adapters-and-sessions.md.

title: Routines file items through the store, fleet create reads the item prefix from the adapter, and no file outside the adapter names bd (fleet-0q4 split e2)
description:
SPEC (split e2 of fleet-0q4, drafted 2026-09-23).

**Behaviour.**
- A routine's `[action.item]` files through `store::open`: create, then update for the assignee [ASSUMES D10], with dedupe through list(Label). It no longer runs bd itself.
- The dedupe listing is no longer capped at 50 rows.
- The routine's "filed by routine" note is dropped. created_by is the routine's actor reference [ASSUMES D9].
- The dry run prints the store request, not a bd argv.
- `fleet create --standalone` reads the item prefix from `capabilities().item_prefix` [ASSUMES D11].
- The final grep shows bd only in the adapter, the guard and the fake.

**Sites (at HEAD bde60be)**
- controller/src/routines/action.rs: argv_of :142-170 (item → item_argv("bd", …) at :167); item_argv :241-275; ACTOR :279; file_item :281-399 (resolution :282-288, dedupe :293-338 with no `-n 0`, create :341-367, note :369-386); open_ids :402-415; created_id :420-~440.
- controller/src/routines/file.rs:73-83 Item (priority, assignee).
- controller/tests/routines.rs:1274 (argv_of arm) and cli/tests/drive_routines.rs:209-~300 (file and dedupe on real bd).
- controller/src/lifecycle.rs:28 STORE_CONFIG and :191-199 item_prefix_in; cli/src/lifecycle.rs:172-174.
- cli/src/status.rs:309-313 (comment).

**Remedy**
1. file_item:
   - `let policy = fleet_core::store::project_policy(&routine.project_root)`; an error is Done(CouldNotTell, <text>);
   - `open(&Opening{root: &routine.project_root, policy: &policy, search_path: &path_for_children(machine.child_path), strict: true, timeout: Duration::from_secs(routine.timeout)})`; an error is Done(CouldNotTell, "the store could not be opened: <e>");
   - by = the routine's actor reference (iex-d's `Actor` of kind routine, id the routine's name);
   - dedupe "open": `list(&Filter::Label(label))`. Err is CouldNotTell "the dedupe query could not be read: <e>". Non-empty is Deduped with the same detail and `existing`;
   - `create(&NewItem{title, description: description.unwrap_or_default(), item_type: kind.unwrap_or("task"), labels (with the routine label), priority})`. Err is Failed "the create did not land: <e>". The "task" default is today's bd default made explicit; check bd's default type on 1.3.0 and use it;
   - when assignee is Some: resolve it to a SeatId with iex-a's seat resolver, then `update(&id, &Update::assignee(seat), &by)`. An unresolvable name is Failed "the routine's assignee `<x>` names no seat of this fleet — <id> was filed unassigned". An update error is Failed "<id> was filed, and its assignee did not land: <e>";
   - Filed "filed <id>" with extra item;
   - delete ACTOR (if iex-d did not), item_argv, open_ids, created_id and the note [ASSUMES D9].
2. argv_of for an item returns `vec!["store", "create", <the create request JSON, one line, from types::request minus root>]`.
3. controller/src/lifecycle.rs: delete STORE_CONFIG and item_prefix_in. Move the latter into core/src/store/bd/mod.rs as the reader behind `Bd::capabilities().item_prefix`: read `<root>/.beads/config.yaml` and take `issue-prefix:`; unreadable means None.
4. cli/src/lifecycle.rs:172-174: `store::open(&Opening{root: &root, policy: &project_policy(&root)?, search_path: &child_path(home), strict: false, timeout: STORE_TIMEOUT})`, then `.capabilities().ok().and_then(|c| c.item_prefix)`.
5. cli/src/status.rs:311: the comment becomes "…a hold raised or cleared by hand, outside fleet, wrote no line here, and the store's own open-hold listing is the one that sees those".
6. File a finding for the routine vocabulary (controller/src/routines/file.rs:177 ITEM_TYPES and the 0–4 range, F14), not fixed here.

**Acceptance**
1. The FINAL GREP is empty (list any BEADS_ACTOR hit left for iex-d on the bead):
   - `git grep -n -i -w -E 'bd|beads' core/src cli/src controller/src ':!core/src/store/bd' ':!core/src/guard' ':!core/src/test_support.rs'`;
   - `git grep -n '\.beads' core/src cli/src controller/src ':!core/src/store/bd' ':!core/src/test_support.rs'`.
2. cli/tests/drive_routines.rs:209 arm, re-pointed: it files once, and the next firing dedupes. It checks the label through `fleet`, not a bd listing. (Keep one bd listing as the real-store witness: tests may name bd.)
3. New arm: a routine with assignee "builder-1" (a seat in the rig) files and the item reads that seat's id as assignee. An unknown assignee gives outcome failed with "names no seat of this fleet", and the item exists unassigned.
4. The controller/tests/routines.rs:1274 sibling arm for an item action asserts argv_of == ["store","create",<json>]. (Red-proof: today's first word is "bd".)
5. cli/tests/lifecycle.rs: a standalone create beside a `.beads/config.yaml` carrying `issue-prefix: zz` writes `item_prefix = "zz"`, and without the file writes the commented line. These are existing arms re-pointed, and must stay green.
6. New arm: a dedupe past 50 open items carrying the label is still Deduped. (Red-proof: with today's unbounded bd list, row 51+ is missed. Assert against a board seeded with 51.)

Gate line: touched suites green; the reviewer runs the full suite, ran or cached, at landing.
Size estimate: ~350 changed lines.
SPEC'D to the zero-clarification bar.

DECISIONS APPLIED (walkthrough fleet-alt.1 spec pass, 2026-09-24). Drafted read-only at bde60be, BEFORE flight 4 landed (fleet-6gr: gate→hold/clear, `fleet hold`/`fleet clear`, [gates] split into [landing]/[permissions]/[guards.targets], routines evaluate the trigger; fleet-4j6: fleet.orders / fleet.run with v:1, label fleet:run; fleet-g68: PRD citations restated, PRDs archived; fleet-d11: dead flight code deleted). Every site cited here is RE-FOUND BY SYMBOL at pickup, and names from those beads are the landed ones. title: fleet store check [--adapter <path>]: the conformance suite against an adapter on a scratch store it makes (fleet-0q4 split d2)
description:
SPEC (split d2 of fleet-0q4, drafted 2026-09-23). **Behaviour.** - `fleet store check` runs every conformance check against an adapter. - The adapter is either the one this project selects (built-in bd when outside a project or when nothing is set), or `--adapter `. - The checks run on a scratch store the adapter makes inside a temp dir fleet creates and always removes. - It answers with the exit table: 0 every check passed or was skipped; 1 a check failed, or the adapter declares no scratch; 2 usage; 3 the adapter could not be run or could not answer capabilities. **Sites (at HEAD bde60be)** - cli/src/main.rs: the Family enum :61-~300 (the Routine arm :118-121 is the model); dispatch :570-571. - cli/src/routines.rs:1-80, the family-module pattern. - cli/src/exit.rs. - core/src/store/conformance.rs (d1). - core/src/store/mod.rs: open, Opening, project_policy (c2). - docs/store.md §9 and its Status line. **Remedy** 1. cli/src/store.rs (new family module): - `#[derive(clap::Subcommand)] pub enum Verb { Check { #[arg(long, value_name = "PATH")] adapter: Option } }`; - help `/// run the store contract's conformance suite against an adapter`; - long_about: ``` run every check of the store contract (docs/store.md) against an adapter, on a scratch store the adapter makes through its `scratch` verb and fleet removes after. Without --adapter it checks the adapter this project selects ([store] adapter, else the built-in bd). Exits 0 when every check passes, 1 when one fails or the adapter declares no scratch, 2 on usage, 3 when the adapter could not be run. ``` - --adapter help: "an absolute path to an adapter executable, checked instead of this project's". 2. main.rs: - `/// the work-graph store this project reads and writes` with `Store { #[command(subcommand)] verb: store::Verb }`; - the dispatch arm is `Family::Store { verb } => Ok(store::command(&verb))`. 3. `store::command`: 1. A relative --adapter makes stderr print "fleet store check: --adapter takes an absolute path to an executable, and `

` is not one", exit 2. 2. Pick the policy table: - with --adapter: `{store: {adapter:

}}`; - without: resolve_at(None). On Ok use here.project.gates; on Err use an empty table (bd). 3. Make `/fleet-store-check--` and `<…>/absent` (both empty). 4. Open with `Opening{root:

, …, strict: true, timeout: STORE_TIMEOUT}`. An open error: print it and exit 3. 5. capabilities(): an error is exit 3. `scratch == false` makes stderr print "fleet store check: declares no scratch capability, and the check runs only on a store it makes for the purpose — nothing was run", exit 1. 6. scratch(/store): an error is exit 3. Open again at the answered root, and open `absent` at /absent. 7. conformance::run. On stdout print one line per check: `PASS `, `SKIP : `, or `FAIL : `. Then `store check: —

passed, failed, skipped`. 8. Remove

recursively in every branch after step 3, including on a panic, using a drop guard. 9. Exit 0 when f == 0, else 1. 4. docs/store.md: §9 describes the command, and the Status line becomes "The contract is live." **Acceptance.** New arms in cli/tests/store_check.rs. 1. `fleet store check` in a scratch project with no [store] runs the built-in bd: exit 0, every line PASS or SKIP, and the temp dir is gone afterwards. (Red-proof: a runner that stops at the first failure prints one FAIL line; the arm asserts FAIL lines for "create then show" and "holds".) 4. `--adapter relative/path`: exit 2. 5. `--adapter /nonexistent`: exit 3, naming the path. title: The external store client: one process per call, JSON on stdin and stdout, fleet's exit table, the 60s bound (fleet-0q4 split c1)
description:
SPEC (split c1 of fleet-0q4, drafted 2026-09-23).

**Behaviour.** `Exec`, a Store over an adapter executable:
- Each trait call is one `<adapter> <verb>` process. It carries the docs/store.md request on stdin [ASSUMES D4] and reads the response on stdout.
- It maps the exit code through the contract's table, and carries stderr's last line into every refusal.
- It is bounded by STORE_TIMEOUT with a process-group kill, and requires schema_version 1 [ASSUMES D15].
- Nothing selects it yet (c2 does).

**Sites (at HEAD bde60be)**
- core/src/process.rs: spawn_in_group :109-126 (stdin null at :110), run_bounded :190-251, deadline_cause :78.
- The write-suffix wording to reuse is at core/src/store.rs:313-318 (bd/mod.rs after b1).
- The ambiguity wording at store.rs:484-486.
- tail() at :402-416.
- core/src/store/types.rs (a1) holds request, answer and the response bodies.

**Remedy**
1. core/src/process.rs:
   - spawn_in_group takes `stdin: Stdio`, and run_bounded passes Stdio::null() (unchanged behaviour);
   - add `pub fn run_bounded_fed(cmd: Command, input: Vec<u8>, timeout: Duration) -> Result<Output, String>`. It is the same as run_bounded, except stdin is piped and a detached thread writes input and then drops the pipe (a broken pipe is ignored). The deadline covers the whole call.
2. core/src/store/exec.rs:
   - `pub struct Exec { adapter: PathBuf, root: PathBuf, timeout: Duration }`, with `Exec::at(adapter: &Path, root: &Path) -> Exec` (timeout = STORE_TIMEOUT) and `with_timeout(Duration)`;
   - `const WRITES: [&str; 9] = ["create","update","append","order.set","order.withdraw","run.set","hold.raise","hold.clear","close"];`.
   - `fn call<T: DeserializeOwned>(&self, verb: &str, fields: Map) -> Result<(T, String), StoreError>` answers the body and the raw stdout. It runs `Command::new(adapter).arg(verb)` (cwd is inherited and never relied on) through run_bounded_fed with `types::request(fields, &root)`, then maps:
     - spawn failure: Unreadable("`<adapter>` could not be run (<why>) — nothing was written");
     - deadline: Unreadable("`<adapter> <verb>` did not answer within 60s"), plus, when verb ∈ WRITES, " — the write's effect cannot be told, so the item must be read before anything is written to it again";
     - exit 0: `types::answer::<T>(stdout)`; an error is Unreadable("`<adapter> <verb>` answered no readable response: <why>");
     - exit 1: decode {"refused": Refusal} into Refused(text):
       - missing: "<id> is not in the store";
       - ambiguous: "`<id>` matches more than one item — <c1, c2, …> — and more of the id says which one this is";
       - already: the Refusal's message;
       - an undecodable exit-1 body: Unreadable("`<adapter> <verb>` refused with no readable refusal: <tail>");
     - exit 2: Unreadable("`<adapter> <verb>` refused the request as usage (exit 2) — this fleet and the adapter do not speak the same store contract: <tail>");
     - exit 3: Unreadable("`<adapter> <verb>` could not tell: <error field, else tail>");
     - any other code: Unreadable("`<adapter> <verb>` exited <n>, which is not a row of the store contract's exit table: <tail>");
     - a signal: "… was ended by a signal: <tail>".
     
     Every Refused and Unreadable text above ends with " (the adapter said: <tail>)" when stderr has a non-blank line and the text does not already carry that tail. tail() moves to core/src/store/mod.rs as a crate-private helper shared by bd and exec.
   - `impl Store for Exec`: each method builds its verb's fields exactly as docs/store.md §7 says.
     - show sets `item.proof = ReadProof::of(raw stdout)` [ASSUMES D5].
     - export and scratch call their verbs only when `capabilities().scratch` or `.export` is declared, and otherwise answer Unreadable("the adapter declares no <verb>").

**Acceptance.** Unit arms in core/src/store/exec.rs, each over a `#!/bin/sh` stub written to a temp dir. The stub copies stdin to request.json and prints a canned answer.
1. show: the stub's recorded request has schema_version 1, the root and the id; the answer decodes to Item; argv[1] == "show".
2. exit 1 ambiguous gives Refused naming both candidates; exit 1 missing gives Refused "<id> is not in the store".
3. exit 2 gives Unreadable naming "usage (exit 2)"; exit 3 gives Unreadable carrying the error; exit 7 gives "not a row".
4. A response with no schema_version, or with 2, gives Unreadable. (Red-proof: skip the version check and see this arm red.)
5. The stub sleeps 5 with with_timeout(1s): Unreadable within 1s + DRAIN_GRACE, and the stub's pid (written to a file) is gone (`kill -0` fails). The same arm with verb update carries the write suffix.
6. Stderr "boom" on exit 3 appears in the text.
7. run_bounded_fed: an arm in process.rs where `cat` echoes a 1 MiB input whole, and run_bounded's own arms stay green.

Gate line: touched suites green; the reviewer runs the full suite, ran or cached, at landing.
Size estimate: ~450 changed lines (exec ~250, process ~40, tests ~160).

title: Order, run and hold writes speak the contract, and their storage shapes move behind the bd adapter (fleet-0q4 split b5)
description:
SPEC (split b5 of fleet-0q4, drafted 2026-09-23).

**Behaviour.**
- set_orders, unset_orders and withdraw_order become `order_set` and `order_withdraw` over a typed Order.
- set_metadata becomes `run_set` over a RunRecord [ASSUMES D2].
- Holds use the HoldId type.
- append and timeline take ItemId.
- The trait becomes the contract's in-process form, verb for verb, and `note` is deleted.
- The bd storage payloads leave the verbs and are built inside the adapter: dispatch.rs `index()` builds a bd metadata object today, and run.rs builds `{"run": …}`.
- order_withdraw clears the assignee and the index in one act.

**Sites (at HEAD bde60be; re-find by symbol after 4j6, zlk-2 and 6gr-1)**

- Bd's same methods (HEAD :695-758).
- dispatch.rs:
  - index_payload and index (:523-543, the storage shape);
  - write_order :500-518 (set_orders);
  - withdraw :437-461 (unset_orders).
- run.rs write_the_pins :1175-1199 (set_metadata and payload).
- seat/retire.rs:62 (withdraw_order).
- gate.rs / hold.rs: callers of gate, open_gates and resolve_gate (HEAD gate.rs:181-195, :418-430, :537-552, :670-690).

   - `fn order_set(&self, id: &ItemId, order: &Order, by: &Actor) -> Result<(), StoreError>`;
   - `fn order_withdraw(&self, id: &ItemId, by: &Actor) -> Result<(), StoreError>`, with no default body: every implementation clears both in one act;
   - `fn run_set(&self, id: &ItemId, run: &RunRecord, by: &Actor)`;
   - `fn hold_raise(&self, id: &ItemId, reason: &str, by: &Actor) -> Result<HoldId, StoreError>`, `fn hold_clear(&self, hold: &HoldId, by: &Actor)` and `fn holds_open(&self) -> Result<Vec<HoldId>, StoreError>` (renaming 6gr-1's hold, clear_hold and open_holds);

title: docs/store.md: the store contract an adapter implements (fleet-0q4 split a2)
description:
SPEC (split a2 of fleet-0q4, drafted 2026-09-23).

**Behaviour.** A user-facing contract doc, written with the docs skill (every behaviour claim verified, citations on the bead). It states the verbs, the JSON, the semantics and the exit table. It carries a Status line saying which parts are live. 0q4-c2 and 0q4-d2 each update that line when [store] adapter and `fleet store check` land.

**Sites (at HEAD bde60be)**
- docs/ has no store.md.
- docs/README.md is the index.
- core/src/store/types.rs is 0q4-a1's.
- cli/src/exit.rs:10-40 is the exit table.
- core/src/store.rs:554-562 BLOCKING, and fleet-5y5's ready rule.
- core/src/store.rs:150-155 is the fragment rule, measured: whole id, then whole hash, then substring of a hash.
- core/src/store.rs:181-191 is the one-writer-per-key rule.
- brain/fleet-layers.md:601-610 has the Q1 and Q2 rulings.

**Remedy**
1. Write docs/store.md with these sections, in this order.
   1. **What a store is.** The work graph fleet reads and writes. bd is built in. Any other store is an executable named by `[store] adapter`.
      - Status line: "The contract is being built (fleet-0q4). `[store] adapter` and `fleet store check` are not yet available."
   2. **Choosing an adapter.** `[store] adapter = "bd"` is the default, and absent means bd; the other form is an absolute path to an executable. The key lives in the project's own file: fleet.toml for an embedded fleet, .fleet/project.toml for a standalone project [ASSUMES D12].
   3. **The call.**
      - `<adapter> <verb>`, one process per call. The request is one JSON object on stdin, the response is one JSON object on stdout, and stderr is for people.
      - fleet carries the last non-blank stderr line (160 characters) into every refusal it prints.
      - Each call is bounded at 60 seconds. On expiry fleet kills the adapter's process group and reads the call as could not tell. For a write, fleet also says the write's effect cannot be told.
   4. **The envelope.** Every request carries "schema_version": 1 and "root" (the absolute project root) [ASSUMES D4]. Every response carries "schema_version": 1. fleet reads any other value, or a missing one, as could not tell [ASSUMES D15].
   5. **The exit table.**
      - 0 answered.
      - 1 refused on the record, with {"schema_version":1,"refused":{"reason":"missing"|"ambiguous"|"already","message":…,"candidates":[…]}}.
      - 2 usage: an unknown verb, a malformed request, a schema_version the adapter does not speak, or a capability verb it does not declare.
      - 3 could not tell, optionally with {"schema_version":1,"error":…}.
      - Any other code, or death by signal, is read as 3.
   6. **Types.** Each a1 type as a JSON example. The Item example is the one a1's test holds.
   7. **Verbs.** For each verb: request fields beyond the envelope, response fields, and exit-1 reasons.

      | verb | request | response | exit 1 |
      |---|---|---|---|
      | version | {} | {name, version} | — |
      | capabilities | {} | {export: {file, dir} \| null, scratch: bool, item_prefix: string \| null} [ASSUMES D11] | — |
      | resolve | {id: text} | {id} | missing, ambiguous (with candidates) |
      | show | {id: text} | {item} | missing, ambiguous. Resolves exactly as resolve does [ASSUMES D16] |
      | list | {filter} | {items: [ItemSummary]} | — |
      | timeline | {id} | {entries: [Entry]}, in append order | missing |
      | create | {item: NewItem, by} | {id} | — |
      | update | {id, by, title?, assignee?} | {} | missing. Neither key present is usage |
      | append | {id, by, entry} | {entry: entry id} | missing |
      | order.set | {id, by, order} | {} | missing |
      | order.withdraw | {id, by} | {} | missing |
      | run.set | {id, by, run} | {} | missing [ASSUMES D2] |
      | hold.raise | {id, by, reason} | {hold} | missing |
      | hold.clear | {hold, by} | {} | missing, already |
      | holds.open | {} | {holds: [hold id]} | — |
      | close | {id, by, reason} | {} | missing, already |
      | export (only when declared) | {into: absolute dir} | {file: absolute path written} | — |
      | scratch (only when declared) | {into: absolute empty dir fleet made} | {root: the absolute root to address the new store with} | — |
   8. **Semantics.**
      - ready: open; not blocked by an open item the store counts as having to finish first; not held. It is UNORDERED.
      - label: open and carrying the label.
      - assignee: every item assigned to the seat, whatever its status.
      - The fragment rule: the whole id; else the one id whose part after its prefix is the text; else the ids whose part after the prefix contains the text. More than one match at the first rule that matches anything is ambiguous. An adapter whose ids carry no prefix treats the whole id as that part.
      - order.set replaces the item's order whole and touches neither the assignee nor the run record. run.set likewise never touches the order.
      - order.withdraw clears the assignee AND the order in one act. After any exit, an item never has the assignee cleared while the order stands.
      - The timeline is append-only. Entries come back in append order with distinct ids, and the store sets each entry's id and time.
      - hold.raise takes the item out of ready until the hold is cleared. hold.clear of a cleared hold is 1 already. holds.open answers ids only.
      - close of a closed item is 1 already.
      - export regenerates that one file under into, and makes the directories it needs.
      - scratch makes a new, empty store inside into and never touches a store outside it.
   9. **Checking an adapter.** `fleet store check [--adapter <path>]` (arrives with 0q4-d2).
2. Add a docs/README.md index row: "store.md — the store contract an adapter implements".
3. Add a drift arm to core/src/store/types.rs tests: read `concat!(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"), "/../docs/store.md")` and assert that every JSON example const from a1's tests appears verbatim.

**Acceptance**

2. `git grep -n -i -w -E 'bd|beads' docs/store.md` hits only §1, §2 and the capability example ("bd is built in"; `adapter = "bd"`; the export example `.beads/issues.jsonl`), and each hit is listed on the bead.

title: Store contract types in core: ids, Status, Order, OrderState, Item, ItemSummary, Filter, Update, Capabilities and the envelope (fleet-0q4 split a1)
description:
SPEC (split a1 of fleet-0q4, drafted 2026-09-23).

**Behaviour.** No runtime change. This bead adds the store contract's domain types to core, with serde derives whose JSON is exactly what docs/store.md (0q4-a2) documents and what the external protocol (0q4-c1) sends. Only their own tests use them until 0q4-b2..b5 move the trait onto them.

**Sites (at HEAD bde60be)**
- core/src/store.rs:47-83: Item today has status: String, orders + has_orders_key, notes, run: Option<serde_json::Value>, and document: String.
- core/src/store.rs:97-105: Orders is four Option<String> fields.
- core/src/store.rs:107-123: AssignedItem.
- core/src/store.rs:85-95: NewItem, which is borrowed.
- core/src/store.rs:125-143: StoreError.
- core/src/item/dispatch.rs:31: KIND "dispatch".
- core/src/item/run.rs:1181-1189: the run object's keys hash, workflow, pack, entry, started_at.
- controller/src/clock.rs:89-99: the stamp form YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ.
- core/src/store.rs:472-509: fleet-998's ambiguity wording.
- The workspace serde has "derive" (Cargo.toml:39). core derives nothing today.

**Remedy**

0. Preconditions. If any of these fails, stop and say so on this bead:
   - `git grep -n 'pub struct SeatId' core/src` hits.
   - `git grep -n -E 'pub (enum|struct) Actor' core/src` hits [ASSUMES D1].
   - `git grep -n -E 'pub (enum|struct) Entry' core/src` hits. Call zlk-1's unsaved-entry type EntryDraft below, and use zlk-1's actual name.
1. Layout.
   - If core/src/store.rs is a file, `git mv core/src/store.rs core/src/store/mod.rs` with no content change. If fleet-xie already made core/src/store/, leave it.
   - Add `pub mod types;` to core/src/store/mod.rs. Do NOT re-export: the old Item/Orders names stay until 0q4-b2.
2. Create core/src/store/types.rs with exactly these items.
   - `pub const CONTRACT_VERSION: u64 = 1;`
   - `ItemId(String)` and `HoldId(String)`:
     - derives: Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, PartialOrd, Ord, Default, Serialize, Deserialize, with #[serde(transparent)];
     - `new(impl Into<String>)` and `as_str()`;
     - impl Display, `Deref<Target=str>`, `From<&str>`, `From<String>`, `PartialEq<str>`, `PartialEq<&str>`, `PartialEq<String>`.
   - `Status { Open, InProgress, Closed, Other(String) }`:
     - #[serde(from = "String", into = "String")];
     - "open", "in_progress" and "closed" map to the named variants; any other text maps to Other(text) verbatim;
     - `as_str()`, `From<&str>`, `PartialEq<&str>` and `PartialEq<str>` compare as_str();
     - Default is Other(String::new()), which keeps today's Item::default() status "".
   - `Stamp(String)`:
     - #[serde(try_from = "String", into = "String")];
     - `Stamp::parse(&str) -> Option<Stamp>` accepts exactly the 20-character form YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ, with month 01-12, day 01-31, hour 00-23, and minute and second 00-59;
     - the TryFrom error text is "`<text>` is not a stamp — the form is YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ".
     - If zlk-1 landed a stamp type (its landing note names one), use that instead and skip this item.
   - `OrderKind { Dispatch, Review }`, with #[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")].
   - `Order { kind: OrderKind, by: Actor, seat: Option<SeatId>, at: Stamp }`, with #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]; seat uses #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")].
   - `OrderState { None, Unreadable, Ordered(Order) }`:
     - #[serde(tag = "state", content = "order", rename_all = "snake_case")], Default None;
     - JSON is exactly {"state":"none"}, {"state":"unreadable"} or {"state":"ordered","order":{…}}.
   - `RunRecord { hash: String, workflow: String, pack: String, entry: String, started_at: Stamp }`, with deny_unknown_fields [ASSUMES D2].
   - `ReadProof(String)`, with Debug, Clone, Default, PartialEq, Eq and no serde; `of(impl Into<String>)` and `carries(&self, token: &str) -> bool` [ASSUMES D5].
   - `Item`:
     - fields: `{ id: ItemId, title: String, status: Status, #[serde(rename="type")] item_type: String, #[serde(default)] labels: Vec<String>, #[serde(default)] assignee: Option<SeatId>, #[serde(default)] order: OrderState, #[serde(default)] blockers: Vec<ItemId>, #[serde(default)] run: Option<RunRecord>, #[serde(skip)] proof: ReadProof }`;
     - derives Debug, Clone, Default, PartialEq, Eq.
   - `ItemSummary { id: ItemId, title: String, status: Status, #[serde(rename="type")] item_type: String [ASSUMES D3], #[serde(default)] labels: Vec<String>, #[serde(default)] order: OrderState }`.
   - `Filter { Ready, Label(String), Assignee(SeatId) }`, with #[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]; JSON is "ready", {"label":"L"} or {"assignee":"<seat id>"}.
   - `NewItem`:
     - fields: `{ title: String, description: String, #[serde(rename="type")] item_type: String, #[serde(default)] labels: Vec<String>, #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if="Option::is_none")] priority: Option<u8> }` [ASSUMES D10];
     - `NewItem::validate()` refuses priority > 4 with "priority is <n>; the range is 0 to 4".
   - `Update { title: Option<String>, assignee: Option<Option<SeatId>> }`:
     - a key that is absent means untouched; "assignee": null means cleared;
     - use a hand-written serialize_with/deserialize_with pair in types.rs, no new crate, so that null and absent stay distinct;
     - constructors `Update::title(String)`, `Update::assignee(SeatId)`, `Update::unassigned()`, and `is_empty()`.
   - `Capabilities { #[serde(default)] export: Option<ExportSpec>, #[serde(default)] scratch: bool, #[serde(default)] item_prefix: Option<String> }` [ASSUMES D11].
   - `ExportSpec { file: String, dir: String }`:
     - both are relative and '/'-separated; dir ends in '/'; file starts with dir;
     - `validate()` refuses an absolute path, a `..` segment, or a file not under dir. The text names the field and the value.
   - `Version { name: String, version: String }`.
   - `Refusal { reason: RefusalReason, message: String, #[serde(default)] candidates: Vec<ItemId> }` and `RefusalReason { Missing, Ambiguous, Already }` (snake_case).
   - Per-verb response bodies:
     - `Resolved{id}`, `Shown{item}`, `Listed{items}`, `Created{id}`, `Appended{entry: EntryId}`, `Raised{hold}`, `OpenHolds{holds}`, `Exported{file: String}`, `Scratched{root: String}`, `Answered{}`;
     - `Timeline{entries: Vec<Entry>}` is defined only if zlk-1 did not define it.
   - `pub fn request(verb_fields: serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value>, root: &Path) -> serde_json::Value` inserts "schema_version": CONTRACT_VERSION and "root": root.display() [ASSUMES D4].
   - `pub fn answer<T: DeserializeOwned>(text: &str) -> Result<T, String>`:
     - decodes the FIRST JSON value (the same rule as today's first_value, store.rs:419);
     - the value must be an object;
     - schema_version must be exactly 1, else the error is "answered schema_version <v>; this fleet speaks 1", or "answered no schema_version" when missing [ASSUMES D15];
     - T is decoded from the object with schema_version removed.
   - Doc comment on every type: one sentence on what it is in fleet's terms. No bd vocabulary: `git grep -n -i -w -E 'bd|beads' core/src/store/types.rs` must be empty.

**Acceptance.** All arms are unit tests in core/src/store/types.rs.
1. Status round-trips "open", "in_progress" and "closed" to their variants and back. "deferred" becomes Other("deferred") and serializes to "deferred". `Status::from("open") == "open"` holds.
2. OrderState serializes to exactly the three JSON strings above. An Order without seat omits the key. An Order with an unknown key fails to decode.
3. Stamp::parse accepts "2026-09-23T10:00:00Z" and refuses "then", "2026-13-01T00:00:00Z" and "2026-09-23 10:00:00Z". (Red-proof: a parse that only checks length passes "2026-13…"; show that red first.)

title: zlk-3: fleet status counts open holds off every registered project's store, not the stream
description:
SPEC (split 3 of fleet-zlk, drafted 2026-09-23).
Names: (the shared names line above.)

Behaviour.
- Status's hold count and a parked run's ", cleared" read the STORE's open holds, which is the adapter's open_holds. At HEAD they are a fold of the stream's park and resolution lines (status.rs:308-331), which misses a hold raised or cleared on another machine or by hand.
- Status is machine-level: runs span projects. So it asks each project this machine registers, as the run pass's Engine does (cli/src/runs.rs:91-107).
- A store that will not answer is named, and the exit is 3, as status does for every unread instrument.

Sites (at HEAD bde60be):
- cli/src/status.rs:
  - :275-306, RunsRead: `gates` becomes `holds: Result<BTreeSet<String>, String>`, read by `open_holds_on(machine_dir)`;
  - :308-331, standing_gates: delete;
  - :515-583, runs_section's last line;
  - :585-600, run_row's ", answered";
  - :156-175, Read::unread includes the holds error.
- cli/src/runs.rs:91-107: `fn projects(&self)` becomes `pub(crate) fn registered_roots(machine_dir: &Path) -> Vec<PathBuf>`, used by both.
- Tests: cli/tests/status.rs.

Remedy:
1. `open_holds_on(machine_dir)`: for each registered root, `resolve_from(&root, machine_dir, None)`. A root that does not resolve is skipped, as Engine does. Then `open_store(&here.project.root).open_holds()`, taking the union. The first Err(e) answers Err(format!("the holds were not counted — {root}'s store did not answer: {e}")).
2. The line becomes `holds  {n} open`. A failed read prints `holds  not counted — {why}`.
3. run_row prints `PARKED at {stamp} on hold {hold}{, cleared}`, where ", cleared" means the hold is not in the open set. The hold still comes from Reading.gate (6gr: hold) until 4b.

Acceptance:
1. cli/tests/status.rs (binary, bd scratch project registered on the machine): two holds raised through `fleet hold`, one cleared by `bd gate resolve` BY HAND (no stream line) → the page says `holds  1 open`.
   RED-PROOF: HEAD counts 2, because the stream never saw the hand clear.
2. A registered project whose bd cannot run → `holds  not counted — …`, exit 3.
3. A parked run whose hold was cleared by hand → the row reads ", cleared".
Gate line: touched suites green; the reviewer runs the full suite, ran or cached, at landing.
Closes: none of the held list. It makes status's hold count the store's.
Size estimate: ~250 lines.

title: zlk-2b-i: `fleet deliver --delivery <file.json>` — the seat hands in JSON validated before any write, and `--item` checks the holder
description:
SPEC (split 2b-i of fleet-zlk, drafted 2026-09-23).
Names: (the shared names line above.)

Behaviour.
- deliver reads a JSON delivery file (1c's DeliveryInput) and refuses exit 2 before ANY write when it does not parse or validate. That is before the commit, the reassignment and the store.
- Until 2b-ii writes the entry, the verb renders the delivery note from the JSON itself, with every continuation line indented off column zero, so the note readers (review, land) keep working. The seat never writes prose, so fleet-4rl's second column-zero marker cannot occur.
- The brief shows the delivery schema in place of the delivery-note grammar. The tiny pack teaches the JSON.
- `--item` gains the holder check (fleet-pl6 (a)), in held_item, which fleet hold shares:
  - a run's own record is held by that run;
  - any other item is held by the seat that is its assignee and whose fleet.orders stands;
  - a non-seat actor is refused by kind (fleet-iex R3).

   - (b) `input::read` (exit 2 on any failure; nothing is written);

   - (f) the rendered note;

2. transitional_note renders exactly these lines. Every value's embedded newline becomes "\n  ".
   - `DELIVERED {commit} — {by}`
   - `commit:  {commit}`
   - `branch:  {branch}`
   - `base:    origin/main at {base}, read at {at}`
   - `files:   {files joined ", "}`
   - `checks:  {check}: {result}; …`, or `checks:  none`
   - `suite:   {command}, rc {rc}`, or `suite:   NOT TESTED — {not_tested}`
   - `spec corrections: {n} — {premise} — refuted by {refuted_by}; …`, or `spec corrections: none`
   - `not proven: {surface} — {command}; …`
   - `decisions: {n}` (or `decisions: none`), then per decision `  D{k} {call}; not taken: {not_taken}; because {because}`

title: zlk-1d: `fleet item show <id> [--json]` renders an item and its timeline, and the brief carries that rendering instead of bd's
description:
SPEC (split 1d of fleet-zlk, drafted 2026-09-23).
Names: (the shared names line above.)

Behaviour.
- Presentation is the viewer's (ruling R4). `fleet item show <id>` prints an item's fields and its timeline, one block per entry. `--json` prints one envelope whose data is the item and its timeline.
- It is the SDK's one read of the store from 4a on. It lands BEFORE any writer appends an entry, so a person has a viewer the moment notes stop.
- The brief's `{item}` becomes this rendering. At HEAD it is bd's own `-q show` text (Store::show_text), and measured on bd 1.3.0 that text prints every comment under a COMMENTS header. So the first entry any verb appended would reach every brief as raw JSON.
- Item gains `description`.

Sites (at HEAD bde60be):
- core/src/store.rs:53-83 (Item): add `pub description: String`. :802-828 (item_from): `description: text_field(row, "description").unwrap_or_default()`.
- core/src/test_support.rs: create (≈:421-460) keeps `item.description`; row_of (≈:296) writes "description" when it is non-empty.
- core/src/item/mod.rs:12-21: add `pub mod show;`. core/src/item/show.rs (new).
- core/src/item/brief.rs:113-128 (Subject.text doc) and :242 (`store.show_text(item)?`): the text becomes `show::render(&record, &store.timeline(&record.id)?)`.
- core/src/item/dispatch.rs:659-663 (write_brief's show_text): `store.show(order.item)` plus `timeline`, then render.
- cli/src/main.rs:11-24 (mods): add `mod item_show;`. :61-? (enum Family): add `Item { #[command(subcommand)] verb: item_show::Verb }` with doc "/// read one item: its fields and its timeline". The arms at :564-584 gain `Family::Item { verb } => Ok(item_show::command(&verb))`.
- cli/src/item_show.rs (new).
- core/defaults/assets/brief.md:30-34 ("## The item"): the placeholder is unchanged; the sentence at :21-22 says the item is the record and this block is fleet's rendering of it.

Remedy:
1. `show::render(item: &Item, timeline: &[Entry]) -> String`, exactly:
   - line 1: `{id} · {title}  [{status}]`
   - line 2: `type {item_type} · labels {labels joined ", " or "none"} · assignee {assignee or "none"}`
   - line 3: `order {kind} by {by} at {at}, seat {seat or "not yet named"}` from `item.orders` (the fleet.orders index); `order none` when the key is absent; `order unreadable` when has_orders_key and orders is None
   - `blocked by {ids joined ", "}` only when blockers is non-empty
   - a blank line, then the description as it is, or `(no description)`
   - a blank line, then `timeline ({n} entries)`, or `timeline (no entries)`
   - then, per entry, `{at}  {by}  {summary}` and its detail lines indented 4 spaces (`show::entry_lines(&Entry) -> Vec<String>`).
   Summaries and details per kind:
   - ordered: `ordered {order} → {seat or "a transient seat, not yet named"}`.
   - order_withdrawn: `order withdrawn ({why}){, seat S}{: cause}`.
   - delivered: `delivered {commit} on {branch}, base {base}`. Details:
     - `files: a, b`;
     - `checks:` then `- {check}: {result}`, or `checks: none`;
     - `suite: {command}, rc {rc}`, or `suite: NOT TESTED — {not_tested}`;
     - `spec corrections: none`, or `- {premise} — refuted by {refuted_by}`;
     - `not proven:` then `- {surface} — {command}`;
     - `decisions: none`, or `D{k} {call}; not taken: {not_taken}; because {because}`;
     - `covers: none`, or `covers: a, b`.
   - reviewed: `accepted {commit}`, or `returned {commit} with {n} finding(s)`. Details:
     - `size: {files} file(s), +{added}, -{deleted}{ ({binary} binary)} — tests: yes|no, executable: yes|no, against {base}`;
     - accepted: `walk: D1 accept, D2 overrule…`, or `walk: none`;
     - returned: `F{k} {text}` per finding.
   - held: `held {hold} — {reason}: {question}`. Details:
     - the context lines;
     - `{letter}. {text}` per option;
     - `on {branch} at {commit}`, or `on the run's hash {run_hash}`;
     - `about {items joined ", "}{ at {commit}}; {licenses} licenses a landing` when about is Some.
   - cleared: `cleared {hold} — answered {letter}{: {text}}`, or `cleared {hold} — cancelled`.
   - landed: `landed {sha} (range {old}..{sha}; squash of {squash_of}{; through run {run}})`. Details:
     - `test: {command}, rc {rc}`, or `test: NOT TESTED — {not_tested}`;
     - one line per check row, as land.rs:1451-1453 `row()` formats it;
     - `work branch: {branch or "(none)"} — {classification}`.
   Every multi-line value's continuation lines are indented under their field.
   `{by}` is the actor's display form as fleet-iex (d) defines it.
2. `show::document(item: &Item, timeline: &[Entry]) -> serde_json::Value` = {"id", "title", "description", "status", "type", "labels", "assignee" (string or null), "order" (the index as {"by","kind","seat","at"}, null when absent, or {"unreadable": true}), "blockers", "timeline": [entry::to_json(e) per entry]}.
