title: zlk-1b: the store appends and reads an item's timeline — bd comments in the adapter, the fake, the contract, and one append-and-read-back helper
description:
SPEC (split 1b of fleet-zlk, drafted 2026-09-23).
Names: (the shared names line above.)

Behaviour.
- The Store trait gains `append` and `timeline`.
- The bd adapter keeps each entry as ONE bd comment whose text is `entry::encode(body)`.
- The timeline reads only comments carrying "fleet.entry". A person's comment is not an entry. A malformed entry is exit 3 [ASSUMES D5].
- The fake store keeps comments the same way and decodes them through the same function.
- Verbs get one helper that appends and then reads the entry back.
- No verb calls any of this yet.

Measured on bd 1.3.0 (scratch board, 2026-09-23). Record these in the trait's doc comment:
- `bd comments add <id> <text> --actor A --json` answers the envelope with data {id, issue_id, author: A, text, created_at}.
- The id is CONTENT-DERIVED (e.g. e9f93b1f-8828-563c-…, version nibble 5; beads v1.3.0 internal/storage/issueops/derivedid.go InsertDerivedComment). It is not time-ordered, so it is never sorted.
- `bd comments <id> --json` lists by created_at ASC, then id ASC (issueops/comments.go:28). A live add truncates to the second and advances past the item's newest comment (derivedid.go:190-205), so the listing is append order.
- An item with no comments answers data []. A missing item exits 1 with data {"error":"resolving <id>: no issue found matching \"<id>\""}, which carries no code.
- There is no edit or delete subcommand.
- A closed item takes comments.
- `bd show --json` answers comment_count and "comments_omitted": true. `bd list --json` answers comment_count only.
- `bd export` writes each issue's comments into the committed .beads/issues.jsonl.

Sites (at HEAD bde60be):
- core/src/store.rs:145-245 (trait Store): add
  - `fn append(&self, item: &str, body: &Body, by: &Actor) -> Result<String, StoreError>;` (the answer is the entry's id)
  - `fn timeline(&self, item: &str) -> Result<Vec<Entry>, StoreError>;`
  Both carry docs.
- core/src/store.rs:593-785 (impl Store for Bd): the two methods.
- core/src/test_support.rs:36-84 (FakeStore fields), :375-497 (impl Store for FakeStore), :720-760 (the Arc forwarding).
- The five doctored stores forward the two methods to `inner`: core/tests/deliver.rs:148, core/tests/dispatch.rs:102, core/tests/gate.rs:139, core/tests/land.rs:382, core/tests/review.rs:165.
- core/src/item/mod.rs: the helper goes beside `control_token` (:689-708).
- core/tests/contract.rs:42-54 (CHECKS); core/tests/store.rs (fake arms).

Remedy:
1. Bd::append.
   - Call `body.validate()` first. On failure: Err(StoreError::Unreadable(format!("the {kind} entry for {item} does not validate: {why} — nothing was written"))).
   - Then `self.created_id(&["comments", "add", item, &encode(body), "--actor", &by.to_string(), "--json"])`. The `--actor` marks the call as a write for Bd::run's timeout message (store.rs:313).
2. Bd::timeline.
   - Run args ["comments", item, "--json"] through `self.run` (not `answered`, because a missing item's answer is read before its status, as show does at :605-623).
   - Open the answer with `self.json(...)`:
     - If it is an Object with "error": Err(StoreError::Missing(format!("{item}: {error}"))).
     - If the status is non-zero: Err(self.refused(...)).
     - If it is an Array: for each row, `entry::read_row(item, id, author, text, created_at)`. Ok(Some) is kept, Ok(None) is skipped, and Err(why) gives Err(StoreError::Unreadable(why)).
     - If it is Null or stdout is empty: Ok(vec![]).
     - Anything else: Err(Unreadable("{named} did not answer a list: {tail}")).
3. FakeStore.
   - Add `pub comments: Mutex<BTreeMap<String, Vec<Comment>>>`, `pub struct Comment { pub id: String, pub author: String, pub text: String, pub at: String }` and a counter `comment_ids: AtomicUsize`.
   - append:
     - logs "append {item} {kind} {by}";
     - applies the same validate() and refusal as Bd;
     - answers Missing for an item it does not hold;
     - takes id `c-<n>` and at `format!("2026-01-01T00:{:02}:{:02}Z", n / 60, n % 60)`;
     - when deaf (ignore_writes): answers the id and stores nothing.
   - timeline:
     - `self.refuse()` first;
     - Missing for an absent item;
     - every row goes through `entry::read_row`, the same function Bd uses.
   - `pub fn comment(&self, item: &str, author: &str, text: &str) -> String` plants a raw comment and answers its id, for a person's text or a malformed entry.
4. The helper in core/src/item/mod.rs:
   `pub enum Unrecorded { NotWritten(StoreError), Unconfirmed(String) }` and `pub fn recorded(store: &dyn Store, item: &str, body: &Body, by: &Actor) -> Result<String, Unrecorded>`:
   - (i) `store.append`, with its error as NotWritten;
   - (ii) `store.timeline(item)`, with its error as Unconfirmed(e.to_string());
   - (iii) no entry with the answered id: Unconfirmed(format!("{item}'s timeline does not hold the {kind} entry {id} the store answered for it"));
   - (iv) the entry's body or by differs from what was written: Unconfirmed(format!("{item}'s {kind} entry {id} read back as {got} and {want} was written")), where both are `entry::to_json`;
   - (v) any entry whose id == control_token(): Unconfirmed(format!("the read-back of {item}'s timeline carries {token}, which nothing wrote — the read is not reading this item"));
   - (vi) otherwise Ok(id).
   Each verb maps Unrecorded to its own STANDS wording (2a onward).

Acceptance:
1. core/tests/contract.rs, check "append then timeline", added to CHECKS so both halves run it (the board held in memory, and bd through `every_check_holds_against_bd_too`):
   - a filed item's timeline is [];

   - the timeline is [id1, id2] in that order, with bodies equal, `by` == A, `at` non-empty, and id1 != id2.
2. core/tests/contract.rs, check "timeline of an absent item": Missing, on both halves.
3. core/tests/contract.rs, a bd-only arm on the shared scratch store:
   - plant `bd -C <root> comments add <item> "a person's words"`. The timeline leaves it out.
   - plant `bd -C <root> comments add <item> '{"fleet.entry":1,"kind":"ordered","order":"dispatch"}' --actor "Alberto Vildosola"`. timeline is Err(Unreadable) naming that comment's id and the author [ASSUMES D5].
   RED-PROOF: with read_row's NotAnEntry branch removed, the first half goes red.
4. core/tests/store.rs, fake arms:
   - the same two plants through FakeStore::comment;
   - a deaf store answers an id from append and an empty timeline;
   - `recorded` on the deaf store is Unconfirmed naming "does not hold".
5. A bd arm: append a Delivered whose commit is 7 characters. The answer is Err(Unreadable) with "nothing was written", and `bd comments <item> --json` lists nothing new.

title: zlk-1a: the entry model — an item's record as typed timeline entries, their wire text and the fold, in core
description:
SPEC (split 1a of fleet-zlk, drafted 2026-09-23).
Names: (the shared names line above.)

Behaviour. core gains the one definition of an item's record:
- an Entry: the store's id, the store's time, a typed actor and a typed body;
- seven body kinds;
- the text a store keeps per entry, a JSON object {"fleet.entry": 1, "kind": …, fields…};
- a decoder that tells a person's text from an entry and refuses a malformed entry;
- validation: full 40-hex shas, option letters, and per-kind invariants;
- Timeline, the fold every later reader uses.
No store is read or written yet (1b does that). No verb changes. fleet-0q4 (a) builds its contract types on these.

Sites (at HEAD bde60be):
- core/src/lib.rs:100-116 (the module list): add `pub mod entry;`.
- core/src/entry.rs (new).
- core/tests/entry.rs (new).
- core/Cargo.toml:25-28: no change. The workspace's serde already carries the derive feature.

Remedy:
1. Constants in core/src/entry.rs:
   - `pub const KEY: &str = "fleet.entry";`
   - `pub const VERSION: u64 = 1;`
   - `pub const KINDS: [&str; 7] = ["ordered", "order_withdrawn", "delivered", "reviewed", "held", "cleared", "landed"];`
2. Types.
   - Every struct derives `Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize` and carries `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]`.
   - Every `Option` field carries `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`.
   - Enums use `#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]`.
   - `pub struct Entry { pub id: String, pub at: String, pub by: Actor, pub body: Body }`. There is no serde on Entry: the reader builds it.
   - `#[serde(tag = "kind", rename_all = "snake_case")] pub enum Body { Ordered(Ordered), OrderWithdrawn(OrderWithdrawn), Delivered(Delivered), Reviewed(Reviewed), Held(Held), Cleared(Cleared), Landed(Landed) }`, plus `pub fn kind(&self) -> &'static str`, which answers the KINDS spelling.
   - `Ordered { order: OrderKind, seat: Option<SeatId> }`; `enum OrderKind { Dispatch }`. There is no review kind and no ordinal: HEAD writes neither (fleet-d11, d744f5c).
   - `OrderWithdrawn { why: Withdrawal, seat: Option<SeatId>, cause: Option<String> }`; `enum Withdrawal { Retire, SpawnRefused }` [ASSUMES D6] [ASSUMES D17 for `cause`].
   - `Delivered { commit: String, branch: String, base: String, files: Vec<String>, checks: Vec<CheckResult>, suite: SuiteRun, spec_corrections: Vec<SpecCorrection>, not_proven: Vec<NotProven>, decisions: Vec<Decision>, covers: Vec<String> }`.
   - `CheckResult { check: String, result: String }`; `SpecCorrection { premise: String, refuted_by: String }`; `NotProven { surface: String, command: String }`; `Decision { call: String, not_taken: String, because: String }`.
   - `#[serde(untagged)] enum SuiteRun { Ran(Ran), NotTested(NotTested) }`, with `Ran { command: String, rc: i32 }` and `NotTested { not_tested: String }`. Each carries deny_unknown_fields.
   - `Reviewed { verdict: Verdict, commit: String, size: Size, walk: Vec<Ruling>, findings: Vec<Finding> }`. `findings` carries `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty")]`.
   - `enum Verdict { Accepted, Returned }`; `Size { files: u64, added: u64, deleted: u64, binary: u64, tests: bool, executable: bool, base: String }`; `Ruling { decision: u32, ruling: RulingKind }` (decision is D<k>, 1-based); `enum RulingKind { Accept, Overrule }`; `Finding { text: String }`.
   - `Held { hold: String, reason: HoldReason, question: String, context: Option<String>, options: Vec<Choice>, branch: Option<String>, commit: Option<String>, run_hash: Option<String>, about: Option<About> }`; `enum HoldReason { Ask, MaxCrashes }`; `Choice { letter: String, text: String }`; `About { items: Vec<String>, commit: Option<String>, licenses: String }` [ASSUMES D8] [ASSUMES D17 for `context`].
   - `Cleared { hold: String, how: Clearance, letter: Option<String>, text: Option<String> }`; `enum Clearance { Answer, Cancel }`.
   - `Landed { sha: String, old: String, squash_of: String, run: Option<String>, test: SuiteRun, checks: Vec<CheckRow>, work_branch: WorkBranch }`; `CheckRow { check: String, verdict: String, evidence: String }`; `WorkBranch { branch: Option<String>, classification: Classification }`; `enum Classification { Safe, CarriesUnlandedWork, Carries, CouldNotTell, NotGiven }`.
3. Validation.
   - `pub fn full_sha(text: &str) -> bool` is true for exactly 40 characters of [0-9a-f].
   - `impl Body { pub fn validate(&self) -> Result<(), String> }`. The first failure wins, and each message names the field in backticks, e.g. "`commit` is not a full 40-hex sha: 1a2b3c4".
   - delivered:
     - commit and base are full_sha;
     - branch is non-empty;
     - files is non-empty ("names no file — `files` lists every path the delivery touched");
     - not_proven is non-empty ("names nothing not proven — `not_proven` is never empty");
     - every nested string is non-empty.
   - reviewed:
     - commit and size.base are full_sha;
     - Returned needs findings to be non-empty ("a return carries at least one finding");
     - Accepted needs findings to be empty;
     - the walk's decision numbers are 1-based and strictly increasing.
   - held:
     - hold is non-empty;
     - question is non-empty and holds no '\n';
     - options is non-empty;
     - each letter matches ^[A-Z]$, and letters are unique;
     - each option's text is non-empty;
     - exactly one of {branch and commit both Some} or {run_hash Some} holds;
     - commit, when Some, is full_sha;
     - about, when Some: items is non-empty, commit (when Some) is full_sha, and licenses matches ^[A-Z]$ and is one of the option letters.
   - cleared:
     - Answer needs a letter that matches ^[A-Z]$;
     - Cancel needs letter None and text None.
   - landed:
     - sha, old and squash_of are full_sha;
     - checks is non-empty.
   - ordered / order_withdrawn:
     - seat, when Some, is non-empty;
     - SpawnRefused needs cause to be Some.
4. `pub fn encode(body: &Body) -> String`: `serde_json::to_value(body)` gives an object; insert KEY: VERSION into it and write it compact.
5. Decoding.
   - `pub enum Read { NotAnEntry, Entry(Body), Unreadable(String) }` and `pub fn decode(text: &str) -> Read`:
     - (i) text.trim() does not parse as a JSON object: NotAnEntry, because a person's comment is not an entry.
     - (ii) the object has no KEY: NotAnEntry.
     - (iii) KEY is not the number 1: Unreadable("carries fleet.entry <v>, and this binary reads version 1").
     - (iv) remove KEY. If `serde_json::from_value::<Body>` fails: Unreadable(<serde's message>).
     - (v) If validate() fails: Unreadable(<its message>).
   - `pub fn read_row(item: &str, id: &str, author: &str, text: &str, at: &str) -> Result<Option<Entry>, String>`:
     - NotAnEntry gives Ok(None).
     - Unreadable(why) gives Err(format!("{item}'s comment {id} carries `fleet.entry` and does not read: {why}")).
     - Entry(body): parse `author` with Actor::parse. On failure, Err(format!("{item}'s comment {id} names its author `{author}`, which is not an actor reference (<kind>:<id>)")) [ASSUMES D5].
     - Otherwise Ok(Some(Entry { id, at, by, body })).
   - `pub fn to_json(entry: &Entry) -> serde_json::Value`: the body's object, carrying "kind" and not KEY, plus "id", "at" and "by": {"kind": <actor kind>, "id": <actor id>}.
6. `pub struct Timeline<'a>(pub &'a [Entry]);`. The slice's order is the store's order, and every answer is by position in it:
   - `current_order() -> Option<(&Entry, &Ordered)>`: the last Ordered with no OrderWithdrawn after it.
   - `last_delivery() -> Option<(&Entry, &Delivered)>`.
   - `standing_delivery()`: the last Delivered with no Reviewed{Returned} after it. This is fleet-45m's rule: a landing does not clear it.
   - `carried_delivery()`: standing_delivery() with no Landed after it.
   - `last_review() -> Option<(&Entry, &Reviewed)>`; `last_landing() -> Option<(&Entry, &Landed)>`.
   - `held(hold: &str)`: the last Held with that hold id.
   - `clearance(hold: &str)`: the first Cleared naming that hold. A Cleared with no Held before it still answers by its hold id.
   - `open_hold()`: the last Held with no Cleared naming its hold after it.

   - the wire text is one JSON object per entry;
   - a text without KEY is a person's and is skipped;
   - a malformed entry is could-not-tell and never skipped;
   - the order is the store's listing order, and ids are never sorted.

1. Round trip. One sample body per kind: encode, then decode, gives the same body. The encoded object carries "fleet.entry":1 and "kind":"<kind>".
2. decode("a person's words") and decode("{\"kind\":\"delivered\"}") each give NotAnEntry.

   - an unknown field "colour" on a delivered body (deny_unknown_fields);
   - a delivered body missing "not_proven".
4. validate refuses, each with an Err naming the field:
   - a delivered body whose commit is 7 characters;
   - a held body carrying run_hash beside branch;
   - a cleared how=cancel carrying a letter;
   - a returned review with no findings;
   - about.licenses naming a letter that no option carries.
   RED-PROOF: delete the short-sha rule and the first case goes red.
5. read_row answers Ok(None) for a person's text. It answers Err naming the comment id for a body authored `Alberto Vildosola`.
6. The folds:
   - [delivered c1, reviewed returned c1, delivered c2, landed]: standing = c2, carried = None;
   - [delivered c1, reviewed returned c1]: standing = None;
   - [ordered, order_withdrawn]: current_order = None;
   - [ordered seat None, ordered seat S]: current_order's seat is S;
   - [held h1, cleared h1, held h2]: open_hold = h2;
   - [held h1 about {items: [X], licenses: "A"}]: holds_about(X) = h1.

title: A seat appears as {id, name?, kind} in the projection, the event payloads, every seat-bearing --json document and the SDK
description:
SPEC (split f of fleet-iex, drafted 2026-09-23).
Every machine-readable seat is the object {"id": "<full id>", "name": "<name>" (absent when none), "kind": "agent" | "human"}.

The projection:
- SeatRow's seat_dir + chosen_name become "seat": {…}.
- in_flight.seat is the object.

Event payloads:
- item.dispatched "seat", dispatch.failed "seat" and session.retired "seat" are the object.
- session.* "name" stays the session's name, which is now <slug>-<short>. The actor carries the seat.

JSON documents: `fleet dispatch --json` "seat", and `seat spawn`, `seat feed` and `seat retire --json` "seat".

`fleet status`'s human lines name a seat by its machine name [ASSUMES D13].

The SDK's Dispatched.seat is typed `Seat { id: string; name?: string; kind: "agent" | "human" }`.

This is an external-contract change, and the bead lists it at landing for anything that reads projection.json or the stream.
Sites (at HEAD bde60be):
- controller/src/projection.rs:62-66 InFlight, :141-212 SeatRow and from_observation, tests :229-376.
- controller/src/run.rs:738-743 and :1253-1256.
- controller/src/seat.rs:95-99 and :144-147; cli/src/nudge.rs:174 (they read row["seat_dir"]).
- cli/src/status.rs:360-361, :405-409, :456-462, :636-651.
- core/src/item/mod.rs:191 (ITEM_DISPATCHED payload keys); core/src/item/dispatch.rs:414-420.
- controller/src/events.rs:144-146 (dispatch_failed_payload); controller/src/transient.rs:1642-1664 (session.retired).
- cli/src/item.rs:709-713 (dispatch --json); cli/src/transient.rs:151-158, :205-212, :324-333.
- packs/ts/assets/sdk/mod.ts:130-135 Dispatched; SDK tests verbs_test.ts:110-120 and takeoff_test.ts:56 ("tr-1" fixtures); testdata/spawns.ts.
- Tests: cli/tests/drive_seats.rs:117, :157, :170; controller/tests/observe.rs:794-804; controller/tests/blocked_poll.rs (its decision helper finds a row by seat_dir); cli/tests/item_json.rs, seat.rs, status.rs; controller/src/events.rs:690.
Remedy:
1. controller/src/projection.rs:
   - `#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize, Clone)] pub struct SeatView { pub id: String, #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none", default)] pub name: Option<String>, pub kind: String }`.
   - SeatRow { seat: SeatView, … }, replacing seat_dir and chosen_name.
   - InFlight { seat: SeatView, effect }.
   - from_observation takes &config::Seat.
2. Every reader of row["seat_dir"] reads row["seat"]["id"]: controller/src/seat.rs, cli/src/nudge.rs and cli/src/status.rs.
3. Payload objects, in the order id, name?, kind:
   - dispatch.rs announce writes "seat" as the object, built from Directory. The kind comes from the directory entry.
   - The transient item.dispatched writes the spawned seat (agent, no name).
   - dispatch_failed_payload(seat: &SeatView, …).
   - session.retired "seat".
4. JSON documents:
   - dispatch --json "seat": the object, or null where no seat was named.
   - The three seat verbs: "seat": the object.
5. status [ASSUMES D13]:
   - The roster line starts with the machine name.
   - The in_flight line reads "{machine name} — {effect}".
   - The context row is keyed on the machine name.
6. SDK:
   - `export interface Seat { id: string; name?: string; kind: "agent" | "human"; }`.
   - Dispatched.seat: Seat.
   - Fixtures {seat: {id: "…", kind: "agent"}}.
Acceptance:
1. controller/tests/observe.rs: the projection's seats[0].seat = {id, name: "Orla", kind: "agent"}, with no seat_dir and no chosen_name. A nameless seat's object has no "name" key.

title: The work graph holds seat ids, part 2: [core] reviewer resolves to a seat id, deliver reassigns to it, review returns to fleet.orders.seat, and land compares ids and writes id trailers
description:
SPEC (split e2 of fleet-iex, drafted 2026-09-23).
[core] reviewer may hold a full id, 8+ hex, a name or a machine name. Every reader resolves it among the listed seats, of any kind, to exactly one seat. Missing or ambiguous is exit 1, naming the key.

What follows from that:
- deliver reassigns the item to the reviewer's full id and reads that back.
- review's return reassigns to fleet.orders.seat, which is an id since e1.
- land's closer is:
  - the reviewer id when a run carried the landing;
  - otherwise the actor resolved through Directory::seat_of, and an actor that is not a seat is refused.
- The closer is compared with the assignee as ids.
- The run licence compares the answering actor, resolved, with the reviewer id.
- Commit trailers carry ids: `Seat: <closer id>`. `Implemented-by:` carries the builder's id when the delivering actor resolves to a seat, and the actor string otherwise (a run).
- land's reviewers_worktree (iex-b1) finds the reviewer's row by the resolved id.
Sites (at HEAD bde60be):
- core/src/item/deliver.rs:142, :165, :361-379 (reviewer_of, no_reviewer), :536-543 (the read-back, and the RERUN "bd update {item} --assignee {reviewer}").
- core/src/item/review.rs:400-408 (builder from orders.seat), :423 (assign), :442-447 (ring and STANDS text), :470-475.
- core/src/item/land.rs:
  - :366-414 reviewers_worktree;
  - :536-560 closer and holder;
  - :565-573 licensed/landed_by;
  - :584 builder = after_dash(delivery);
  - :904-908 the note's actor/builder;
  - :1777-1800 licensed;
  - :1801-1809 after_dash;
  - :1812-1819 message().
- core/src/policy.rs:37 (the census ("core","reviewer")) is unchanged.
- Tests:
  - core/tests/land.rs `the_marker_and_the_two_trailers_ride_the_commit_subject` (:1074 and :1078), `a_run_lands_as_the_reviewer_and_names_the_run_beside_it`, `a_runs_landing_is_refused_an_item_another_seat_holds`;
  - core/tests/deliver.rs, review.rs;
  - cli/tests/ring_land.rs:910-911 and deliver.rs.
Remedy:
1. `reviewer_of(project, dir) -> Result<SeatRef, Stop>`:
   - Read the string as today.
   - Resolve it with dir.resolve_listed(value).
   - On failure: Stop::refused("`[core] reviewer = \"{value}\"` {Unresolved text}"), or usage for Blank.
   - no_reviewer's text is unchanged.
2. deliver assigns reviewer.id.to_string(). The read-back compares the id. The RERUN line prints the id.
3. review: the builder id string comes from orders.seat, assigned and rung as the id. The STANDS text names dir.label(id).
4. land:
   - closer: SeatId = the reviewer id for a run, else dir.seat_of(landing.by). None is exit 1: "`{by}` is neither a seat of this fleet nor a run — whoever closes an item lands its work".
   - The holder compare is `assignee == closer.to_string()`. The refusal texts name dir.label for both sides.
   - licensed: dir.seat_of(after_dash(answer)) == Some(reviewer id).
   - builder: after_dash(delivery) resolved through seat_of. That gives the id string, else the raw string.
   - message(): "Seat: {closer id}\nImplemented-by: {builder}".
   - landed_by and the note render label(closer) followed by " ({closer id})".
   - reviewers_worktree: the row whose "id" equals reviewer.id.
Acceptance:

2. core/tests/review.rs: a return reassigns to the order's seat id.
3. core/tests/land.rs:
   - the trailers read "Seat: {reviewer id}" and "Implemented-by: {builder id}";
   - a run's landing on an item held by another seat's id is refused, naming both labels;
   - a licence answered by the reviewer's name (resolved) passes, and one answered by another seat is refused.
4. cli/tests/ring_land.rs:910-911 expects the id trailers.

title: The work graph holds seat ids, part 1: dispatch and brief resolve --to to a seat id, the assignee and fleet.orders.seat carry it, and the holder checks compare ids
description:
SPEC (split e1 of fleet-iex, drafted 2026-09-23).
Core gains a seat Directory, which the cli fills:
- `listed`: the fleet.toml roster, plus the machine's transient rows, plus this machine's identity when identity.toml exists. Reading never mints.
- `running`: the machine's config.json rows.

The dispatch path:
- `fleet dispatch --to <arg>` and `fleet brief --to <arg>` resolve the argument among the RUNNING seats: an agent seat this machine runs. Missing or ambiguous is exit 1.
- The assignee and fleet.orders.seat are written as the full id.
- The one-at-a-time check (fleet-pg7's holds) lists by the id.
- A transient dispatch assigns the spawned seat's full id.
- The brief's `{seat}` renders the seat's machine name. It stays "(transient)" before a spawn.

deliver's and ask's holder check (held_item) finds the seat by resolving the actor string among the listed seats. This is a bridge until iex-d2 types the actor. It then lists by id. An actor that resolves to no seat, with no --item, is refused.

`fleet prime` lists the items assigned to the id of the seat whose row names this directory.

A routine's [action.item] assignee resolves at load to a full id [ASSUMES D14].
Sites (at HEAD bde60be):
- core/src/item/dispatch.rs:
  - :122-124 Wiring.seats: &[String];
  - :137 Given.seat;
  - :188-236 refuse_unless_dispatchable (membership at :212-221, holds at :224);
  - :260-263 the named assign;
  - :272 the brief render;
  - :288;
  - :296-305 the ORDERED, NOT RUNG texts;
  - :344-353 the transient assign;
  - :374;
  - :414-432 announce ("seat");
  - :523-543 index/index_payload. After fleet-4j6 this is the fleet.orders writer.

- core/src/seat/identity.rs (iex-a1): add Directory.
- cli/src/item.rs:
  - :827-846 run_dispatch (seats: &here.seats);
  - :866-868 brief (`parsed.to.as_deref().unwrap_or(TRANSIENT)`);

  - :1103 and :1130 seats_of;
  - :1170-1175.
- cli/src/prime.rs:189-205 seat_here and :235-244 items (assigned_to).
- cli/src/transient.rs:263-288 (retire's held/withdraw by the row id).
- cli/src/runs.rs:224-231 withdrawn_from.

- Tests:
  - core/tests/dispatch.rs `a_named_dispatch_writes_the_assignee_the_note_and_the_index` and `a_spawned_seat_takes_the_assignee_the_index_and_the_brief`;
  - core/tests/brief.rs (19 seat literals), deliver.rs, gate.rs, retire.rs;
  - cli/tests/dispatch.rs, item_json.rs, seat.rs;
  - core/tests/contract.rs (its orders helper).
Remedy:
1. core/src/seat/identity.rs:
   - `pub struct Directory { pub listed: Vec<SeatRef>, pub running: Vec<SeatRef> }`.
   - `resolve_running(&self, arg) -> Result<&SeatRef, Unresolved>`.
   - `resolve_listed(&self, arg) -> Result<&SeatRef, Unresolved>`.
   - `label(&self, id: &SeatId) -> String`: the machine name of a listed or running seat, else the id.
   - `seat_of(&self, by: &str) -> Option<SeatId>`: resolve_listed(by).ok(), where a Missing or Ambiguous answer means "not a seat". iex-d1 extends it to "seat:<id>"; iex-d2 deletes it.
2. cli Here.seats becomes Directory. It is built in declared_at and embedded_at:
   - listed = roster(&project.guards) seats' refs + transient rows' refs + read_identity(machine_dir).as_ref();
   - running = the rows' refs.
3. dispatch:
   - Wiring.seats: &Directory.
   - The --to arg resolves with resolve_running. A failure is Stop from Unresolved; the Missing text replaces "is not a seat this machine runs".
   - Every downstream use takes id.to_string(): assign, index seat, holds, announce "seat", Given.seat.
   - The ORDERED/NOT RUNG texts name label(id).
   - The ring is called with the id. SeatRing resolves a full id exactly.
   - The transient path assigns the Spawned.seat id string.
4. brief:
   - `--to` resolves with resolve_running.
   - Subject.seat = the machine name.
   - The cli passes the resolved seat, or TRANSIENT.
5. held_item(store, by, named, dir):
   - Unchanged with --item.
   - Otherwise `dir.seat_of(by)`. None gives exit 1: "`{by}` is not a seat of this fleet, so it holds nothing — pass --item <id>". Some(id) gives holds(store, &id.to_string()).
   - Pass Directory through deliver's and ask's Wiring.
6. prime: items(project_root, &row.id.to_string()).
7. retire: held and withdraw take the row's id string. The note names label(id).
8. [ASSUMES D14] routines [action.item] assignee:
   - load resolves the value with core's resolve over listed ∪ running, which the cli and run.rs pass in.
   - Missing or ambiguous is a load reason: "[action.item] assignee is `{v}`, which {Unresolved text}".
   - item_argv writes the full id.

1. core/tests/dispatch.rs: `--to orla` (Orla is a running seat) writes assignee = Orla's full id and fleet.orders.seat = the same id. The read-backs pass. Shown red against today's code first: today it writes "orla".
2. `--to` a human seat's name is exit 1. The human is not a running seat.
3. `--to` an ambiguous name is exit 1 naming both.
4. The fleet-pg7 arms stay green with ids: an unordered item plus an ordered epic lets dispatch proceed; ordered items are refused by name and status.
5. core/tests/deliver.rs: deliver `--by orla` (a name) finds the item assigned to Orla's id. `--by run-x` with no --item is exit 1 "is not a seat".
6. core/tests/brief.rs: `--to orla` renders "You are `orla-{short}`". With no --to it renders "(transient)".
7. cli/tests/prime (cli/tests/lifecycle.rs's prime arm, or a new arm in cli/tests/seat.rs): in Orla's worktree, prime lists the items assigned to her id.
8. controller/tests/routines.rs: an [action.item] assignee "Orla" is filed with her full id; "nobody" fails the load.
Gate line: touched suites green; the reviewer runs the full suite, ran or cached, at landing.

Every site cited here is RE-FOUND BY SYMBOL at pickup, and names from those beads are the landed ones. Every [ASSUMES Dn] in this spec was ruled as assumed by Alberto (AskUserQuestion, 2026-09-24). fleet-iex rulings in force: D1 the short id is the LAST 8 hex digits of the v7 (its first 8 are a timestamp that repeats for ~65 s); D7 the controller sets FLEET_ACTOR=seat:<id> on every session it starts.

Review calls, accepted: the controller's Withdrawal seam still hands the machine name and the cli closures use the row's id (hand retire) or resolve it back through resolve_running (run cleanup) — same result, smaller blast radius; the Directory is built in controller config::directory(rows, policy, machine_dir) rather than inline in the cli because the controller tick needs the same thing, and declared_at/embedded_at call it; routines' listed ∪ running is a private known_seats helper in routines/file.rs; a blank [action.item] assignee now fails the load with the resolver's Blank text (was filed as-is — an inference from the spec's missing/ambiguous rule); the brief re-rendered after a spawn still says (transient), as before; index_repair(order, seat) now names the seat the read-back wanted (before: the typed argument, and nothing on the transient pass). title: The stream carries the actor as a typed reference {kind, id}; tail filters by --seat (resolved) and --actor, and the SDK reads the typed actor
description:
SPEC (split d3 of fleet-iex, drafted 2026-09-23).
Every events.jsonl line's "actor" becomes a JSON object {"kind": "seat" | "run" | "routine" | "controller", "id": "…"} instead of a string (R3). The seat.* and session.* events keep naming the seat the event is ABOUT [ASSUMES D12].

Readers take the typed actor:
- the fold drops a seat event whose actor is not kind seat, or not a known seat id. It refuses by kind.
- sessions rebuild, the run's spawned set, crashed_output and seat::record's read-back compare typed actors.

Tail filters:
- `fleet event tail --seat <arg>` resolves the argument through the resolver, over the roster, the rows and the identity, and keeps lines whose actor is {seat, id}.
- The new `--actor <kind:id>` keeps an exact typed match.

The SDK filters with `--actor run:<id>` and reads actor as {kind, id}.

The payload "by" on session.nudged is the typed object.

  - :14-23 Event.actor;
  - :25-27 CONTROLLER;

- Tests that read "actor" as a string:
  - controller/tests/adoption.rs and controller/tests/blocked_poll.rs (their lines helpers);
  - cli/tests/drive_effects.rs, drive_loop.rs, drive_stream.rs, events.rs, nudge.rs, routines.rs, run.rs;

Remedy:

   - `#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize, Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)] pub struct ActorRef { pub kind: String, pub id: String }`. This is the controller's own copy [ASSUMES D2: or re-export core's Actor with a serde impl; take whichever D2 rules].
   - Event.actor: &ActorRef.

   - Record.actor: ActorRef. read_after drops a line whose actor is not an object carrying string kind and id.
   - RawLine.actor: Option<ActorRef>.
   - CONTROLLER becomes `fn controller(machine_dir) -> ActorRef`, with its id from identity_or_mint [ASSUMES D8].
2. core Events::append takes &Actor. StreamEvents converts it.
3. Every appender passes a typed actor:
   - seat events and session.* events: {seat, <id>};
   - controller events: controller(…);
   - routine events: {routine, <name>};

4. Readers:

title: Core's verbs take the typed actor: bd gets its <kind>:<id> string, and every seat-only check refuses a non-seat actor by kind
description:
SPEC (split d2 of fleet-iex, drafted 2026-09-23).

title: The actor is a typed reference at the cli: --by and FLEET_ACTOR take a seat or kind:id, BEADS_ACTOR is no longer read, and with neither the verb acts as this machine's identity
description:
SPEC (split d1 of fleet-iex, drafted 2026-09-23).
The actor becomes a typed reference, {kind: seat | run | routine | controller, id}, with the string form "<kind>:<id>". It is defined in core and resolved once at the cli boundary.

How each writing verb chooses its actor, in order:
1. --by.
2. FLEET_ACTOR.
3. This machine's identity (R6). identity.toml is minted where absent. When the fleet's roster does not list that identity, the verb still runs, and prints one stderr line per invocation naming `fleet seat add --human` [ASSUMES D6].

BEADS_ACTOR is not read anywhere. The "no <who> — pass --by" refusals (exit 2) go, because a verb always has an actor now.

The grammar of --by and FLEET_ACTOR:
- "seat:<full id>" is accepted as given [ASSUMES D9].
- "run:<id>", "routine:<name>" and "controller:<id>" are accepted as given.
- Anything else is a seat argument, resolved over the fleet's roster, the machine's rows and this machine's identity. A failure is exit 1 with the resolver's text.

Core's verbs still take `by: &str` in this bead and receive the string form. The Directory bridge from iex-e1 reads "seat:<id>" as that seat.

Writers that pass a bare string today move to the typed form here, because a bare string now resolves as a seat:
- the SDK passes `--by run:<id>`, and filters its own tail lines with `--seat run:<id>`, an exact actor-string match until iex-d3;
- a routine's `fleet run` argv passes `--by routine:<name>`;
- step.rs falls back to "run:<id>".

The controller starts every session with FLEET_ACTOR=seat:<id> [ASSUMES D7]. So a seat's own bare `fleet deliver` acts as the seat, never as the machine's human.

title: A transient spawn mints a fresh seat id that is never reused; transient-N and its lowest-free counter go
description:
SPEC (split c of fleet-iex, drafted 2026-09-23).
`fleet seat spawn` claims a transient seat by minting a fresh SeatId under the seat-list lock. The seat has no name, so its machine name is "agent-<short>".
- The worktree is <worktrees>/agent-<short>.
- The config directory is <machine>/config/agent-<short>.
- The row is {"name": "agent-<short>", "id", "kind": "agent", "transient": true, "model", "worktrees"}. "name" stays as the key until iex-b1 drops it.
- The transient is never written to fleet.toml.
- An id is never handed out twice, so a retired seat's name is never reused.

retire's withdrawal of the orders a seat still holds STAYS. What changes is the reason given for it: the orders are released so their items become dispatchable again. The reason is no longer that the next spawn would inherit the name.

spawn prints the seat's machine name, alone, on stdout. After b1 the key it prints is the id; see Remedy 4.
Sites (at HEAD bde60be):
- controller/src/config.rs:
  - :121-123 TRANSIENT_PREFIX (delete);
  - :125-146 TransientSeat/Claimed/ClaimError;
  - :148-209 claim_transient_seat, whose doc at :148-166 says "Take the lowest free transient-N … The counter REUSES a number a retire freed", and its body at :172-185.
- controller/src/transient.rs:
  - :565-566 (Spawned doc);
  - :586-640 spawn (the claim);
  - :644;
  - :834-846 make_config_dir's doc ("a spawn re-using a name a retire left behind");
  - :1414-1423 (the comment "The seat list is what hands `transient-N` out" and its refusal text "the name is not free").
- controller/src/platform/mod.rs:168-174 (lock_beside's doc: "whose subject is the NAME").
- core/src/lib.rs:82-89 (retire's reason: "the next spawn takes the lowest free transient one").
- core/src/seat/retire.rs:1-19 (module doc "A TRANSIENT NAME GOES BACK ON THE PILE"), :55-60 and :92-99 (texts "before the name is given to anybody else").
- cli/src/transient.rs:162-164 (prints the name); cli/src/main.rs:313-320 (spawn long_about, "It prints the seat's name").
- Tests: controller/tests/transient.rs (34 transient-* references), cli/tests/seat.rs (53), core/tests/retire.rs (5), core/tests/store.rs (3), cli/tests/deliver.rs (3), cli/tests/drive_loop.rs:397, cli/tests/lifecycle.rs:1531 and :1575, cli/tests/common/mod.rs:53, cli/src/runs.rs:245 (test const SEAT = "transient-3").
Remedy:
1. claim_transient_seat mints, under the existing lock:
   - `let seat = SeatRef { id: SeatId::mint(), name: None, kind: Kind::Agent }; let name = seat.machine_name();`.
   - Delete the `taken` scan and the 1..=u32::MAX search.
   - The existing "{worktree} already exists" refusal stays.
   - Claimed gains `pub id: SeatId`.
   - The row pushed is {"name": name, "id": id, "kind": "agent", "transient": true, "model", "worktrees"}.
   - Delete TRANSIENT_PREFIX.
2. Rewrite claim_transient_seat's doc. Replace the counter paragraphs with: "Mint a fresh seat id, cut its worktree, and append its row — under ONE lock, so the row is never written for a tree that was not made. An id is never handed out twice, so nothing a retired seat left behind can be inherited by a later one."
3. Restate the retire reason in three places.
   - core/src/lib.rs:82-89 becomes: "`seat` is the record half of the verbs that end a seat, and `retire` is the one it carries: the orders the seat still holds are withdrawn — the assignee cleared, the order index unset, one note saying so, both writes read back — before its row goes. The reason is the work: an item still ordered to a seat that no longer exists is one nobody will deliver and nothing will dispatch again. The session, the worktree and the row are the controller's, and the cli is where the two halves meet."
   - Rewrite core/src/seat/retire.rs:1-19's first paragraph on the same reason.
   - Change the texts at retire.rs:92-99 ("before the name is given to anybody else") to "before the seat's row is dropped".
   - Change controller/src/transient.rs:1414-1423's comment to "THE RECORD BEFORE THE ROW", and its refusal to "…the seat-list row STANDS: clear the item and re-run this".
   - Change make_config_dir's doc to "A directory that already stands is EMPTIED first — a fresh id makes that a defect, never a reuse."
4. Spawned.seat carries the machine name ("agent-<short>"), and `seat spawn` prints it.
   - cli/src/main.rs:313-320: "It prints the seat's name" becomes "It prints the seat's machine name, agent-<short id>".
   - In iex-b1, Spawned.seat becomes the full id and the line becomes "It prints the seat's id". b1 owns that edit.
5. Tests:
   - Every arm expecting "transient-1" reads the spawned name from the spawn's stdout, or from the JSON "seat".
   - The rig comment at cli/tests/common/mod.rs:53 is rewritten.
Acceptance:

title: Add `fleet seat add --agent|--human`: it mints or lists a seat as one [seats.<id>] table in the fleet's own fleet.toml and reads it back
description:
SPEC (split a3 of fleet-iex, drafted 2026-09-23).
`fleet seat add` writes one [seats.<id>] table into the fleet's own fleet.toml: the file the verbs read their policy from, Here.policy_file. It then reads the table back before it answers 0.

The two forms:
- `--agent` mints a fresh id for a seat the controller runs, with an optional `--name` and `--model`.
- `--human` lists this machine's identity from <machine dir>/identity.toml, minting that file where there is none. It never asks for a name.

Output:
- stdout carries the seat's full id and nothing else.
- stderr carries the status lines.
- --json prints the envelope instead.

The file is edited by appending text, never re-serialized, so every comment and unknown key survives.
Sites (at HEAD bde60be):
- cli/src/main.rs:
  - :11-24, the mod list (add `mod seat_add;`);

- cli/src/envelope.rs:22 ok and :32 refusal.

- New files: cli/src/seat_add.rs and cli/tests/seat_add.rs.
Remedy:
1. cli/src/seat_add.rs: `#[derive(clap::Args)] pub struct AddArgs`. Every help text below is quoted exactly.
   - `--agent`: bool. Clap: `conflicts_with = "human"`, `required_unless_present = "human"`. Help: "a seat the controller runs, under a freshly minted id".
   - `--human`: bool. Help: "this machine's identity, minted where there is none".
   - `--name NAME`: Option<String>. Help: "what a person calls the seat; the id stays the key".
   - `--model MODEL`: Option<String>, with `requires = "agent"`. Help: "the model an agent seat runs on".
   - `--project NAME`: Help: "the project this directory must resolve to".
   - `--json`: Help: "print the envelope document instead of the id".
2. cli/src/main.rs: add `Add(seat_add::AddArgs)` to SeatVerb, first in the enum.
   - Short help: "add a seat to this fleet: a fresh id, its kind, a name if given".
   - long_about, exactly: "add a seat to the fleet's own fleet.toml: one [seats.<id>] table, appended\nand read back before it answers 0. --agent mints a fresh id for a seat the\ncontroller runs; --human lists this machine's identity, minting it into\nidentity.toml in the machine directory where there is none. Nobody is asked\nfor a name. It prints the seat's id."
   - Also: the `mod seat_add;` line and the seat_command arm `SeatVerb::Add(args) => seat_add::command(args)`.
3. seat_add::command(args) -> Exit. The steps, in order:
   1. Resolve Here through crate::transient::resolved(args.project). A Stop exits with its code.
   2. Validate --name [ASSUMES D10]. These are exit 2, printed "fleet seat add: {why}":
      - a name of 8 or more characters, all [0-9a-fA-F-]: "--name `{n}` reads as a seat id — pick a name that is not 8 or more hex digits";
      - a name ending in '-' plus 8 hex: "--name `{n}` ends the way a seat's machine name does (-<8 hex>) — pick another";
      - a blank name: "--name is empty".
   3. Take platform::lock_beside(&here.policy_file). Failure is exit 3.
   4. Read the file and run roster_in on it. An unreadable file or a roster refusal is exit 3: "{file}: {why}".
   5. Duplicate name [ASSUMES D10]: when another seat carries the same name ignoring case, exit 1: "`{n}` already names {machine name} ({id}) — two seats cannot answer to one name".
   6. The seat.
      - Agent: SeatId::mint(), kind Agent.
      - Human: identity_or_mint(&platform::machine_dir()), kind Human. Where the identity is already listed, exit 1 [ASSUMES D11]: "this machine's identity {machine name} ({id}) is already [seats.{id}] in {file}". The row's name is --name when given, else the identity's own name, else none. The verb never edits identity.toml's name.
   7. Build the new body: the file text, a '\n' when the file does not end with one, then seat_table(&seat, model).
      - Parse the whole new body as TOML before writing. A failure is exit 3: "{file} would not parse after the edit: {e}".
      - Then write_atomic.
   8. Read back: run roster_in on the re-read file. It must hold the id with that kind, name and model. Otherwise exit 3: "{file} was written and does not read [seats.{id}] back".
   9. Output.
      - stdout: the full id and a newline.
      - stderr: "added: {kind} {machine name} — [seats.{id}] in {file}".
      - For a human whose identity was minted, stderr also carries "identity: minted at {machine dir}/identity.toml".
      - For an agent, stderr also carries "next: git worktree add {worktrees dir}/{machine name} <a branch>, then `fleet start` renders it".

title: fleet start reads [seats.<id>] through core's roster: agent seats render as <slug>-<short> rows carrying id and kind, human seats are never rendered, chosen_name goes
description:

title: Add core's seat identity: the uuid crate, SeatId, Kind, the [seats.<id>] reader, identity.toml, and the one resolver every seat argument goes through
description:
SPEC (split a1 of fleet-iex, drafted 2026-09-23).
Core gains the one definition of what a seat is. Nothing calls it yet; a2 to a4 wire it in.

A seat is {id, kind, name?}:
- The id is a UUID v7, stored whole. It displays as its full 36-character lowercase form and shows as an 8-character short id [ASSUMES D1: the LAST 8 hex digits].
- kind is human | agent.
- name is optional.

A seat's machine-facing name is <slug>-<short>. The slug is the name lowercased and reduced to [a-z0-9-], or the kind when there is no name.

The reader turns fleet.toml's [seats.<id>] tables into seats. It refuses the shapes the clean break retires (name-keyed tables, chosen_name).

The resolver turns any seat argument into exactly one seat, or refuses with the reason. It accepts a full id, an 8+ hex fragment, a name, or a machine name.

core also reads and mints <machine dir>/identity.toml.

Sites (at HEAD bde60be):
- core/Cargo.toml:18-29: the dependency comment ("The same three the controller carries, no new crate") and [dependencies].
- Cargo.lock: uuid and getrandom 0.4 enter.
- core/src/seat/mod.rs:1-8: the module list (only `pub mod retire;` today).
- New file core/src/seat/identity.rs.
- The parser this copies. It is read here, not changed; a2 deletes it.
  - controller/src/policy.rs:157-177 RawSeatEntry/RawSeats.
  - controller/src/policy.rs:392-476: SEAT_ACTIVE, SEAT_PARKED, SEAT_PARKED_ALIASES, SeatEntry, seats_in and parked_status.
  - Its tests, controller/src/policy.rs:1076-1200.
- The TOML escaper to copy: controller/src/lifecycle.rs:166-186 `basic`. Core may not import it (cli/tests/workspace.rs:50 refuses a core→controller edge).
- The exit mapping: core/src/item/mod.rs:38-70 (Stop::refused, ::usage, ::could_not_tell).
- New test file core/tests/seat_identity.rs.
Remedy:
1. core/Cargo.toml: add the uuid dependency under [dependencies].
   - The line is `uuid = { version = "=1.23.3", default-features = false, features = ["std", "v7"] }`.
   - Pin it exactly in this member only, the way controller/Cargo.toml:41-45 pins jiff. Do not add it to the workspace table.
   - Rewrite the comment above [dependencies] so it names four crates, and add this paragraph: "uuid: a seat's id is a UUID v7, minted here and stored whole, because an id cut down to what is unique inside one fleet stops being unique when seats carry into a workspace or onto another machine (fleet-iex R1, Alberto's ruling). Default features off; `v7` for `now_v7` (it pulls the rng, getrandom) and `std`. The `serde` feature is not taken: a SeatId serializes through its own string form."
   - Keep the sentence saying core depends on no other member.
   - Then run `cargo update -p uuid --precise 1.23.3`. Both 1.23.3 and getrandom 0.4.x are already in the local registry.
2. core/src/seat/identity.rs. The public API, with these exact names:
   a. `pub struct SeatId(uuid::Uuid)`
      - Derives: Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, PartialOrd, Ord, Debug.
      - `SeatId::mint()` calls `Uuid::now_v7()`.
      - `SeatId::parse(text: &str) -> Result<SeatId, String>` trims its input. It accepts only the 36-character 8-4-4-4-12 hyphenated form, in either case, and any UUID version. Its refusal text: "`{text}` is not a seat id — a seat id is 36 characters, 8-4-4-4-12 hex".
      - `Display` prints the lowercase hyphenated form.
      - `pub fn short(&self) -> String` returns the last 8 characters of the Display form [ASSUMES D1].
      - Hand-written serde Serialize/Deserialize go through the Display string.
   b. `pub enum Kind { Human, Agent }`
      - `as_str()` returns "human" or "agent".
      - `Kind::parse(&str) -> Option<Kind>` matches exact lowercase after a trim.
   c. `pub struct SeatRef { pub id: SeatId, pub name: Option<String>, pub kind: Kind }`
      - Derives: Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq.
      - `slug()`: trim the name and lowercase it (str::to_lowercase). Map every char outside [a-z0-9] to '-', collapse runs of '-' into one, and trim '-' from both ends. If nothing is left, or there is no name, the slug is kind.as_str().
      - `machine_name()` returns format!("{slug}-{short}").
      - Examples the tests pin: "Orla"→"orla", "Zoë Q."→"zo-q", "R2-D2"→"r2-d2", "  "→the kind.
   d. `pub struct Seat { pub seat: SeatRef, pub model: Option<String>, pub parked: bool }`: one [seats.<id>] table.
   e. Move SEAT_ACTIVE, SEAT_PARKED and SEAT_PARKED_ALIASES here verbatim from controller/src/policy.rs:396-402. Move parked_status with them, with its refusal text saying `[seats.{id}]`.
   f. `pub fn roster(policy: &toml::Table) -> Result<Vec<Seat>, String>` and `pub fn roster_in(body: &str) -> Result<Vec<Seat>, String>`. They read the `seats` table.
      - No `seats` table gives an empty Vec.
      - A `seats` value that is not a table gives Err("`seats` is not a table").
      - Keys are read in BTreeMap order, which for v7 ids is mint order.
      - Every key must parse as a SeatId. Otherwise: Err("[seats.{key}] is keyed by a name — a seat is keyed by its id now; `fleet seat add --agent --name {key}` mints one").
      - Every value must be a table.
      - `kind` is required. Missing: "[seats.{id}] carries no `kind` — say `kind = \"agent\"` or `kind = \"human\"`". An unknown word: "[seats.{id}] kind = \"{w}\" is neither `agent` nor `human`".
      - `name` is an optional string; it is trimmed, and a blank name is None.
      - `chosen_name` present: Err("[seats.{id}] carries `chosen_name`, which is `name` now").
      - `model` is optional, and a blank model is None. On a human row: Err("[seats.{id}] is a human seat and carries `model` — only an agent seat runs on a model") [ASSUMES D15].
      - `status` is read by parked_status. On a human row: Err("[seats.{id}] is a human seat and carries `status` — only an agent seat is parked") [ASSUMES D15].
      - Any other key is ignored, which is what controller/src/policy.rs:1113-1120 pins today.
   g. `pub enum Unresolved { Blank, Missing { arg: String, known: Vec<String> }, Ambiguous { arg: String, candidates: Vec<String> } }`
      - `code()` returns 2, 1 and 1 respectively.
      - Display texts:
        - Blank: "names no seat — the argument is empty".
        - Missing: "`{arg}` names no seat — the seats are {known joined ', ' or 'none'}".
        - Ambiguous: "`{arg}` names {n} seats — {candidates joined ', '} — say more of the id".
      - Each known seat or candidate prints as "{machine_name} ({full id})".
      - `impl From<Unresolved> for crate::item::Stop`: code 1 becomes Stop::refused and code 2 becomes Stop::usage, both with the Display text.
   h. `pub fn resolve(seats: &[SeatRef], arg: &str) -> Result<usize, Unresolved>` answers the index of the one seat. The rules, in order:
      - (i) Trim. An empty argument is Blank.
      - (ii) If arg parses as a full SeatId, the answer is exactly that id or Missing. No fragment logic runs.
      - (iii) Otherwise a seat is a candidate when any of these holds:
        - its name equals arg, ignoring ASCII case;
        - arg ends with '-' plus exactly 8 hex digits, and those 8 equal the seat's short(). This matches a machine name on its id part, so a rename moves nothing (R4).
        - arg is 8 or more characters of [0-9a-fA-F-], and the lowercase full id starts with it or ends with it [ASSUMES D1].
      - (iv) De-duplicate by id. Zero candidates is Missing, one is Ok, more than one is Ambiguous.
   i. The identity file.
      - `pub const IDENTITY: &str = "identity.toml"`.
      - `pub struct MachineIdentity { pub id: SeatId, pub name: Option<String> }`, with `as_ref() -> SeatRef` (kind Human).
      - `pub fn read_identity(machine_dir: &Path) -> Result<Option<MachineIdentity>, String>`:
        - An absent file is Ok(None).
        - A file that does not parse, with a missing or invalid `id`, or with `kind` other than "human" is Err("{path}: {why}").
        - Other keys are ignored.
      - `pub fn identity_or_mint(machine_dir: &Path) -> Result<(MachineIdentity, bool), String>`, where the bool means "minted by this call". The mint steps:
        1. create_dir_all(machine_dir).
        2. Write the text below to `identity.toml.{pid}.tmp`, opened create_new, and sync it.
        3. `std::fs::hard_link(tmp, identity.toml)`. This is atomic and never clobbers.
        4. Remove the tmp file.
        5. On AlreadyExists, read the file the other process linked and answer minted = false.
      - The file text, exactly: "# This machine's identity: who acts when a fleet verb runs here with no\n# --by and no FLEET_ACTOR. The id is the key; add `name = \"...\"` if you\n# want one. Written by fleet.\nid = \"{id}\"\nkind = \"human\"\n".
   j. `pub fn seat_table(seat: &SeatRef, model: Option<&str>) -> String` returns the text one appended table takes:
      - "\n[seats.{id}]\nkind = \"{kind}\"\n";
      - then a `name = "…"` line and a `model = "…"` line, each only when present;
      - each value escaped by a private copy of lifecycle.rs's `basic` (step 2 site above).
3. core/src/seat/mod.rs:
   - Add `pub mod identity;`.
   - Add one module-doc sentence: "`identity` is what a seat IS: its id, kind and name, the fleet.toml table that lists it, the machine's own identity file, and the one resolver every seat argument goes through."
4. There are no caller changes in this bead.
Acceptance (core/tests/seat_identity.rs):
1. mint:
   - 50 minted ids are all version 7.
   - Display is 36 lowercase characters.
   - parse(display) round-trips.
   - parse refuses the 32-character simple form and "orla", both with the refusal text above.
2. short [ASSUMES D1]:
   - 100 ids minted in one loop have pairwise-distinct short() values.
   - Their first 8 characters are all equal, unless the first and last id fall in different 65,536 ms buckets. The arm reads the buckets from the ids' own timestamp bits.
   - This arm is the proof that a v7 prefix is a clock.
3. slug and machine_name:
   - The four examples in step 2c.
   - A nameless agent's machine name is "agent-{short}". A nameless human's is "human-{short}".
4. roster:
   - A file holding one named agent (with model and status = "parked"), one named human and one nameless agent parses to three seats, in id order, with the right fields.
   - Each refusal in step 2f answers its exact text. The cases are: a name-keyed table, a missing kind, an unknown kind, chosen_name, model on a human, status on a human, and an unknown status word.
   - An unknown key is ignored.
   - A file with no [seats] is an empty roster.
   - The parked-status arms of controller/src/policy.rs:1132-1200 are carried over with id keys.
5. resolve:
   - Each of these finds the seat: its full id; a unique 8-character prefix; its unique short (suffix).
   - A 7-character fragment is Missing.
   - "ORLA" finds the seat named "Orla".
   - "wren-{short}" finds the seat named "Orla". This is the rename-stable machine name.
   - Two seats both named "Orla" give Ambiguous, code 1, listing both "{machine name} ({id})".
   - "" gives Blank, code 2.
   - Missing lists every known seat.
6. identity:
   - read_identity on an empty directory is None.
   - identity_or_mint writes the exact text and answers minted = true. A second call answers the same id with minted = false.
   - 8 threads minting into one fresh directory all answer one id.
   - kind = "agent" in the file is refused, naming the path.
7. cli/tests/workspace.rs stays green and unchanged: core still names no member of the workspace.

title: doctor core: one module finds the doctor checks through the layers and runs each one bounded; fleet run's runtime check runs through it
description:
SPEC (fleet-2u3.1, drafted 2026-09-23). The core half of `fleet doctor`, split off fleet-2u3.1 by size. It adds core/src/item/doctor.rs, which finds every `doctor/<name>/` entry the resolved layers carry, reads its doctor.toml, and runs its script through core's bounded runner with a verdict read off the exit. `fleet run`'s runtime check (the one doctor execution at HEAD) is rewritten onto it, so the verb in fleet-2u3.1 and the run share one runner. It adds no verb.

Behaviour after this lands:
- A doctor check is a `doctor/<name>/` directory as the resolver sees it. Resolution is PER FILE: `doctor/<name>/doctor.toml` and `doctor/<name>/<run>` each come from the highest layer that carries that path. A pack on top that carries a same-named entry shadows the lower one, and the defaults are the bottom layer. This is the rule run.rs already follows at 1009 and 1032.
- A check's LAYER is the layer that carries its doctor.toml.
- A check's exit gives its verdict: 0 is pass, 1 is finding, and anything else is could-not-tell. "Anything else" covers exit 3 (stale-branches' own "could not read"), exit 2, 127, and death by a signal. It also covers a timeout, a spawn failure, and an entry with no doctor.toml, no `run` key, or an unresolvable script. The aggregate verdict is could-not-tell if any check could not tell, else finding if any check found something, else pass.
- `fleet run` behaves as it does at HEAD, with one exception. A runtime check that runs past 60s is killed with its process group and the run stops at could-not-tell (exit 3). At HEAD it hangs, because run.rs:1033-1038 calls Command::output() with no bound. A check killed by a signal is also could-not-tell now. At HEAD it is refused with exit 1.

Sites (at HEAD bde60be):
- core/src/item/run.rs:75-84: RUNTIME_CHECK = "doctor/runtime-version", DOCTOR_TOML, PACK_DIR = "FLEET_PACK_DIR". All three are pub and only run.rs uses them (git grep finds no other reader; core/tests/pack.rs:547,654 spell "FLEET_PACK_DIR" literally).
- core/src/item/run.rs:287-288: run() builds the child path and calls the_doctor_is_green. :454 is rerun's child_path_for call. rerun runs no doctor.
- core/src/item/run.rs:794-797: `struct Pinned { runtime, pack }`, private. :799-817: manifest_of, private.
- core/src/item/run.rs:942-956: `fn child_path_for(pinned: &Pinned, base: &str) -> String`, private. It reads only pinned.runtime.name. :960-990: installer_bin, holding, is_program.
- core/src/item/run.rs:1003-1055: the_doctor_is_green. It finds the doctor.toml through packs.slot (1009-1015), reads `run` (1016-1031), resolves the script per file (1032), and runs `sh <script>` with FLEET_PACK_DIR = the declaring pack and PATH = child path (1034-1038). It has no timeout. An exit other than 0 is Stop::refused with the check's stdout (1039-1054), and a spawn failure is could_not_tell (1038).
- core/src/item/brief.rs:44-82: Packs { layers, resolution }, with slot() at 65 and read() at 74. :91-102: read_under.
- core/src/resolve.rs:56-64: Resolution.files maps a relative path to its carrier layer name. :267-271: slot_path. :369-388: the highest layer wins per path, and each lower copy is recorded in `shadowed`. :184-192: layers_over puts the defaults at the bottom.
- core/src/defaults.rs:42: LAYER = "defaults", the bottom layer's name.
- core/src/process.rs:78-80: deadline_cause. :190-243: run_bounded(cmd, timeout) -> Result<Output, String>, which spawns the child in its own process group, kills the group at the deadline, and sets stdin to null.
- core/src/store.rs:263: STORE_TIMEOUT = 60s, the precedent for a whole-call bound.
- core/src/pack.rs:21-29 is SLOTS (holds "doctor"). :150/:200 is Defect::DoctorWithoutDoctorToml. :770-778 is check_slots: an entry must hold doctor.toml. Nothing checks its contents.
- core/src/item/mod.rs:12-21: the item submodules. core/src/lib.rs:77-80 is the `run` paragraph of the module map.
- What each doctor.toml declares at HEAD: two keys, `description` (string) and `run` (the script's file name inside the entry). There is no `name` key, because the directory is the name. There is no exit table and no timeout. The files are core/defaults/doctor/{guards-installed,isolation-pair,runtime-version}/doctor.toml:1-2, packs/tiny/doctor/{guards-installed,stale-branches,verbs-on-path}/doctor.toml:1-2 and packs/ts/doctor/deno-version/doctor.toml:1-2.
- The exits the scripts use at HEAD:
  - 0/1: runtime-version run.sh:75,86,110,114; isolation-pair run.sh:32,72-73; verbs-on-path; deno-version.
  - First non-zero of `fleet guard <class> --check`: guards-installed (defaults run.sh:17-20, tiny run.sh:24-29). A `fleet` that is not on PATH makes this 127.
  - 0/1/3 with 3 winning: stale-branches run.sh:8-13,83-89.

Remedy:
1. New file core/src/item/doctor.rs. Register it with `pub mod doctor;` in core/src/item/mod.rs between `dispatch` and `gate` (:14-15). Add one paragraph to the core/src/lib.rs module map after :77-80: "`doctor` is the doctor slot as a runner: every `doctor/<name>/` entry the layers resolve, its doctor.toml's script run bounded, and the verdict its exit gives."
2. Constants in doctor.rs:
   - `pub const SLOT: &str = "doctor";`
   - `pub const DOCTOR_TOML: &str = "doctor.toml";` (moved from run.rs:80)
   - `pub const PACK_DIR: &str = "FLEET_PACK_DIR";` (moved from run.rs:84)
   - `pub const RUNTIME_VERSION: &str = "runtime-version";`
   - `pub const TIMEOUT: Duration = Duration::from_secs(60);` [ASSUMES D4]
   Delete RUNTIME_CHECK/DOCTOR_TOML/PACK_DIR from run.rs:75-84. run.rs imports what it needs from `super::doctor`.
3. `pub enum Verdict { Pass, Finding, CouldNotTell }` with:
   - `word()`: "pass" | "finding" | "could not tell"
   - `code()`: "pass" | "finding" | "could_not_tell" (the JSON spelling, which matches the exit table's row name for 3)
   - `exit() -> u8`: 0 | 1 | 3
   - `of_exit(code: Option<i32>) -> Verdict`: Some(0) → Pass, Some(1) → Finding, anything else including None → CouldNotTell
   - `pub fn aggregate<I: IntoIterator<Item = Verdict>>(all: I) -> Verdict`: CouldNotTell beats Finding beats Pass. An empty set is Pass.
4. `pub struct Entry { pub name: String, pub layer: String, pub root: PathBuf, pub description: Option<String>, pub script: Result<PathBuf, String> }`.
   - `root` is the carrier layer's root, which becomes FLEET_PACK_DIR.
   - `script` is Err(the reason) when the entry cannot be run. The reason strings are fixed:
     a. `doctor/<name>/doctor.toml` is not in packs.resolution.files: "`doctor/<name>` holds no doctor.toml". `layer` is then the carrier of the first resolved path under `doctor/<name>/`.
     b. The file is unreadable, or does not parse as TOML: "<path> does not parse as TOML: <e>". This is run.rs:1018-1023's wording.
     c. `run` is absent or not a string: "<path> names no `run` script for the check to run". This is run.rs:1024-1031's wording.
     d. packs.slot(`doctor/<name>/<run>`) fails: the Stop message slot() gives (brief.rs:66-71).
   - `description` is the `description` string, or None. Other keys are ignored: validating doctor.toml is `pack check`'s job, not the runner's.
5. `pub fn entries(packs: &Packs) -> Vec<Entry>` returns one Entry per distinct `<name>` among the resolution.files keys of the form `doctor/<name>/<anything>`, in name order (the BTreeMap order). `pub fn entry(packs: &Packs, name: &str) -> Option<Entry>` returns the same for one name.
6. `pub struct Invocation<'a> { pub pack_dir: &'a Path, pub path: &'a str, pub cwd: Option<&'a Path>, pub env: &'a [(&'a str, &'a std::ffi::OsStr)], pub timeout: Duration }` and `pub struct Checked { pub verdict: Verdict, pub exit: Option<i32>, pub stdout: String, pub stderr: String, pub line: String }`.
7. `pub fn run(entry: &Entry, how: &Invocation) -> Checked`:
   - If entry.script is Err(why), return {CouldNotTell, exit None, stdout "", stderr "", line why}. Nothing is spawned.
   - Otherwise build `Command::new("sh").arg(script)`. This is the same `sh <script>` as run.rs:1034. Set `.env(PACK_DIR, how.pack_dir).env("PATH", how.path)` and each of `how.env`, and `.current_dir(cwd)` when cwd is Some. Everything else is inherited, as at HEAD.
   - Run it with `crate::process::run_bounded(cmd, how.timeout)`.
     - Err(why) gives {CouldNotTell, exit None, line why}. `why` is deadline_cause's "did not answer within 60s" or run_bounded's "could not start sh: …".
     - Ok(out) gives exit = out.status.code(), verdict = Verdict::of_exit(exit), stdout and stderr lossy UTF-8.
   - `line` is the last non-empty trimmed line of stdout, else the last of stderr. With both empty it is "said nothing and exited <n>", or "was killed by a signal and said nothing" when exit is None.
8. `pub fn pinned(packs: &Packs) -> Vec<(Layer, Result<Runtime, String>)>`. It walks every non-defaults layer in layer order (top first) and keeps each whose manifest declares [runtime] as (layer, Ok(runtime)). A manifest that cannot be read or parsed gives (layer, Err(the manifest_of message)). It reads through run.rs's manifest_of (:799-817), made `pub(crate)`. This is the set of packs a runtime check measures.
9. Change run.rs:942 to `pub fn child_path_for(runtime: &str, base: &str) -> String`. The body is unchanged apart from `let name = runtime;`. The callers at :287 and :454 pass `&pinned.runtime.name`. It becomes pub so the verb (fleet-2u3.1) gives runtime-version rows the PATH `fleet run` gives their workflows, without a second copy.
10. Rewrite the_doctor_is_green (run.rs:1003-1055) onto the module. It keeps its signature and every message:
    - `doctor::entry(wiring.packs, RUNTIME_VERSION)`. On None, or on script Err from case (a), return Stop::could_not_tell with the message at :1010-1014 verbatim ("no installed pack carries `doctor/runtime-version/doctor.toml` — …"). On any other script Err(why), return Stop::could_not_tell(why).
    - `doctor::run(&entry, &Invocation { pack_dir: &pinned.pack.root, path, cwd: None, env: &[], timeout: doctor::TIMEOUT })`.
    - Pass is Ok(()).
    - A non-pass verdict with exit Some(_) is Stop::refused with the message at :1043-1054 verbatim, built from checked.stdout.
    - A non-pass verdict with exit None (timeout, spawn failure, signal) is Stop::could_not_tell("`<pack>`'s runtime check did not answer, so `<workflow>` is not opened — <checked.line>").
    - The function builds no Command itself.

Acceptance (core/tests/doctor.rs, new, on scratch layers built with fleet_core::embedded::write_all into a temp defaults dir as cli/tests/run.rs:51-56 does, and Packs::under over a temp packs dir):
1. Discovery, defaults only: entries() names are exactly [guards-installed, isolation-pair, runtime-version], each with layer "defaults", a script Ok ending in run.sh, and description Some.
2. Shadowing. Pack `scratch` carries doctor/guards-installed/{doctor.toml,run.sh} and doctor/fx-extra/{doctor.toml,run.sh}.
   - guards-installed's layer is "scratch" and its script is under scratch's root.
   - fx-extra appears with layer "scratch".
   - Per-file resolution: a second pack carries only doctor/isolation-pair/doctor.toml. It has layer "scratch2", and its script resolves to the defaults' run.sh.
   - Red-proof: remove the scratch copy and guards-installed's layer reads "defaults".
3. Unrunnable entries are could-not-tell and spawn nothing:
   - doctor/bare/run.sh with no doctor.toml → "`doctor/bare` holds no doctor.toml".
   - doctor.toml without `run` → "names no `run` script".
   - doctor.toml that is not TOML → "does not parse as TOML".
   - `run = "missing.sh"` → the slot message.
   - Each gives exit None.
4. Exit mapping. Scripts `exit 0`, `exit 1`, `exit 3`, `exit 2`, `exit 7` and `kill -9 $$` give Pass/0, Finding/1, CouldNotTell/3, CouldNotTell/2, CouldNotTell/7 and CouldNotTell/None.
   - aggregate([Pass, Finding]) = Finding. aggregate([Finding, CouldNotTell, Pass]) = CouldNotTell. aggregate([]) = Pass.
5. Line rule:
   - `printf 'a\nlast\n\n'; exit 1` → line "last".
   - `echo why >&2; exit 3` → line "why".
   - A silent `exit 1` → "said nothing and exited 1".
6. The bound. A script `sleep 30` run with timeout 200ms → CouldNotTell, exit None, line "did not answer within 200ms", returned in under 5s. RED-PROOF: with run() built on Command::output() (HEAD's shape) the arm runs 30s and fails its elapsed assertion.
7. Environment and cwd. A script prints $FLEET_PACK_DIR, $PWD, $PATH and one extra env pair. Each equals the Invocation's value.
8. pinned(): with layers [top (runtime), mid (no runtime), defaults], it returns [top] with Ok(runtime.name). A top layer whose pack.toml is not TOML returns (top, Err(_)).

title: Declare, check and document the supported versions of bd and Claude Code, as Deno's already is
description:
Raised by Alberto, 2026-09-23 (walkthrough fleet-alt.1 session): "is the current supported version of both beads and claude code documented anywhere in the project?" Ruling (AskUserQuestion): one bead — declare, check, document.

Measured at 6d456ce:
- bd: no supported version anywhere. docs/getting-started.md:39-41 names `bd` with no version, and core/src/store.rs carries only "measured on bd 1.2.2" comments. fleet-reb adds the first pin (1.3.0, checked).
- Claude Code: no project-declared version. A fleet MAY set `[substrate.claude_code] version = "…"` (or `[substrate] claude_code = "…"`) in fleet.toml (controller/src/policy.rs:628-648). The controller compares the running version each poll and writes substrate.moved on a mismatch (controller/src/run.rs:1093-1110). docs/ never mentions [substrate]. The only version in the tree is a test fixture, 2.1.261 (policy.rs:891, 1204). This box runs 2.1.280.
- Deno is the model to follow: packs/ts/pack.toml:10-12 declares 2.9.7, and the defaults' runtime-version doctor check measures it.

Remedy:
1. One place in the source declares fleet's SUPPORTED versions: bd (fleet-reb's constant, reused, not a second copy) and Claude Code. The Claude Code value is the version the claude_code adapter's ring suites last passed on this box, measured at pickup and recorded on this bead with the run.
2. A doctor check per tool in core/defaults/doctor/, modelled on runtime-version, compares the installed version with the declared one. A mismatch is named with the install or upgrade line; the check reports and does not refuse.
3. When a fleet sets no [substrate] pin, the declared Claude Code version is the controller's default expectation, so substrate.moved means "not the version fleet supports". A fleet's own [substrate] pin still wins.
4. docs/getting-started.md gains a "What fleet runs on" table: bd, Claude Code, Deno (from packs/ts/pack.toml) and git, each with its supported version and the doctor check that measures it. docs/seats.md or docs/status.md documents [substrate] and substrate.moved.
5. CONTRIBUTING.md says a supported-version move is one constant plus a re-measure, as fleet-reb's is.

Acceptance: each doctor check exits 0 on the declared version and names the mismatch on another (a stub binary answering a different version). title: fleet seat attach <seat> opens the seat's tmux session read-only, and --write takes the keyboard
description:
SPEC (fleet-2u3.13, flight 11's attach row, drafted 2026-09-25, revised 2026-09-25). Sites at 2a48e90. Blocked by fleet-rge6.1 (`Host::attach`, `SOCKET`, `session_for`). This bead is reparented under the flight 11 epic and carries the row's body. Its earlier text, "a requirement carried over, not a spec", is superseded.

**Behaviour.** A person watches a seat work in their own terminal, and fleet renders nothing. The carried audit said "the agent adapter trait has no attach verb". The answer is that attach belongs to the host, not the adapter (ruling 2). Any agent running under tmux gets it, and it needs no agent verb.

- A new verb, `fleet seat attach <seat> [--write] [--project <name>]`: `SeatVerb::Attach(attach::AttachArgs)` in cli/src/main.rs (enum at 374-434, dispatch at 754-765), implemented in the new cli/src/attach.rs. Its `long_about`: "open a seat's session in this terminal, read-only unless --write. Detach with the tmux prefix and d. Typing under --write is typing as the seat: the session's verbs act as it."
- The steps:
  1. Resolve the project through `transient::resolved` (cli/src/transient.rs:574-593). A `--project` that does not match exits 2.
  2. Resolve the seat through the seat list's resolver, exactly as `fleet seat nudge` does (`transient::seat_named`, used at cli/src/nudge.rs:62). It takes a full id, eight or more hex digits, a name or a machine name.
  3. Call `host.list()` on socket `fleet` (E1). With no session for `session_for(seat)` it exits 4 (`Exit::NoSession`): "`<machine name>` has no session on fleet". An unreadable host exits 3 with the host's cause.
  4. A dead pane can still be attached, because remain-on-exit keeps its last screen. The verb first prints "the session ended with status N", which is how a person reads why a start failed.
  5. Exec `host.attach(session, write)` in place of this process (`std::os::unix::process::CommandExt::exec`): `tmux -L fleet attach-session -t <seat id>`, with `-r` unless `--write` is given. Read-only mode drops the person's keys.
- The child's environment has `$TMUX` removed, so a person already inside their own tmux gets a nested client instead of tmux's refusal. fleet does no TTY check of its own; tmux's refusal and its exit pass straight through.
- The verb needs no projection and no running controller, since tmux holds the sessions across a controller restart (ruling 3). It writes nothing to the stream. `--write` prints one line before the exec: "typing into <machine name>'s session acts as that seat".

**Sites.** cli/src/main.rs 374-434 and 754-765; cli/src/attach.rs (new); cli/tests/attach.rs (new). fleet-rge6.6's docs pass writes the "Attaching to a seat" section of docs/seats.md.

**Interfaces consumed.** From fleet-rge6.1: `Host::attach`, `Host::list`, `SOCKET`, `session_for`, `TmuxHost::resolve`, and `fleet-tmux-stub` for the tests (E7). **Produced:** the verb, which a cockpit can wrap. A web terminal over tmux control mode is out of scope (ruling 9).

**Acceptance.** cli/tests/attach.rs runs with `FLEET_TMUX_BIN` pointing at `fleet-tmux-stub` (fleet-rge6.1). The stub answers `list-panes` from its state and records `attach-session`'s argv. The arms:
- `fleet seat attach <machine name>` execs `-L fleet -f /dev/null attach-session -r -t <seat id>`;
- `--write` drops `-r`;
- the full id and the bare name produce the same argv;
- a seat with no session exits 4 and nothing is exec'd;
- a dead pane prints its status line and still execs;
- an unknown seat exits with the resolver's code;
- `--project other` exits 2;
- `TMUX` is absent from the child's environment.

A manual check under the real tmux is recorded on the bead: read-only keys do nothing, `--write` types, and detaching leaves the seat running.

**Reviewer calls 2026-09-25.** (1) `--write` appends one `seat.attached {seat, mode: "write", at}` to the stream before the exec, so a keyboard taken over a seat is on the record; a read-only attach writes nothing. (2) An attach does not hold off the controller's nudge or feed: nothing needs that arbitration yet, and a person typing under `--write` sees a paste arrive. Revisit when a cockpit wraps the verb.
