notes:
SPEC (fleet-2u3.1, drafted 2026-09-23). CARRIED from cli PRD P1 (brain/prds/fleet-cli-prd.md:990-993) and packs PRD P1 (brain/prds/fleet-packs-prd.md:595). The audit found it NOT BUILT: there is no Doctor arm in cli/src/main.rs:563-585, and only doctor/runtime-version ever runs, inside `fleet run` (core/src/item/run.rs:79, 288). This bead adds the verb over DRAFT 1's core module. It answers fleet-ght's first clause ("which verb runs pack doctors": this one). fleet-ght's other two clauses stay fleet-ght's. fleet-0ml (adopt-board), fleet-2jt and fleet-reb (version checks) add entries under core/defaults/doctor/, which this verb runs with no code change. Behaviour: - `fleet doctor [...] [--json] [--packs-dir ]`. - From inside a project, it resolves the project (the item verbs' walk) and the pack layers. It then runs every doctor check the layers carry in name order, or only the checks named. It prints one row per check as each finishes, then a summary line. It exits with the aggregate: 0 when every check passed, 1 when a check reported a finding, 3 when a check could not tell. 3 wins over 1. - The verb writes nothing. What a check's own script does is that check's business: isolation-pair makes and removes a scratch directory. Sites (at HEAD bde60be): - cli/src/main.rs: - :11-24: the module list. - :60-302: `enum Family`. Status is at :262-274 and Prime at :291-301. - :542-585: dispatch(). - :1285-1288, :1295-1322: the help-shape arms (debug_assert, under 80 columns, which walk every subcommand). - :1327-1335: the_help_page_measured_above_lists_every_family, with its list at :1329. - cli/src/item.rs: - :202-214: RunArgs, the `--packs-dir` flag convention. - :318-346: how run builds Packs and the child path. Packs::under is at :320, current_exe at :324, platform::child_path(&platform::home_dir()) at :328. - :734-736: stop_exit (private). - :743-771: `enum Human`, with stdout normally and stderr under --json (private). - :775-791: answered and refused (private). - :875-889: Here { project.root, packs_dir, defaults_dir, … }. - :996-1000: resolve_at. - cli/src/envelope.rs:22-39: ok() and refusal(). The key order is fixed, and data is serialized by serde_json with preserve_order off, so data's keys come out alphabetically. - cli/src/exit.rs:12-40: the table (0 Done, 1 Refused, 2 Usage, 3 CouldNotTell), with class() at :46-56. - cli/src/ui.rs:52-59: Tone { Good, Bad, Flat }. :93-107: Ui::status(stream, tone, verb, subject, outcome) renders "verb subject — outcome". - controller/src/platform/mod.rs:89-91: home_dir. :108-122: child_path (constructed, never inherited). - core/src/item/run.rs:120-150: ENV_BIN = "FLEET_BIN" and ENV_PROJECT = "FLEET_PROJECT". - cli/tests/run.rs: - :51-56: defaults_into. - :166-300: Rig. - :318-333: run_on_path, which passes --packs-dir, sets current_dir to the project and applies .hermetic(home, machine, claude_bin). - :277-292: runtime_only_in_the_installers_bin. - controller/tests/common/hermetic.rs: vars(). With no claude_bin it sets FLEET_CLAUDE_BIN to a refusing stub. - The checks the layers carry at HEAD: - The defaults carry guards-installed, isolation-pair and runtime-version (core/defaults/doctor/*, core/defaults/assets/shadow-registry.toml:21-41). - tiny carries guards-installed (a shadow), stale-branches and verbs-on-path (packs/tiny/doctor/*). - ts carries deno-version (packs/ts/doctor/deno-version/*). - runtime-version with no FLEET_PACK_DIR reads `$here/../..`, the defaults root, which has no pack.toml. It then says "broken" (core/defaults/doctor/runtime-version/run.sh:26-33). That is why the verb runs it per pinned pack (step 5). - docs: - docs/conventions.md:172-176 lists the --json verbs. :215-231 is "Verbs whose exit means something narrower". - docs/packs.md:82-83 lists the defaults' doctor entries. :336 is "`doctor//` holds `doctor.toml`". - docs/guards.md:323-326 is guards-installed. - docs/runs.md:88-91 is fleet run's runtime check. Remedy: 1. New file cli/src/doctor.rs. Add `mod doctor;` in the main.rs module list between `claude` and `envelope` (:11-12). In item.rs, make stop_exit (:734), Human (:743) and refused (:785) `pub(crate)`. No other change goes into item.rs. 2. Usage. `#[derive(clap::Args)] pub struct DoctorArgs` has: - `checks: Vec` (value_name "CHECK"): "the checks to run, by name; every check when none is named" - `#[arg(long)] json: bool`: "print the outcome as one JSON document" - `#[arg(long = "packs-dir", value_name = "DIR")] packs_dir: Option`: "where the packs are installed" Add `Doctor(doctor::DoctorArgs)` to `enum Family` after Status (:274), with the help text in step 10. Add the arm `Family::Doctor(args) => Ok(doctor::command(&ui, &args)),` to dispatch() after the Status arm (:582). 3. Resolve before anything runs: - `item::resolve_at(args.packs_dir.clone())`, then `Packs::under(&here.packs_dir, &here.defaults_dir)`. Either failing is the verb's own refusal: `fleet doctor: ` on stderr, the refusal envelope under --json, and exit stop_exit(stop.code). That is 3 for no project and for layers that do not resolve. - `let all = doctor::entries(&packs);` Named checks are deduplicated, keeping first-given order. Each must be the name of one of `all`. Otherwise the verb stops with usage (exit 2) before any check runs: "no doctor check named `` — the layers carry: " [ASSUMES D6]. Rows run in `all`'s name order, filtered to the named set when names are given. 4. Every ordinary check (each Entry except runtime-version) runs with doctor::run(&entry, &Invocation) where: - pack_dir = entry.root (the doctor.toml's carrier layer) - path = this process's PATH, or "" when unset [ASSUMES D3] - cwd = Some(&here.project.root). stale-branches reads the project file from its cwd (packs/tiny/doctor/stale-branches/run.sh:17-23), and `fleet guard --check` walks up from it (cli/src/main.rs:1111-1115). - env = [(ENV_PROJECT, project root), (ENV_BIN, std::env::current_exe())]. A current_exe failure is the verb's own could-not-tell, as run.rs's is (item.rs:324-326). - timeout = doctor::TIMEOUT (60s) [ASSUMES D4] 5. runtime-version runs through fleet run's own path, not a copy of it [ASSUMES D2]: - For each (layer, pin) in doctor::pinned(&packs), in layer order, run one row with `measures` = layer.name. - Ok(runtime): run the resolved runtime-version entry with pack_dir = layer.root and path = `fleet_core::item::run::child_path_for(&runtime.name, &platform::child_path(&platform::home_dir()))`. That is the PATH run.rs:287 hands the run's own doctor, bundle and run lines. cwd, env and timeout are as in step 4. - Err(why): a could-not-tell row whose line is `why`, and nothing is spawned. - When pinned() is empty, print one row: verdict pass, exit null, measures null, line "nothing pinned: no installed pack declares a [runtime] table". Nothing is spawned. - A pack that shadows doctor/runtime-version is honoured, because the entry is resolved and not assumed. Its rows show that pack as layer. 6. Human output. Each row goes to Human::under(args.json) (stdout, or stderr under --json) as soon as its check returns: - The row is `ui.line(tone, verdict.word(), subject, Some(&checked.line))`. Tone is Good for pass and Bad otherwise. subject is " ()", or " for ()" on a runtime-version row. So it renders as `pass isolation-pair (defaults) — isolation-pair: holds` and `finding runtime-version for scratch (defaults) — runtime-version: broken — …`. - A row that did not pass is followed by every non-empty line of the check's stdout and then its stderr, each prefixed with two spaces. These are the lines a person acts on: the four --check lines, stale-branches' delete lines. - After the rows comes one summary line: `ui.line(tone, "doctor", " checks" | "1 check", Some("

pass, finding, could not tell"))`. Tone is Good when the aggregate is pass and Bad otherwise. 7. The --json envelope [ASSUMES D1]. stdout carries exactly one line: `{"ok":true,"verb":"doctor","data":{"checks":[…],"counts":{"could_not_tell":c,"finding":f,"pass":p},"verdict":"pass"|"finding"|"could_not_tell"}}` Each check object is `{"description":,"exit":,"layer":"","line":"","measures":,"name":"","stderr":"","stdout":"","verdict":"pass"|"finding"|"could_not_tell"}`. The keys are alphabetical, as envelope.rs:13-17 says they will be. ok is true whatever the aggregate: the report IS the outcome, and the exit code (0/1/3) is the aggregate, unchanged by the flag. ok:false is kept for the verb's own refusals in step 3, which are refusal(verb, exit, why) with code "could_not_tell" or "usage". 8. Exit: `Exit::from_status(doctor::aggregate(verdicts).exit())`. That is 0 when all rows passed, 1 when any row reported a finding and none could not tell, and 3 when any row could not tell. Here is how each check's own exit maps onto that. Today's doctor.toml declares no exit semantics; its keys are only `description` and `run`. - 0 → pass. - 1 → finding. This is every script's red at HEAD. - 3 → could not tell. stale-branches' "could not read" (run.sh:8-13). - 2, 127, any other code, a signal, a timeout, a spawn failure, or an unrunnable entry → could not tell. The doctor's aggregate reproduces stale-branches' own precedence: a partial sweep is not a clean one. 9. Sequential, one check at a time. The verb holds no lock and needs no store, and nothing here starts a session. 10. Help text. Every line must be under 80 columns; main.rs:1295 checks it. The about is "run the doctor checks the pack layers carry". long_about: ``` run the doctor checks the pack layers carry: every doctor// entry resolved through the layers, the defaults at the bottom and each installed pack above, a pack's entry replacing a lower one of the same name. Name checks to run those alone. Each check runs its doctor.toml's `run` script with sh from the project root, bounded at 60 seconds, with FLEET_PACK_DIR naming the pack that carries it. runtime-version runs once for each pack that declares a [runtime] table, on the PATH `fleet run` gives that pack's workflows. One row per check: pass, finding or could not tell, its name, its layer and its last line; a row that did not pass is followed by all it printed. It writes nothing. Exit 0 when every check passed, 1 when one reported a finding, 3 when one could not tell — it exited 3 or anything but 0 and 1, was killed, or did not answer in time. 3 wins over 1. --json prints one document whose data carries every row, with the same exit. ``` 11. Add "doctor" to the family list at main.rs:1329. 12. Docs, written with the docs skill (each claim verified, and the review note on this bead): - docs/conventions.md: add `fleet doctor` to the --json list (:172-176). Add a bullet to "Verbs whose exit means something narrower" (:215-231): 0/1/3 as in step 8, and under --json ok is true whatever the aggregate, with data.verdict carrying it. - docs/packs.md: after :336, add "Doctor checks": doctor.toml's two keys, the per-file shadowing, the cwd, FLEET_PACK_DIR/FLEET_PROJECT/FLEET_BIN, the 60s bound, the exit mapping and runtime-version's once-per-pinned-pack rule. - docs/guards.md:323-326: "`fleet doctor` runs it." - docs/runs.md:88-91: the check fleet run runs is the one `fleet doctor runtime-version` runs, bounded at 60 seconds. Acceptance. There is a new binary-driven suite, cli/tests/doctor.rs. Its Rig is modelled on cli/tests/run.rs:166-333: - a temp root holding project/ (with fleet.toml), machine/ (defaults_into) and stubs/ - `--packs-dir machine/packs`, current_dir project, `.hermetic(home, machine, Some(stubs/claude))`, NO_COLOR=1 - `.env_remove("CLAUDE_SECURESTORAGE_CONFIG_DIR")` - PATH = stubs : the directory of env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_fleet") : the process PATH The claude stub answers the isolation pair: when CLAUDE_SECURESTORAGE_CONFIG_DIR is set, it prints `{"loggedIn": true}` and exits 0; otherwise it prints `{"loggedIn": false}` and exits 1. No board is needed, and no arm runs bd. 1. The defaults, all green. fleet.toml is `[project]\nitem_prefix = "fx"\n` and no pack is installed. - Exit 0. - stdout's rows, in order: `pass guards-installed (defaults) — record bare-id: configured — [project] item_prefix` `pass isolation-pair (defaults) — isolation-pair: holds` `pass runtime-version (defaults) — nothing pinned: no installed pack declares a [runtime] table` - The last line is `doctor 3 checks — 3 pass, 0 finding, 0 could not tell`. 2. A finding. As arm 1, but fleet.toml has no item_prefix. - Exit 1. - The guards-installed row starts `finding guards-installed (defaults)`, and a following two-space-indented line contains `record bare-id: not configured`. - The other two rows pass. - The summary reads `2 pass, 1 finding, 0 could not tell`. Arm 1 is the control. 3. Could-not-tell wins. As arm 1, plus pack `scratch` carrying doctor/fx-unread (`echo unreadable >&2; exit 3`), doctor/fx-found (`echo found; exit 1`) and doctor/fx-seven (`exit 7`). - Exit 3. - The rows read `could not tell fx-unread (scratch) — unreadable`, `finding fx-found (scratch) — found` and `could not tell fx-seven (scratch) — said nothing and exited 7`. - RED-PROOF: delete fx-unread and fx-seven, and the same rig exits 1. 4. title: The SDK takes a returned delivery as carried: a re-flown returned item is skipped as RETAKEN, and until(delivered) answers the old commit
description:
FINDING from walkthrough fleet-alt.1's spec pass, 2026-09-23 (the fleet-zlk research). Verified by reading packs/ts/assets/sdk/mod.ts at 31c0c01; no arm demonstrates it yet. Alberto: "File the SDK-returns bug now".

F [Required] correctness packs/ts/assets/sdk/mod.ts:389-395, 466-486. spawn() closes a step as `${RETAKEN}<commit>` when ANY item.delivered for the item sits at or below this execution's FLEET_STREAM_SEQ, and until(items, "delivered") answers the latest item.delivered payload from anywhere on the stream. Neither looks at item.returned. So an item whose delivery a reviewer RETURNED, and whose builder was then retired (which withdraws the order, leaving the item open and ready), is skipped on the next flight as already delivered, with the returned commit. That flight proceeds to review or land a commit whose last verdict is RETURNED. land refuses it (core/src/item/land.rs accepted_commit), but the item is never rebuilt, and the flight spends its slot.

Fence: mod.ts:187-195. RETAKEN exists for "an item a failed run delivered and left behind", at or below the position this execution started from. The fence holds for a delivery nobody judged; it does not hold for a delivery a verdict returned.

Remedy:
- spawn() counts a delivery as carried only when no item.returned for the same item follows it at or below FLEET_STREAM_SEQ.
- until(items, "delivered") answers, per item, the latest item.delivered that no later item.returned follows. An item whose latest delivery was returned is still outstanding.
- The same rule applies to item.landed where it closes the item: a landed item is never a carried delivery to review.
- The comment at mod.ts:187-195 says so.
Under fleet-zlk this moves to the store's timeline. This bead is the fix on today's stream.

Acceptance, with the SDK's own test rig (packs/ts/assets/sdk/testdata/, verbs_test.ts or takeoff_test.ts):
- AC1 A stream holding item.delivered then item.returned for X, below the start seq: spawn dispatches X (no RETAKEN). Shown red against today's code first.
- AC2 The same stream without the return still answers RETAKEN (the fence).
- AC3 until([X], "delivered") with delivered, returned, delivered answers the second commit; with delivered then returned it waits.
Gate line: `deno test` for packs/ts/assets/sdk green; the reviewer runs the full suite, ran or cached, at landing.

SPEC'D to the zero-clarification bar.
notes: Landed 91a8b8d: a private standing(clearedBy, upTo) replays item.delivered against the kinds that clear it, in seq order. spawn() takes returned and landed at or below FLEET_STREAM_SEQ, so a returned or landed delivery is not carried and the item is dispatched. until(items,'delivered') takes returned only. RULED AT REVIEW: a landing does not clear a delivery for until, so a workflow waiting on a landed item gets its delivery rather than waiting forever (the spec's landing bullet is about the carried check). The fence comment on Run.spawn says so. Arms in verbs_test.ts: AC1 (delivered then returned, and delivered then landed, dispatch; red first), AC2 (no return: RETAKEN; a return above the start seq is not read), AC3 (returned waits, redelivered answers the second commit; landed answers its delivery). deno test 31/31; full Rust suite 1002/1002. title: Rename gates: the human pause is a hold, its answer a clearance, and automated pass/fail conditions are checks
description:
FINDING from walkthrough fleet-alt.1, 2026-09-23, raised while reading core/src/store.rs:206-224. Alberto, verbatim:
"gates. same thing as above. explain it to me, what it is, where it came from, why we need it. the word gate matches our flying analogies so im not opposed to keeping it i just wanna make sure that everything borrowed from beads makes sense and is well defined inside of fleet. other tools have different names for this like checks so it might be worth exploring what the canonical terms out there are"

Ruling (AskUserQuestion, 2026-09-23): adopt hold / clearance / checks. The human pause is a HOLD, its answer is a CLEARANCE, and automated pass/fail conditions are CHECKS.

Where the word comes from: bd's gate is an "async wait condition that blocks workflow steps", with types human, timer, gh:run, gh:pr and bead (`bd gate --help`, bd 1.2.2). fleet uses only `human`: fleet ask raises one (Store::gate, core/src/store.rs:206-212), the item leaves the ready set, and fleet answer resolves it (Store::resolve_gate, :223-224).

The five senses of "gate" inside fleet today (39 source files mention it), each mapped under the ruling:
1. bd's human gate, the question that parks an item: core/src/item/gate.rs and Store::gate/open_gates/resolve_gate. Becomes a HOLD; answering it is its CLEARANCE. The verbs fleet ask / fleet answer and the word "parked" already fit, and the spec pass decides whether the verbs are renamed.
2. The builder's gate, the command handed by fleet dispatch --touched (11 hits for "builder's gate"). Becomes a CHECK.
3. The landing's gate rows, each condition fleet land verifies before its push (6 hits for "gate row"). Become CHECKS.
4. The [gates] policy table (core/src/policy.rs:25-32, 71-97): ci_marker, tool_commands, release_ref_glob and the prod_* targets. These are not all checks. The spec pass names the table from what it holds.
5. The controller's routine gate, controller/src/routines/gate.rs, which decides whether a routine fires. The spec pass decides whether that is a check or a trigger condition with its own name.

Canonical terms elsewhere, from general knowledge and to be surveyed in the spec pass: automated pass/fail is a "check" (GitHub status checks, the Checks API) or a "quality gate" (SonarQube, Azure Pipelines release gates); a human pause is an "approval" (GitHub environments, GitLab), a "manual judgment" (Spinnaker), an "input" (Jenkins), a "suspend" (Argo) or an "interrupt" (LangGraph).

title: Design: a seat is an identity with a UUID, an optional name and a kind (human or agent), and humans hold seats
description:
FINDING from walkthrough fleet-alt.1, 2026-09-23, raised while reading core/src/store.rs:143-242. Alberto, verbatim:
"seats. i keep seeing it mentioned everywhere. explain it to me, what it is, where it came from, why we need it. if it's what i think it is, a string that is meant to represent a human or agent then i have follow-ups: the id of a seat cant be the name, the name should be optional and seat id should be a short id from the uuid crate. earlier you asked me that we need to ask the user for a name during create so that assigned_by can use it. we shouldnt have to ask the user that. during create the human should get an autogenerated uuid and an entry on fleet.toml with name empty, they can add their name if they want. later on if we have things like a cloud offering and workspaces, etc. those seats and their ids should carry over. a seat should also say whether it's a human or an agent."

Rulings (AskUserQuestion, 2026-09-23):
- A seat's id is a full UUID v7, stored whole and displayed as a short prefix. Every command that takes a seat accepts the id, any unique prefix of it, or a unique name. Rationale: a truncated id is unique within one fleet only, and seats carry over into future workspaces.
- A seat has an optional name and a kind: human or agent.
- A human's seat is a MACHINE IDENTITY plus a PROJECT ROW. Each machine keeps "who I am" (id, kind human, optional name) in the machine directory. The project's fleet.toml lists seats by id. A new collaborator's first command creates their machine identity and offers to add it to the project. Nobody is asked for a name.

Today, at primary 0f8ad4c:
- A seat is an agent slot: a seat-list row in <machine dir>/config.json, a worktree, and a session the controller keeps alive (brain/fleet-vision.md:29-30; docs/seats.md, Terms).
- Named seats are [seats.<name>] in fleet.toml, keyed by name, with chosen_name as a display name (docs/seats.md:40-60). Transient seats are named transient-<n>.
- Humans are not seats. They are a free-string actor: --by, or FLEET_ACTOR / BEADS_ACTOR (cli/src/item.rs:1165-1175), written into bd's audit trail and every note.
- The name is the id. core/src/lib.rs:90-97: retire must withdraw every order a seat holds because the next spawn takes the lowest free transient-<n> and would inherit a standing order. A unique id removes that class of bug.

Constraints for the design pass:
- core carries only serde, serde_json and toml (core/Cargo.toml:18-29). Adding `uuid` is Alberto's ruling above; the manifest comment is updated with the reason.
- Everything keyed by seat name today moves to the id: the seat list, worktree and session names, the assignee and orders.seat (fleet-0q4's SeatName becomes SeatId), --to, and fleet seat retire.
- The actor (`by`) becomes a seat id, so a human's acts carry their seat.
- The controller manages agent seats only. A human seat has no session, worktree or revive.
- Migration of existing fleet.toml [seats.<name>] tables and seat-list rows: the spec pass decides, given release/0.1.0 is not yet out.

Related: fleet-0q4 (SeatName → SeatId in the domain types), fleet-zlk (assignee vs orders.seat).

Acceptance: a design note on this bead ruled by Alberto, then implementation beads split from it.

title: Adopt an existing board: a read-only scan verb and a mapping skill for projects adding fleet
description:
FINDING from walkthrough fleet-alt.1, 2026-09-23. Raised by Alberto, verbatim: "we're gonna need either a verb or an agent skill that helps users normalize data if they're adding fleet to an existing project. if the user wants to fly beads that use different conventions wouldnt the tool throw an error? for example if the existing beads were using metadata.orders but with slightly different schema"

Fence: none. No verb, doc or skill covers adopting an existing board today: `git grep -n -i 'adopt\|existing project\|existing board\|onboard' -- docs cli/src/main.rs` finds nothing.

Shape (recommended in the sitting, Alberto chose to file it as two parts under one bead):
1. A READ-ONLY VERB, which measures. It scans the project's board and reports, with counts and example ids:
   - items carrying names fleet owns but did not write (after fleet-4j6, anything under the `fleet` key or `fleet:` labels that fails fleet's schema);
   - foreign conventions a person may want mapped into fleet's: an existing order-like metadata key, an existing notion of assignee or reviewer, and labels or types the project's rules would need to match;
   - notes carrying fleet's marker words, until fleet-zlk retires the prose grammar.
   It writes nothing. It uses the shared exit codes: 0 means nothing to adopt, 1 means found and listed, 3 means the board could not be read. Candidate homes are `fleet adopt --check` or a check in the defaults' doctor slot; the spec pass picks one.
2. A SKILL, which applies judgement. It walks a person through the verb's report: what each foreign convention means, how it maps onto fleet's (for example "your orders.owner is our seat"), and the migration writes, each one confirmed by the person before it is made and read back after.

Depends on fleet-4j6: until fleet's own keys are namespaced, "foreign" and "fleet's" cannot be told apart on the board.

Acceptance: the verb's suite drives a fixture board with a foreign metadata.orders, a `run` label that is not fleet's, and marker words in a person's note, and the report names each one. The skill is exercised once against that fixture board, and the transcript is on the bead.
Gate line: touched suites green; the reviewer runs the full suite, ran or cached, at landing.

THIS IS A FINDING, NOT A SPEC: it is specced before anyone works it; do not work it as filed.
notes:
SPEC (walkthrough fleet-alt.1 spec pass, 2026-09-23). Ruling (Alberto, AskUserQuestion): the read-only scan is A DOCTOR CHECK, run by fleet doctor (fleet-2u3.1), and the mapping skill reads its report.
- The check lives in the defaults' doctor slot (core/defaults/doctor/adopt-board/, with doctor.toml and a script), beside guards-installed, isolation-pair and runtime-version.
- It READS THE BOARD THROUGH FLEET, never through bd directly (fleet-0q4: no bd outside the adapter): through `fleet item show --json` (fleet-zlk) and a list form of it. If no list verb exists by then, the check's bead adds `fleet item list --json` over the contract's list verb.
- It reports, with counts and up to five example ids each:
  - items carrying fleet's namespaced keys or labels that fail fleet's schema (fleet.orders or fleet.run with an unknown v; fleet:run on a non-record);
  - foreign conventions a person may want mapped: bare orders, run or assignee-like metadata keys, and labels or types the project's rules would need to match;
  - until fleet-zlk lands, notes carrying fleet's old marker words.
- Its exit follows the doctor's table: 0 nothing to adopt, 1 found and listed, 3 could not read. It writes nothing.
- The skill (packs/tiny/skills/adopt/, or the defaults' if it is core's) walks the report, and each mapping write is confirmed by the person and read back.
Depends on: fleet-4j6 (namespacing), fleet-2u3.1 (fleet doctor), fleet-zlk (the item read verb).
Acceptance: as filed, with "the verb" read as "the doctor check".

title: Namespace what fleet owns on the board: its metadata keys and the run label collide with an existing board's data
description:
FINDING from walkthrough fleet-alt.1, 2026-09-23, core/src/store.rs:360-381 and core/src/item/run.rs:88. Raised by Alberto, verbatim: "if the user wants to fly beads that use different conventions wouldnt the tool throw an error? for example if the existing beads were using metadata.orders but with slightly different schema"

F [Required] correctness core/src/item/run.rs:88, core/src/store.rs:360-381 — fleet claims plain names in shared spaces: the metadata keys `orders`, `flight` and `run`, and the label `run`. On a board that already uses any of them, fleet refuses, misreads silently, or acts on the user's data.

Fence: none cited for the plain names. store.rs:181-188 explains ONE WRITER PER TOP-LEVEL KEY because bd merges metadata at the top level. A single namespaced key keeps that property: fleet owns one key and nobody else writes it.

Evidence, at primary 0f8ad4c, by reading (no failing test yet):
- Refuses: dispatch refuses any item with a foreign metadata.orders of any shape, as "already carries an order" (core/src/item/dispatch.rs:189-195).
- Misreads: orders_of reads each field as a string and silently turns a number or an object into None (store.rs:370).
- Acts on the user's data, retire: seat::retire::held takes every open item assigned to the seat that has an `orders` key (core/src/seat/retire.rs:40-47) and withdraws it, clearing the assignee and unsetting metadata.orders. If a seat's name matches an existing assignee, the user's own metadata.orders is deleted.
- Acts on the user's data, the run label: the bare label `run` (run.rs:88) marks a run's record item. gate::ask treats such an item as a run's park, which "touches no git at all" (core/src/item/gate.rs:127-133). A seat on an existing item labelled `run` that asks a question has its work left uncommitted before it is retired. land.rs:1752-1765 uses the same label to decide whether the landing acts as the reviewer.

Remedy:
- Fleet writes and reads ONE metadata key it owns, `fleet`, carrying a schema number and holding `orders`, `run` and anything later beneath it.
- Fleet's run records carry a namespaced label, `fleet:run` (or the kind fleet-zlk settles).
- A read that finds no `fleet` key reads "no order", whatever else the item's metadata holds.
- A `fleet` key with a schema this binary does not know is exit 3, could not tell, never a guess.
- metadata.flight has no reader (held finding F1 on fleet-alt.1) and is not carried over.
- The note marker words are fleet-zlk's.

Acceptance, suites beside the touched files on the fake store:
- An item with a foreign metadata.orders (any shape) dispatches normally, and its foreign key is untouched after dispatch, deliver, retire and land.
- An item labelled `run` that is not a fleet run record asks, parks and commits like any other item.
- Existing fleet-written records keep working, or a one-time migration is part of this bead: the spec pass decides which, given release/0.1.0 is not yet out.
Gate line: touched suites green; the reviewer runs the full suite, ran or cached, at landing.

Related: fleet-0q4 (the adapter owns the storage layout), fleet-zlk (typed record; note markers).

notes:
DECISION (fleet-alt.1, 2026-09-23): CLEAN BREAK before 0.1.0. No migration code; the namespaced shapes are the only shapes; this repo's own board is converted once by hand in the landing.
FOLDED IN (fleet-alt.1 store sweep, 2026-09-23, Alberto): fleet-y3l. Its ACs become this bead's: (AC-y1) dispatch's RERUN line is chosen per disagreeing field: assignee gives the assignee repair, the index gives the namespaced-key repair; (AC-y2) the wrong-assignee arm asserts the assignee repair and is shown red first (core/src/item/dispatch.rs:727-735; core/tests/dispatch.rs:552). ALSO IN SCOPE: packs/tiny/skills/preboard/SKILL.md:47 (filter 5) reads the bare  key and must read fleet's namespaced one; docs/items.md:22,87 name metadata.orders.
CORRECTION to the note above (a shell quoting slip dropped a word): "reads the bare  key" should read "reads the bare orders key". packs/tiny/skills/preboard/SKILL.md:47 (filter 5) treats an orders key on the item as ASSIGNED, and must read fleet's namespaced key instead.
SPEC (walkthrough fleet-alt.1 spec pass, 2026-09-23). Rulings (Alberto, AskUserQuestion): clean break before 0.1.0; DOTTED TOP-LEVEL KEYS; the run label is `fleet:run`.

Measured on a scratch bd 1.2.2 board (2026-09-23):
- Writing {"fleet.run":{…}} then {"fleet.orders":{…}} keeps both keys.
- --unset-metadata fleet.orders removes only that key.
- bd list --json answers both keys.
- One nested {"fleet":{…}} object is REPLACED WHOLE by the next write to `fleet`: a nested run was lost when a nested orders was written. Nesting would break store.rs's one-writer-per-top-level-key rule, which is why the keys are dotted.

Remedy (line numbers at 31c0c01 plus the staged fleet-fhi; re-read at pickup):
1. Keys. `metadata.orders` becomes `metadata["fleet.orders"]`, and `metadata.run` becomes `metadata["fleet.run"]`. Each object carries `"v": 1`. Define the key names and the version as constants in one place, beside the store module, and have every reader and writer use them:
   - writers: the index payload at core/src/item/dispatch.rs:521 (index() and index_payload), the run record's set_metadata at core/src/item/run.rs:1190, and unset_orders / withdraw_order at core/src/store.rs:571 and :584;
   - readers: orders_of at store.rs:404, item_from's run at store.rs:678, and run.rs:1021 (`.get("run")`);
   - the fake store in core/src/test_support.rs.
2. Version. A read finding a fleet key whose `v` is missing or not 1 answers the unreadable state: orders becomes present-but-unreadable (has_orders_key true, orders None), and run becomes a refusal naming the key and version with exit 3. It never guesses. A read finding no fleet key reads "no order" or "no run", whatever else the item's metadata holds, including a bare `orders` or `run` key someone else wrote.
3. Label. run::LABEL (core/src/item/run.rs:88) becomes "fleet:run". Its uses follow: create (run.rs:1149), open_labelled (run.rs:653), gate::ask's run test (core/src/item/gate.rs:132) and land's caller_run (core/src/item/land.rs:1752). A bare `run` label means nothing to fleet.
4. Repair lines. Carried from fleet-y3l (folded in): dispatch's RERUN line is chosen per disagreeing field (core/src/item/dispatch.rs, disagrees()). An assignee disagreement gets the assignee repair; an index disagreement gets the fleet.orders repair.
5. Outside the crates. packs/tiny/skills/preboard/SKILL.md:47 (filter 5) reads the fleet.orders key, not `orders`. docs/items.md:22 and :87 name fleet.orders and the `v` field. docs/runs.md names fleet:run and fleet.run wherever it names the run label or metadata.
6. This repo's board. Converted by hand once in the landing, and listed on this bead: every open item's `orders` key re-written as `fleet.orders` with v 1, and every open run record's `run` key and `run` label moved to the new names. Clean break: no migration code.

Acceptance, on the fake store unless noted:
- AC1 An item carrying a foreign metadata.orders (any shape) and a foreign bare `run` label dispatches, delivers, reviews and lands normally, and its foreign key and label are byte-identical afterwards.
- AC2 Retiring a seat assigned an item with a foreign `orders` key and no fleet.orders leaves that key untouched.
- AC3 An item labelled `run` (not fleet:run) that asks parks and commits its tree like any seat's item.
- AC4 fleet.orders with "v": 2 reads as present-but-unreadable, and dispatch refuses it with exit 3.
- AC5 Carried from fleet-y3l: the wrong-assignee arm asserts the assignee repair line, shown red against today's code first.
- AC6 One arm through the real bd shows fleet.orders and fleet.run surviving each other's writes.
Gate line: touched suites green; the reviewer runs the full suite, ran or cached, at landing.
Order: after fleet-16s (store fields) and fleet-9r6 (envelope), both of which touch the same readers.

SPEC'D to the zero-clarification bar.
Landed 610b18e: core/src/store/keys.rs holds ORDERS="fleet.orders", RUN="fleet.run", VERSION_FIELD="v", VERSION=1, stamped() (every writer) and versioned() (every reader). Writers: dispatch::index, run::write_the_pins, Bd::unset_orders and withdraw_order (--unset-metadata fleet.orders). Readers: orders_of (v missing or not 1 -> present-but-unreadable), item_from's run, run.rs object_of (exit 3 naming key and version). run::LABEL = "fleet:run"; run::OBJECT deleted. RERUN repair per disagreeing field: assignee -> 'bd update <item> --assignee <seat> --actor <by>', index -> the versioned fleet.orders payload. The fake, capped.rs and the fixtures (re-recorded on bd 1.3.0, one row carrying another tool's bare orders/run) follow. Arms: AC1 per verb (dispatch, deliver, review, land); AC2 retire; AC3 bare-run-labelled item parks and commits; AC4 v2 and no-v on fake and real bd (run side); AC5 red first plus an index-repair companion; AC6 contract check fleet_keys on both stores. Merge with fleet-6gr.2: one new land fixture wrote [gates], fixed on rebase. Full suite 1037/1037. title: Design: an item's record is a timeline of typed entries the store adapter owns, not prose notes parsed back
description:
FINDING from walkthrough fleet-alt.1, 2026-09-23, raised by Alberto while reading core/src/store.rs:24-66, verbatim:
"why do we need to also show it in notes for a human? that's making an assumption based on beads being the first store adapter. whatever tool humans are using to look at items should handle reading metadata.orders and presenting that information to the user. what else is notes used for on the fleet side? right now based on just the orders case it feels like a timeline of events"

Ruling (Alberto): the record must not assume bd. A human-facing copy of structured data is the viewer's job, not the verbs'.

Fence: docs/items.md:8-10, "every verb that writes, writes a note on the item and reads it back before it exits 0, so the item's notes, in order, are its record". Its reason, one inspectable record written and read back, still holds. The medium it names (prose notes on a bd item, parsed with a marker grammar) is what this redesign replaces.

Evidence, at primary 0f8ad4c:
- Every verb that writes appends a note opened by a column-zero marker, with a grammar from a pack-overridable template in core/defaults/assets/:
  - order and withdrawal: core/src/item/dispatch.rs:419, 446 and 478; core/src/seat/retire.rs:66
  - DELIVERED / RE-DELIVERED: core/src/item/deliver.rs:172, markers at core/src/item/mod.rs:552
  - ACCEPTED / RETURNED WITH FINDINGS: core/src/item/review.rs:467, mod.rs:557
  - QUESTION and PARKED: core/src/item/gate.rs:181 and 418, markers at gate.rs:70 and mod.rs:569
  - ANSWERED: gate.rs:537, mod.rs:575
  - LANDED: core/src/item/land.rs:914, mod.rs:563
- State is decided by parsing that text back with last_region (mod.rs:593) and last_marker_at (mod.rs:666):
  - the commit to land: land.rs:567
  - the licence to squash, the last verdict naming the commit: land.rs:1682
  - the last landing: land.rs:1568
  - the last answer: land.rs:1776
  - the review's delivery: review.rs:501
  - the park's gate id: gate.rs:485
  - whether a park is answered, by marker order: gate.rs:659-665
  - the last verdict: gate.rs:736
- Only the order keeps a structured copy (metadata.orders); every other entry kind exists only as prose.
- The same moments are also written, typed, to the controller's event stream (item.dispatched, item.landed, …), so there are two timelines.
- Guarding against quoted markers is its own code: mod.rs:586-592.

Direction (for the design pass, not a spec):
- The store keeps an item's timeline as typed entries: a kind, structured fields (commit, verdict, gate id, seat, ordinal …) and any human-authored body (findings, a question's options) as a field.
- Current state is a fold over typed entries, never a parse of text.
- The order note goes away; the order is an entry or the index.
- Presentation is the viewer's.
- The bd adapter (fleet-0q4) chooses how entries are stored.
- To settle in design: whether the item timeline and the event stream become one log or stay two; what happens to the pack-overridable note templates; how docs/items.md restates "the record".

Related: fleet-0q4 (the adapter this sits behind). fleet-nv0 (brief decides from the index) stands on its own and can land first.

Acceptance: a design note on this bead, ruled by Alberto, then implementation beads split from it.
Gate line: per implementation bead.

THIS IS A FINDING, NOT A SPEC: it is designed and specced before anyone works it; do not work it as filed.
notes:
DESIGN QUESTIONS ADDED from walkthrough fleet-alt.1: (1) labels as a kind: gate.rs:132 and land.rs:1758 recognise a run's record item by a label; a typed record would name the kind. (2) assignee duplicates orders.seat on an ordered item, and dispatch writes and checks both (dispatch.rs:547); decide whether the assignee is its own fact or the adapter's rendering of the order.
DECISION (fleet-alt.1, 2026-09-23): one log or two (the item timeline vs the event stream) is decided IN THE DESIGN PASS, which compares both with a worked example; Alberto rules there.
CASES THE DESIGN MUST MAKE IMPOSSIBLE (held here, fleet-alt.1 store sweep): fleet-4rl (a second column-zero marker in a note body is read as a new region, deliver.rs:404-427 / mod.rs last_region); fleet-20s (preboard reads an 'On flight' note nothing writes); fleet-56e (landing records carry 7-char shas beside full ones); fleet-z4w (the SDK's gate park and the crash-cap park both write item.parked, and the controller's fold cannot tell them apart).
DESIGN RULED (walkthrough fleet-alt.1 spec pass, 2026-09-23; Alberto, AskUserQuestion, one decision at a time). Facts from the research pass at 1b90166; line numbers are that commit's.

THE FACT THAT DECIDES IT: the event stream is per machine (<machine dir>/events.jsonl, controller/src/events.rs; machine_dir from platform::machine_dir), never synced or versioned, with no fsync and no retention. The board is shared: bd syncs to the git remote named in .beads/config.yaml, and every landing commits the export (core/src/item/land.rs:613-671). An answer written from machine B reaches the board but only B's stream, so a run on machine A waiting on it never wakes, and A's status counts the gate as unanswered.

RULINGS
R1 TWO LOGS; THE STORE IS THE RECORD. An item's timeline of typed entries in the store is its only record, shared by every machine, and every decision reads it. The per-machine stream keeps machine events (session.*, seat.*, controller, routine.*, run lifecycle). For items it carries only WAKE SIGNALS {item, entry, kind}, telling the controller and the SDK when to re-read the store. No reader decides a fact from a stream payload.
R2 THE BD ADAPTER STORES ENTRIES AS BD COMMENTS. One comment per entry; its text is a JSON object {"fleet.entry": 1, "kind": …, fields…}.
  Measured on bd 1.2.2 (scratch board, 2026-09-23):
  - `bd comments add <id> <text>` appends {id (UUID v7, time-ordered), issue_id, author, created_at}.
  - `bd comments <id> --json` lists them.
  - There is no edit or delete subcommand.
  - bd show answers only comment_count, and bd list answers no comments, so listings stay light.
  - A person's comment is not an entry: the adapter reads only bodies carrying "fleet.entry".
  Metadata was rejected: bd replaces a top-level key whole (a timeline array is a racing read-modify-write), and metadata rides every listing (a key per entry would make every list carry every history).
R3 A SEAT HANDS IN JSON. A delivery and a question are JSON files: the entry minus the fields only the process fills (commit, base, time, actor). The verb deserializes with serde (deny_unknown_fields) and refuses before ANY write when the file does not parse or validate. The JSON Schema for each ships in the defaults and is shown in the seat's brief. There is no prose grammar anywhere.
R4 FLEET WRITES NO NOTES. The notes field is left to people. Presentation of a timeline is the viewer's: `fleet item show <id>` renders it, and --json answers it.

THE ENTRY MODEL (fields are the design's; exact names at implementation)
Envelope, on every entry: fleet.entry (version, 1), kind, id (the store's entry id; for bd, the comment id), at (the store's time), by (an actor reference: fleet-iex's seat id, or a run, routine or controller reference).
Kinds and their fields:
- ordered: order kind (dispatch | review), seat, ordinal?. The fleet.orders metadata index (fleet-4j6) stays as the CURRENT-order projection that listings filter on. It is written in the same act, and the entry is the record.
- order_withdrawn: why (retire | spawn_refused | could_not_tell), seat.
- delivered: commit (full sha), branch, base (full sha), files[], checks[] {check, result}, suite {command, rc} | not_tested, spec_corrections[], not_proven[], decisions[] {call, not_taken, because}, covers[].
- reviewed: verdict (accepted | returned), commit (full), size line fields, decisions walk[], and findings[] when returned.
- held: the hold (fleet-6gr's name for bd's gate) with hold id, reason (ask | max_crashes | …), question, options[] {letter, text}, and branch and commit (or the run hash on a run's record).
- cleared: hold id, letter? (absent when cleared by cancel), text?, how (answer | cancel).
- landed: sha (full), old (full), squash_of (full), run?, test {command, rc} | not_tested, checks[] (one per landing check, each with its verdict), work_branch {branch, classification}.
Readers derive state by folding entries in the store's order: the last delivered, the last reviewed, whether the last held is cleared, and so on.

WHAT THIS RETIRES AND FIXES (each needs an arm in its implementation bead)
- The marker grammar: last_region, last_delivery, last_verdict, last_landing, last_park, last_answer, last_marker_at, order_line, off_column_zero, grammar_holds (core/src/item/mod.rs:607-709, review.rs:494-541, gate.rs:250-331, deliver.rs:403-427, brief.rs:146-153). The note templates retire (core/defaults/assets/*-note.md, verdict.md); the shadow registry drops them and gains the input schemas.
- fleet-4rl (a marker inside a body): impossible, no grammar. fleet-20s (the 'On flight' note): preboard reads entries and fleet.orders only. fleet-56e (7-char shas): every sha field is full, validated at write. fleet-z4w (the crash-cap latch): the held entry's reason tells an ask from max_crashes, and the controller reads the store.
- Also impossible, found in the research pass and verified:
  - The SDK ignores returns: packs/ts/assets/sdk/mod.ts:389-395 treats any earlier item.delivered as carried, and until(delivered) at :466-486 does the same. Under R1 both read the store's last delivered AFTER the last reviewed=returned.
  - item.held: waited on (sdk/mod.ts:113; controller/src/runs.rs:63) and written by nothing (core/src/item/mod.rs:158). It goes.
  - cancel's gate.resolved carries letter: null and the SDK returns the string "null" (core/src/item/run.rs:614-616; sdk/mod.ts:463). A cleared entry with how: cancel and no letter makes the SDK's wait answer 'cancelled' rather than a letter.
  - The crash-cap park's note and event disagree (gate.rs:407-415 vs controller/src/runs.rs:511-524). One entry.
- The land licence (land.rs:1768-1790) reads a typed cleared entry and checks the hold, the item and the answerer. Which letter licenses a landing is the workflow's (takeoff) and is fixed in the implementation bead with fleet-pl6 and fleet-w4w, which it relates to.

THE STREAM AFTER THIS
item.* and gate.* events become wake signals {item, entry, kind}. controller/src/runs.rs could_wake keeps matching on item and kind, and then the run re-reads the store. status's open holds (cli/src/status.rs:313-332) read the store (the adapter's open holds), not the stream. The SDK gains one verb over the store for its reads, `fleet item show <id> --json` (timeline included); until, spawn and gate read it. The payload tables in core/src/item/mod.rs:205-258 shrink to the signal.

DEPENDS ON: fleet-iex (the actor reference in `by`), fleet-6gr (the names held and cleared), fleet-4j6 (fleet.orders), and fleet-0q4's contract (append entry, read timeline, and open holds as contract verbs).

IMPLEMENTATION SPLIT, each its own bead when its flight comes, specced then:
(1) entry types, the JSON Schemas, and the bd adapter's append/read over comments;
(2) the writers switch, one verb per bead or grouped: dispatch/withdraw, deliver, review, ask/answer/cancel, land;
(3) the readers switch: review, land (licence and builder), answer, brief, status;
(4) the stream's item events become signals; the controller's wake and the SDK (until, spawn, gate) read the store through `fleet item show --json`;
(5) the seat input: the JSON files, the schemas in the brief, and the tiny pack's prompts, manual, clock-out and handoff skills, and docs/items.md;
(6) delete the marker grammar and the note templates.
Clean break before 0.1.0: this repo's open items carrying prose notes are not migrated; the notes stay as history for people.
CORRECTION to the design's premise (2026-09-23): the board was NOT synced to a Dolt remote. Its origin pointed at a missing repo, and bembot90/tinyfleet holds no Dolt refs; the remote has now been removed. The board is shared across machines only through the .beads/issues.jsonl export each landing commits. The ruling stands: the store (and its committed export) is what is shared, and the per-machine stream never is. But "bd syncs to the git remote" in the note above is wrong.
FROM fleet-4j6's landing (Alberto, 2026-09-24 morning, 'leave it for fleet-zlk'): dispatch's read-back refusal still hands the note-disagreement cases ('the last order note', 'the notes') the fleet.orders index repair line, which does not fix a note. Not fixed there because zlk retires order notes (R4, fleet writes no notes); the implementation bead that switches dispatch's writer should delete these read-backs with the notes.
close_reason: All 17 splits landed on release/0.1.0 (0c9d349..51abfb0, flight 6); the record is typed timeline entries the store adapter owns; one routine note remains, recorded on fleet-zlk.17 for Alberto's ruling

title: fleet brief decides from the order index, not a text search of the notes
description:
FINDING from walkthrough fleet-alt.1, 2026-09-23, core/src/item/brief.rs:146-153 and :268-274, raised by Alberto: "isnt searching the notes for orders given really brittle? isnt that what beads metadata is for?"

F [Required] correctness core/src/item/brief.rs:268-274 — `fleet brief` gates on order_line(), the last line anywhere in the notes containing "orders given" (brief.rs:146-153). A withdrawn order still passes, so a brief goes out for an item nobody holds, which brief.rs:255-257 says must never happen.

Fence: brief.rs:255-257, "a brief for it would tell a seat it may begin when nothing said so". The fence holds; the gate reads the wrong surface to enforce it. docs/items.md:21-23 defines the order as the note plus the index, and the index is the machine-read half.

Evidence, at primary 0f8ad4c, by reading (no failing test exists yet):
- Notes are append-only. A withdrawal writes "ORDER WITHDRAWN at retire" (core/src/seat/retire.rs:26) or "DISPATCH WITHDRAWN — spawn refused" (core/src/item/dispatch.rs:47), and neither contains "orders given". It also unsets metadata.orders (Store::withdraw_order).
- After a withdrawal, order_line still returns the old "dispatched by X — orders given" line, and brief::for_item (called from cli/src/item.rs:860) renders the brief.
- Every other order decision already reads the index: dispatch.rs:189, 427, 454, 558 and 712; deliver.rs:286; review.rs:396; seat/retire.rs:44 and 69.
- A person's note containing "orders given" would also be taken as the order line.

Remedy: brief::for_item refuses unless the item's index is present and readable (item.orders is Some, the same reading the other verbs take). The brief's order text is rendered from the index, or from the note only when the index agrees. order_line stays only as dispatch's read-back of its own write (dispatch.rs:589); the note is the record people read and no code decides from it.

Acceptance: a suite beside core/src/item/brief.rs (core/tests) drives three cases on the fake store: dispatch, then withdraw, then brief refuses with exit 1; a note containing "orders given" on an item with no index is refused; a dispatched item still gets its brief. The suites beside the touched files are green.
Gate line: touched suites green; the reviewer runs the full suite, ran or cached, at landing.

description:

title: Refactor store: isolate the work graph from beads behind an adapter, ready for new adapters
description:
FINDING from walkthrough fleet-alt.1, 2026-09-23, core/src/store.rs:1-22.

Alberto, verbatim: "Store needs to be completely isolated from beads and ready to support new adapters in the future."

Fence: packs PRD principle 7, "Beads the one dependency. The work graph is bd's; every note a verb writes is a bd note … nothing here invents a second store" (brain/prds/fleet-packs-prd.md:76-78), and R20, "A verb writes to the work graph through `bd` only; no verb reaches the store another way" (:585-586). Alberto's ruling above reverses principle 7 for the store boundary. R20's intent, that no verb goes around the store, still holds: it is what the adapter enforces.

Evidence, at primary 0f8ad4c:
- The trait and the bd adapter share one module. Store is at core/src/store.rs:143-242, Bd at :244-720, and the trait's docs cite bd behaviour ("measured on bd 1.2.2", :208-221).
- A bd path is published at the trait's level: EXPORT = ".beads/issues.jsonl" (store.rs:20-22). It is imported by core/src/item/land.rs:54, which also knows the .beads/ directory (land.rs:614, 649-671, 720, 2015-2030).
- Files outside store.rs and test_support.rs that mention bd or beads (git grep -c -i 'beads\|\bbd\b'): cli/src/item.rs 28, core/src/item/land.rs 11, cli/src/runs.rs 8, cli/src/transient.rs 4, cli/src/prime.rs 4, core/src/item/run.rs 3, controller/src/routines/action.rs 3, core/src/item/review.rs 2, core/src/item/dispatch.rs 2, core/src/item/deliver.rs 2, and one each in core/src/guard/mod.rs, controller/src/lifecycle.rs, cli/src/step.rs, cli/src/status.rs and cli/src/main.rs. Some of these are prose and some are behaviour, such as a RERUN line printing a bd command (core/src/item/dispatch.rs:487) or bd binary resolution (cli/src/runs.rs:56-63). The spec pass sorts which is which.

Remedy (direction, not spec):
- The store module holds the trait and its domain types, with no bd vocabulary.
- The bd adapter becomes its own module.
- Every bd fact moves behind the adapter: the argv, the quirks, the export file and the directory it lives in, and the binary resolution.
- Verbs and the cli reach the store only through the trait.
- Whatever the landing must commit into git (today the export) comes from the adapter, not from a constant.

Acceptance: behaviour preserved. No file outside the adapter names bd or .beads in code. The suites beside the touched files are green.
Gate line: touched suites green; the reviewer runs the full suite, ran or cached, at landing.

THIS IS A FINDING, NOT A SPEC: it is specced before anyone works it; do not work it as filed. It likely exceeds 500 lines, so the spec pass splits it: the adapter module first, then each leaking caller.

notes:
PLAN — fleet-alt.1, core foundations, 4,696 lines, five sections in reading order (line numbers at primary 0f8ad4c):

1. The work graph boundary — core/src/lib.rs:1-129 (map only; its verbs are outline sections 3–4), core/src/store.rs:1-769. ~900 lines.
   Trace: dispatch writes the order index and reads it back — Store::set_orders → Bd::wrote → Bd::run (`bd -C <root> update <id> --metadata … --actor`) → Answer; then Store::show → first_value → sole → the error key → item_from → orders_of.
   First appearances: the Store trait as the seam a suite forces a disagreeing read-back through; "the record before the act's end" (rules.md); Missing vs Unreadable as exit 1 vs exit 3; bd as a dependency boundary (first JSON value, -n 0 caps, null-not-[] listings, top-level metadata merge).

2. The pack format — core/src/pack.rs:1-840, core/src/registry.rs:1-102, core/src/os_litter.rs:1-19. ~960 lines.
   Trace: `fleet pack check packs/tiny` — pack::check → dir_names (OS litter) → SLOTS → parse_manifest → string_key / parse_runtime (placeholders) / parse_config (declarations) → check_slots → check_registry.
   First appearances: the Gas City reference format (G24) and the one slot it lacks (workflows); the runtime table's five placeholders; a pack setting's declaration; the shadow registry.

3. Layers, and the two censuses — core/src/resolve.rs:1-472, core/src/settings.rs:1-249, core/src/policy.rs:1-226. ~950 lines.
   Trace: `fleet run takeoff` resolving its workflow and reading `takeoff.test` — resolve::layers → installed → ordered → layers_over (defaults placed at the bottom) → resolve → unlisted_shadows → slot_path; settings::resolve → set; policy::read("core.run", "max_open").
   First appearances: layering and shadowing; the bottom layer's registry as the whole shadowable surface; the census (a key nothing reads is a gate a person believes in) and MOVED.

4. The defaults and the lock — core/build.rs:1-86, core/src/embedded.rs:1-66, core/src/digest.rs:1-131, core/src/defaults.rs:1-436, core/src/lock.rs:1-222. ~940 lines.
   Trace: `fleet start` materializing the defaults — build.rs → embedded::FILES → defaults::install → lock::read → retire_bundled_core → tree_hash vs embedded_hash → swap_in → pin → lock::append / holds → lock::write (temp, sync, rename).
   First appearances: embedded-then-materialized (readers take a path); the tree hash as the ownership test; the hand-rolled SHA-256 and why; packs.lock.

5. Adding and removing a pack — core/src/add.rs:1-741, core/src/remove.rs:1-208. ~950 lines.
   Trace: `fleet pack add <checkout>//packs/tiny --version <v>` — parse_source → parse_version → Scratch → fetch (clone --no-checkout, checkout, rev-parse) → check_format → locate_import (ts Inside) → AlreadyInstalled → check_layering → rename imports first → pin; then `fleet pack remove` — importers → directory → drop_line.
   First appearances: the two-slash source form; imports installed from the same clone; the write order that leaves a recoverable state.

Sections run 900–960 lines, a little over the 800 guide, because each is one subsystem; "slower" splits the next one.
PACING (Alberto, verbatim): "we're gonna go file by file and line by line instead of this giant wall of text, at the beginning of each section it should just point at where to start. the check should happen at the end of each section to make sure i know how things work. the findings should also go at the end of each section since right now i dont have enough knowledge to make a decision. the findings should be walked one by one with AskUserQuestion" — Part 1 restarts at core/src/store.rs:1 in small line-range steps; the part-1 check posted earlier is withdrawn and asked again at the end of the part; F1–F3 held until then.
SKILL: .claude/skills/walkthrough/SKILL.md edited at Alberto's word ("modify the walkthrough skill based on this feedback") — § 8 file-by-file steps, the opening only points, check and tie-up trace at section end; § 10 findings one at a time via AskUserQuestion after the check; § 7, § 11 and the description aligned. Left uncommitted in the primary.
Q (Alberto): "why is there anything mentioning beads at this level?" — A: by design — packs PRD principle 7 ("Beads the one dependency … nothing here invents a second store", fleet-packs-prd.md:76-78) and R20 (:585-586); the Store trait is a test seam (store.rs:4-6), not a backend abstraction, so store.rs is the one module meant to know bd. The leak worth judging is bd knowledge past it: core/src/item/land.rs:54,614,2030 (EXPORT, .beads/) and cli/src/item.rs (28 bd mentions) — held for outline sections 4 and 10.
FILED (Alberto's word, off his question on store.rs:1-22): fleet-0q4 ← "Store needs to be completely isolated from beads and ready to support new adapters in the future. file a bead for it"; fleet-g68 ← "another for archiving PRDs for things that are already built. we dont need to keep updating prds as we work on stuff, the code and docs/ are the source of truth". Both marked FINDING, NOT A SPEC.
Q (Alberto): "why is status and item_type not an enum?" — A: no reason is written beside either; both copy bd's string. status should be an enum (11 literal comparisons across 6 files, and a typo compiles), with a catch-all variant; item_type stays a string because the project's rules config owns its values (rules.rs:111). Q (Alberto): "what's an order?" — A: the record that says a seat may begin (dispatch.rs:1-11): assignee, order note and metadata.orders index, written as one act, note before index; it exists for rule 1, work is given never taken; kind is dispatch or review (dispatch.rs:31,37). Q (Alberto): "would it make sense to wrap id string in a newtype?" — A: yes; the trait takes several &str in a row (assign(item, seat, by) etc., 46 call sites), and gate ids and item ids are interchangeable today. DECISION: folded both into fleet-0q4 (AskUserQuestion).
Q (Alberto): "lets talk more about orders, is it like a special kind of bead? did we define it or is it something beads already defines?" — A: fleet defines it; bd has no notion of an order. An order is a convention stored in three generic bd places: the assignee field, a note ending in 'orders given' (template core/defaults/assets/dispatch-note.md, found by ORDER_MARK at core/src/item/brief.rs:34-36), and a metadata key 'orders' (by, kind, seat, at, ordinal). Definition: docs/items.md:21-23. The note is the record a person reads; the index is the machine-readable copy so no verb parses prose.
Q (Alberto): "isnt searching the notes for orders given really brittle? isnt that what beads metadata is for?" — A: yes. Every decision already reads the index except brief::for_item (brief.rs:269), which gates on order_line's text search; a withdrawn order leaves the old 'orders given' line behind, so fleet brief renders for an item nobody holds. FILED: fleet-nv0 (bug, SPEC'D) at Alberto's choice 'file a bug now'.
Q (Alberto): "why do we need to also show it in notes for a human? that's making an assumption based on beads being the first store adapter. whatever tool humans are using to look at items should handle reading metadata.orders and presenting that information to the user. what else is notes used for on the fleet side? right now based on just the orders case it feels like a timeline of events" — A: yes. Notes are an append-only per-item event log with marker grammars (DELIVERED, verdict, QUESTION/PARKED, ANSWERED, LANDED, plus orders), and fleet reads its state back by parsing it: land's commit and licence (land.rs:567, 1682), review's delivery (review.rs:501), the park's gate and answered-ness (gate.rs:485, 659-665). Only orders also keep a structured copy. FILED: fleet-zlk (design: typed timeline entries the adapter owns); fleet-nv0 amended.
Q (Alberto): "what other fields in Item now dont pass the smell test based on this conversation? for example, why isnt created_at a DateTime" — A: created_at is a String because core carries only serde/serde_json/toml (core/Cargo.toml:18-29) and jiff is the controller's, but nothing reads it (F1), so delete rather than type it. Field verdicts: id → ItemId; status → enum; assignee → SeatName, and it duplicates orders.seat; notes → fleet-zlk; orders+has_orders_key → one enum; blockers → Vec<ItemId>; item_type stays; labels used as a run-record kind tag (gate.rs:132, land.rs:1758); flight DEAD (no reader; its intended consumer rules::effective at core/src/item/rules.rs:58 has no caller anywhere); run → typed record; document → inside the adapter. DECISION: reshapes folded into fleet-0q4; labels-as-kind and assignee-vs-seat noted on fleet-zlk. HELD for section end: F1 widened to include Item.flight; rules::effective's dead matcher held for outline section 3.
Q (Alberto): "we're gonna need either a verb or an agent skill that helps users normalize data if they're adding fleet to an existing project. if the user wants to fly beads that use different conventions wouldnt the tool throw an error? for example if the existing beads were using metadata.orders but with slightly different schema" — A: not reliably. It refuses (dispatch.rs:189), misreads silently (store.rs:370, the note marker words), or acts on the user's data: retire unsets a foreign metadata.orders (retire.rs:40-47), and the bare label 'run' makes ask skip the git commit (gate.rs:127-133). The root cause is fleet claiming plain names in shared spaces. FILED (Alberto chose 'two beads'): fleet-4j6 (bug, namespace fleet's keys and label; Required) and fleet-0ml (read-only scan verb + mapping skill; blocked by fleet-4j6).
Q (Alberto): "for Ready why not ReadyItem, Ready made me think it's an event or something else entirely?" — A: agreed; Row (store.rs:110-121) has the same vagueness. Ready is F1's to delete (ready() answers ids, since its one caller dispatch.rs:179-182 checks membership only); if kept, rename it ReadyItem. HELD F4 [Nit] readability core/src/store.rs:110-121 — Row names neither its listing nor its subject — remedy: rename to AssignedItem; read by core/src/seat/retire.rs:40-47 and core/src/item/deliver.rs:286.
HELD F5 [Optional] architecture core/src/item/{brief,deliver,dispatch,gate,land,review,run}.rs — the StoreError→Stop mapping (Missing→refused/exit 1, Unreadable→could_not_tell/exit 3) is written 8 times across 7 files, twice in dispatch.rs:687-699 alone — evidence: git grep -n 'StoreError::Missing(why) => Stop::refused' counts 8 — remedy: one From<StoreError> for Stop beside Stop in core/src/item/mod.rs, callers use ?; ≈ -40 lines
CADENCE (Alberto, verbatim, 2026-09-23): "we're gonna stop the walkthrough after this one file to work on every bead that will come out of it. that way when i review the code my knowledge of it is fresh. we will do that multiple times in the walkthrough (sometimes after one single large file like this one or maybe after 2-3 small ones) so make sure everything is being recorded on the walkthrough bead 'cause this is gonna take a week at least with many refactors along the way." — The walk pauses at a WORK BREAK after a file or a few, the beads filed off it are worked, then the walk resumes. Refactors move line numbers, so every resumption re-runs step 0 and re-plans the remaining steps against the new SHA. The first break is after core/src/store.rs.
HELD F6 [Nit] correctness core/src/store.rs:152-154 — open_labelled's doc says 'the list read answers no metadata, so a caller that needs an item's flight object reads it with Store::show'; measured on bd 1.2.2, 'bd list --label fleet --json -n 0 --all' answers fleet-6ravv WITH metadata.orders, and Row (store.rs:115-117) relies on exactly that; 'flight' is dead (F1) — remedy: drop the false sentence and the flight reference; ≈ -3 lines
Q (Alberto, verbatim): "ok three things i wanna flag: 1. seats. i keep seeing it mentioned everywhere. explain it to me, what it is, where it came from, why we need it. if it's what i think it is, a string that is meant to represent a human or agent then i have follow-ups: the id of a seat cant be the name, the name should be optional and seat id should be a short id from the uuid crate. earlier you asked me that we need to ask the user for a name during create so that assigned_by can use it. we shouldnt have to ask the user that. during create the human should get an autogenerated uuid and an entry on fleet.toml with name empty, they can add their name if they want. later on if we have things like a cloud offering and workspaces, etc. those seats and their ids should carry over. a seat should also say whether it's a human or an agent. 2. gates. same thing as above. explain it to me, what it is, where it came from, why we need it. the word gate matches our flying analogies so im not opposed to keeping it i just wanna make sure that everything borrowed from beads makes sense and is well defined inside of fleet. other tools have different names for this like checks so it might be worth exploring what the canonical terms out there are/ 3. some of these Store functions feel like queries that could belong in a single query fn with an enum passed to it, happy to be proven wrong so argue against it you think that's the wrong move"
A:
(1) A seat today is an AGENT slot: a seat-list row, a worktree and a session the controller keeps alive (brain/fleet-vision.md:29-30; docs/seats.md terms). Named seats come from [seats.<name>]; transient seats are transient-<n>. Humans are not seats: they are a free-string actor (--by, FLEET_ACTOR/BEADS_ACTOR, cli/src/item.rs:1165-1175). A seat's id is its name, and transient names are reused, which is the hazard lib.rs:90-97 guards against (orders passed to the next holder of the name); a UUID id removes it. Adjustments: store the full UUID (v7) and display a short prefix, because a truncated id is not unique across workspaces; the uuid crate breaks core's three-crate rule (core/Cargo.toml:18-29), Alberto's call; open: where a human seat lives when fleet.toml is committed project policy and a second person never runs create.
(2) A gate is bd's async wait condition (bd gate --help: human, timer, gh:run, gh:pr, bead); fleet uses only human, for ask/answer. Inside fleet "gate" means at least five things: bd's human gate, the builder's gate (--touched), the landing's gate rows, the [gates] policy table, and controller/src/routines/gate.rs; 39 source files mention it. Canonical terms (general knowledge, to be surveyed): automated pass/fail = check or quality gate; human pause = approval, manual judgment, input, suspend, interrupt. ALREADY FILED (from flight 7's reviews, open, on no flight), met in the walk and named, not re-filed: fleet-run (store::Item → types::Item), fleet-j7q (the contract has no reopen, so retire and "fenced writes" cannot finish over Exec), fleet-pjl (close's untyped by; the timeline's two actor forms), fleet-b47 (writes on a missing item; NewItem::validate never called), fleet-vqre (two OrderKinds), fleet-z5m (bd's fragment rule is a prefix, not "a substring", bd/mod.rs:526-528), fleet-urp, fleet-2tp, fleet-xpc, fleet-4qpq.
Q (Alberto): "i thought ItemId was meant to use uuid no?" — A: no; the UUID v7 ruling (first sitting, fleet-iex) is for SEAT ids — SeatId wraps uuid::Uuid, minted by now_v7 (core/src/seat/identity.rs:33,38), displayed by its last 8 hex digits. An item id is minted by the STORE (bd's fleet-<hash>), and fleet holds it as the text the store gave, never parsed, shortened or sorted (types.rs:35-36); an adapter's store may mint any shape. The hazard the UUID fixed — a reused seat name inheriting orders (lib.rs's retire note) — does not exist for items, whose ids are never reused.
Q (Alberto): "what do you mean by fenced write?" — A: a conditional write (compare-and-set): the write carries a precondition on the item's current state — 'only while seat X holds it', 'only while it is in_progress' — that the store checks in the same step as the write, and a failed precondition writes NOTHING and answers Moved. Needed because a verb reads, decides, then writes, and another actor (a seat, the controller, a retire, a person) can change the item in between; unfenced, the stale decision overwrites the newer state (fleet-3e6: a retire reopened an item its holder had just closed). bd: --if-assignee / --if-status, exit 13 (bd/mod.rs:244-261). The trait's defaults (mod.rs:212-216, 265-275) are a weaker read-then-write with a window, for a store with no fence of its own.
Q (Alberto): "ok so these fenced writes are not implemented by the adapters, they're internal for us only" — A: half right (corrected): they are not CONTRACT verbs (not in docs/store.md, mod.rs:125-131), so an external adapter implements nothing for them and Exec gets the trait's defaults composed from contract verbs (hand_over = show + update, with the window). But the built-in bd adapter DOES override all three with one fenced bd call each (bd/mod.rs:642-657, 715-717, 732-761). And over Exec the order_withdraw_from default fails at reopen (exec.rs:294-300), so a retire cannot finish: fleet-j7q (open, ruled 2026-09-25) moves the fence (if_assignee/if_status, refusal reason moved) and a reopen into the contract so external adapters implement it.
Q (Alberto): "so if we end up moving bd out of this codebase as an exec adapter this is something we need to keep in mind?" — A: yes: anything bd does through a trait override and not a contract verb is lost the day bd goes behind Exec. Measured list: (1) order_withdraw_from + reopen — covered by fleet-j7q; (2) hand_over's fence — NOT covered: j7q's ruling fences order.withdraw only, so over Exec hand_over is show + plain update, which has the window AND which bd 1.3.0 refuses for a non-holder on an in_progress item (bd/mod.rs:637-641) — review's return (core/src/item/review.rs:401) would fail; held as a finding for section 1's end; (3) bd-only outside the trait: prime's pin line and FLEET_BD_BIN (bd::tracker_line / bd::resolve, cli/src/prime.rs, core/src/supported.rs) become the adapter's version answer; the conformance another_writer plant (test-side); close's bare-seat actor (fleet-pjl puts that in the bd adapter, so it moves with it); (4) cost: two processes per call instead of one.
Q (Alberto): "Retire is when a seta goes on vacation right?" — A: no (corrected): retire ENDS a transient seat for good — stops its session, removes its worktree, drops its row, and its id goes with it (docs/seats.md:714-727, 'Retiring a transient seat'); before the row drops it withdraws every open/in_progress ordered item the seat holds (core/src/seat/retire.rs:1-8) so no work is stranded on a seat that no longer exists. The temporary one is REST: a named seat asks for a fresh session in the same worktree, same seat, same id (docs/seats.md:63-64, 562-583); a rest touches no item. A named seat is never retired by this verb; a transient seat never rests (exit 6).
Q (Alberto): "Why would we want to replace item order but leave assignee and run record alone? Whats the use case?" — A: the three move at different moments in different verbs, so each write owns one field and needs no read of the others (a read-modify-write would be a race). Measured: (1) transient dispatch writes the order TWICE — first with no seat, before the spawn exists (dispatch.rs:389), then after the spawn assigns the item (update, :426-431) it replaces the order with one naming the spawned seat (:439); replaced whole because an order is one value (kind, by, seat, at) and a field merge could mix two orders. (2) deliver moves the assignee to the reviewer and leaves the order standing (deliver.rs:167-172) — the mirror case. (3) the run record is written by fleet run on the run's record item (run.rs:1176, 1212); on bd both keys share the item's one metadata object, and fleet-4j6 measured a nested {fleet:{…}} write erasing the other — so each write touching only its own key is the guarantee conformance checks 13-14 hold. Whether a record item is ever also dispatched was not measured; the guarantee is about the storage, not a known collision.
RESUME (WORK BREAK 2, 2026-09-25): Alberto stopped the store re-walk to open a design session (another agent) on moving bd behind the Exec adapter. Section 1 of 7 (the seam and the opener) walked through core/src/store/mod.rs:465; remaining in section 1: mod.rs:467-551 (moved, restatused, validated, unchanged, already_closed/cleared, holder_named, tail, first_value), then section 1's tie-up trace, check and findings (F1, F2 as planned, plus F12 below); sections 2-7 as planned. HANDOFF to the bd-as-Exec design session (given to Alberto 2026-09-25, measured at fe30b88): (1) bd's trait overrides with no contract verb: hand_over (bd/mod.rs:642-657; NOT in fleet-j7q — F12), reopen (715-717) and order_withdraw_from (732-761; fleet-j7q). title: the SDK's gate parks the run's own record, and the controller's fold reads that item.parked as the crash-cap park latch, so a run that asked a gate skips its later max_crashes park
description: Found by the fleet-thh builder (2026-09-23). The SDK's gate asks through fleet ask --item <run>, which writes item.parked with item = <run>. controller/src/runs.rs fold reads an item.parked for the run as Folded.parked, the latch that says the crash-cap park already stands. So a run that asked a gate and later reaches [core.run] max_crashes is treated as already parked and gets no crash-cap gate. Done when the latch tells a crash-cap park from a workflow's own gate (e.g. by the park's marker or gate kind) and an arm shows a gated run that then crashes max_crashes times is parked.

title: until's wake has the read-at-exit race: a delivery that lands between until's read and the workflow's exit sits at or below run.waiting's recorded seq and never wakes the run
description: Found reviewing fleet-thh (2026-09-23). run.waiting's seq is read when the workflow exits (core/src/item/run.rs read_the_exit). Wake::Items matches only item lines above that position (controller/src/runs.rs could_wake), so a line for a named item that lands after until read the stream and before exit is never matched. Matching anywhere is not safe for items because the wake does not carry which state until wants (an earlier item.dispatched would match every poll). Fix direction: carry the wanted state in the wake (the SDK throws {items, state}), then match anywhere for that state. Done when an arm with the delivery inside the gap is red, then green, and an earlier state of the same item does not re-run the workflow every poll.

Measured on bd 1.2.2: bd resolves a partial id by SUBSTRING, not prefix. 'bd show 6gr --json' answers fleet-6gr. 'bd show 0 --json' answers the JSON {"error": "no issues found matching the provided IDs"}, with the ambiguity only on stderr ('ambiguous ID "0" matches 14 issues: [fleet-0zs … fleet-nv0 fleet-x0cad …] / Use more characters to disambiguate'). 'bd show zzzz --json' answers the same JSON error, and stderr reads 'no issue found matching "zzzz"'.

Remedy:
- Every verb that takes an item argument resolves it ONCE at its entry, through Store::show, and from then on uses the id the answer carries (Item.id), never the typed argument: every write, note, event, brief path, ring text and refusal. The verbs are dispatch, brief, deliver --item, ask --item, answer, review, land, and any other taking an item.
- dispatch compares that full id against the ready ids (core/src/item/dispatch.rs:182, as rewritten by fleet-16s).
- An ambiguous argument is exit 1, naming the matches bd listed, read from the answer's stderr (it is bd's only carrier of the ambiguity on 1.2.2). A missing one stays exit 1 as today.
- If fleet-9r6 lands first and bd's error carries a code that tells ambiguous from not-found, use the code.

- AC2 dispatch <ambiguous substring> exits 1 and names at least two matches (one arm through the real bd, since the stderr shape is bd's).
- AC3 dispatch <no match> exits 1.
- AC4 brief, deliver --item and ask --item with a suffix write only full ids (one arm each).

title: Autopilot as a routine: a machine setting read and written through fleet settings (fleet-layers Q12, ruled A), and a routine on a schedule whose guard reads it and opens the oldest plan while the open runs are under the cap — the switch's new home after plan, fly and autopilot left core
description:
## Why

fleet-layers Q12 (ruled 2026-09-17, A): autopilot's home is a machine setting, read and written through the API, by fleet settings or the cockpit's screen — machine state, not policy, not process environment. tinytown-tnkuq.94 removed fleet autopilot and the switch file from core with plan and fly; unattended composition is tiny's takeoff workflow over fleet run (tinytown-tnkuq.110, flown). The board's line "filed when .110 has flown" is this bead. fleet-layers § What tiny ships on day one places autopilot as a routine AFTER day one, so this is not on the switch's road; it is filed so the requirement is not discoverable only by tripping over it.

## What (frame)

A settings verb (fleet settings get|set <key>) over a file in the machine directory; the key autopilot with values on and off; a routine in tiny (packs/tiny/orders or routines) on a schedule whose guard reads the setting through the API and, when on, opens the oldest plan while the open runs are under the cap ([core.run] or the routine's own cap) — never while a run is open above it; off, nothing opens. Alberto's standing order stands over it: the switch is OFF while he is asleep or absent.

## Acceptance Criteria (frame — finalized by the spec pass)

fleet settings set autopilot on|off round-trips; the routine's guard reads it; with on and no open run the oldest plan opens once; with off nothing opens; the cap holds.

## Risk

After the MVP and after the switch; owes a spec pass.
